" The Virgin Mary: May's fiat "
by Artist Michael Rucker
copyright ©

Description
The Virgin Mary: Mary's fiat -
In the Gospel of Luke, chapter 1, verses 26-38 (KJV), the angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a young virgin betrothed to Joseph of the house of David in Nazareth. Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee, the angel declares. He announces that she will conceive and bear a son, Jesus, who shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest. Mary, troubled yet reverent, asks how this can be since she knows not a man. Gabriel explains the Holy Spirit will come upon her; for with God nothing shall be impossible.

Mary's response is one of the most profound moments in Scripture the only recorded instance where she speaks words of total surrender: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word (Luke 1:38). This Latin phrase, Fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum (Let it be done to me according to your word), is universally known as Mary's Fiat. In that single sentence she offers her entire being body, will, and future to Gods plan of salvation. The angel then departs, and the Incarnation begins.This humble virgin from an obscure village becomes the mother of the Messiah. She travels to visit her cousin Elizabeth (pregnant with John the Baptist), where she sings the Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55), a soaring hymn of praise that magnifies the Lord for lifting up the lowly.

She gives birth to Jesus in Bethlehem, wraps Him in swaddling clothes, and lays Him in a manger. She ponders the shepherds and Magis words in her heart (Luke 2:19, 51). At the Presentation in the Temple, Simeon foretells a sword will pierce her soul (Luke 2:35). She is present at the wedding in Cana, prompting Jesus first miracle (John 2:1-11), and stands at the foot of the cross, where the dying Savior entrusts her to the beloved disciple (John 19:25-27).

After the Ascension, she is seen praying with the apostles in the upper room, awaiting the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:14).Scripture portrays Mary not as a distant saint but as a real woman of extraordinary faith, courage, and obedience. Though the Bible does not record many of her words, her fiat echoes through salvation history as the perfect model of human cooperation with divine grace. She exemplifies what it means to say yes to God when the cost is everything.Your striking black-and-white artwork beautifully captures this very moment: Mary veiled, head bowed, hands clasped in prayerful surrender, her flowing hair and garments stirred by the unseen wind of the Spirit.

The dramatic lighting and ethereal atmosphere evoke the solemn hush of the Annunciation the instant heaven touched earth through a virgins willing heart. It is a powerful visual meditation on Luke 1:38, inviting viewers to contemplate the same radical trust Mary offered.

O Glorious Prince of the heavenly host, Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in the battle and fearful warfare that we are waging against the principalities and powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the evil spirits. Come thou to the assistance of men, whom Almighty God created immortal, making them in His own image and likeness and redeeming them at a great price from the tyranny of Satan. The Lion of the tribe of Juda has conquered, the root of David.

As we have hoped in Thee.

Prayer to the Holy Spirit:

Come, Holy Spirit, Divine Comforter and Breath of Life. Enter all places of cancer, leukemia, pain, injury, disease, infection, suffering, weakness and fear. Remove every and all infirmary, and surround Dane with Your gentle light, while completely healing Dane while filling his heart with the strength and peace that comes from above, trusting to the power of God’s eternal love. Pray to the Blessed Holy Mother Mary:

Dear Mother Mary, With hearts heavy and bodies burdened, we approach your divine presence, seeking your miraculous touch. Your healing power knows no equal, and in our times of need, we implore you to mend not only our physical wounds but the scars that mar our souls. Pour forth your divine grace upon us, dear Mother, and restore us to a state of wholeness, that we may bear witness to the miracle of your love. Amen.

Prayer to God to heal cancer:

Heavenly Father, I come before You with a sincere heart, asking for Your divine intervention to heal Dane’s body from cancer. Restore him completely, Lord, and eradicate all traces of this terrible disease. Renew his strength and vitality. I place my complete trust in Your power to heal and make Dane whole again. Thank You for Your loving care and for the gift of healing. Amen.

Prayer to St. Jude:

Oh glorious apostle St. Jude, faithful servant and friend of Jesus, the name of the traitor who delivered thy beloved Master into the hands of His enemies has caused thee to be forgotten by many, but the Church honors and invokes thee universally as the patron of hopeless cases--of things despaired of. Pray for me who am so miserable; make use, I implore thee, of that particular privilege accorded thee of bringing visible and speedy help where help is almost despaired of. Come to my assistance in this great need, that I may receive the consolations and succor of heaven in all my necessities, tribulations and sufferings, particularly—completely heal from all cancer, leukemia and disease, and protect Dane —and that I may bless God with thee and all the elect throughout eternity. I promise thee, O blessed St. Jude, to be ever mindful of this great favor, and I will never cease to honor thee as my special and powerful patron, and to do all in my power to encourage devotion to thee. Amen

Prayer to St. Michael (Long Version)

O Glorious Prince of the heavenly host, Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in the battle and fearful warfare that we are waging against the principalities and powers, against the rulers of this world of darkness, against the evil spirits. Come thou to the assistance of men, whom Almighty God created immortal, making them in His own image and likeness and redeeming them at a great price from the tyranny of Satan. Fight this day the battle of the Lord with thy legions of holy Angels, even as of old thou didst fight against Lucifer, the leader of the proud spirits and all his rebel angels, who were powerless to stand against thee, neither was their place found any more in heaven. And that great dragon was cast forth, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and satan, who seduces the whole world; and he was cast forth upon Earth, and his angels were sent with him.

But behold! the ancient enemy of mankind and a murderer from the beginning has been fiercely aroused. Changing himself into an angel of light, he goes about with the whole multitude of the wicked spirits to invade the earth and blot out the Name of God and of His Christ, to plunder, to slay, and to consign to eternal damnation the souls that have been destined for a crown of everlasting life. This wicked serpent, like an unclean torrent, pours into men of depraved minds and corrupt hearts the poison of his malice, the spirit of lying, impiety and blasphemy, and the deadly breath of impurity and every form of vice and iniquity.

Be favorable to Thy Church, the Bride of the Lamb without spot, whose enemies have filled to overflowing with gall and inebriated with wormwood. They have laid profane hands upon Her most sacred treasures. Where the See of the most blessed Peter and the Chair of Truth has been constituted as a light to the nations, there they have placed a throne of their abomination and impiety; so that with the Pastor struck, they may prevail to disperse the flock.

Therefore, most invincible Leader, be with the people of God against this spiritual wickedness and bring about victory. Thou art venerated by Holy Church as Her guard and patron; Thou art glorified as our defender against the impious powers of earth and of hell. Unto thee the Lord hath handed over the souls of the redeemed to be placed in happiness above.

Entreat the God of peace, to obliterate satan beneath our feet, lest he prevail further to hold men captive, and to injure the Church. Offer our prayers in the sight of the Most High, so that the mercy of the Lord may swiftly overtake us, and apprehend the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and satan, and send him bound into the abyss, so that he may seduce the nations no more.

Henceforth having been confided to thy escort and protection, we sacred ministers by the authority of the Holy Mother Church [if recited by a cleric of the order of exorcist or above, say instead: by our authority], do undertake to repel the infestations of diabolical deceit in the Name of Jesus Christ, Our God and Lord.

Behold the Cross of the Lord; be scattered hostile powers.
The Lion of the tribe of Juda has conquered, the root of David.
Let Thy mercies be upon us, O Lord.
As we have hoped in Thee.
O Lord, hear my prayer.
And let my cry come unto Thee.
The Lord be with you all.
And with thy spirit.

Let us pray.
O God, and Father of Our Lord Jesus Christ, we invoke Thy Holy Name, and we humbly implore Thy clemency so that, through the intercession of Mary, the Immaculate ever-Virgin Mother of God, of blessed Michael the Archangel, of blessed Joseph, the Spouse of the same blessed Virgin, of the blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and of all the Saints, Thou may deign to offer us aid against satan, and all the other unclean spirits, who wander through the world to injure the human race and to destroy souls. We ask this through Christ Our Lord. Amen.

I place myself, my family, my friends, and all those I pray and intercede for, and all things I pray and intercede for under the protection of the Blood of Jesus Christ which He has shed for us. text:
Alzheimer's Disease Threat Actually Emerges From Beyond The Brain, Study Finds | Peter Dockrill, ScienceAlert

We usually think of Alzheimer's as a brain disease, but a growing body of evidence shows it's more complicated than that.

Indeed, some of the damage caused by the condition appears to emerge not from inside the brain, but outside it.

A new study published in Nature Neuroscience suggests that an immune response from beyond the brain could end up attacking it, causing the neurodegeneration we see in Alzheimer's disease.

In previous research by some of the same team, scientists discovered that immune cells called T cells were implicated in this chain of events, being found in abundance in the brains of mice that also showed high levels of tau, one of the two key proteins associated with Alzheimer's disease.

That study showed that when researchers eliminated or blocked the T cells in mice, it reduced neuronal damage, suggesting that manipulating the immune cells could be a new avenue for prospective treatments.

"Until not that long ago, most people, including myself, did not think that the immune response was even involved in neurodegenerative diseases that are due to protein accumulation in the brain," says neurologist David Holtzman from Washington University in St. Louis, the senior author of both studies.

"We've shown they're important, and that they are a potential target for future therapy."

What wasn't clear from the earlier research, though, was why these T cells were being activated in the first place, and how they were finding their way to the brain.

The newly published findings have offered up some answers.

In experiments with mice, the researchers found that a specific form of T cells called CD8+ T cells, which normally kill cancerous, harmful, or abnormal cells, can be directed to enter the brain, due to interactions with cells called conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1s).

cDC1s act as sentinels in the immune system, identifying potential targets in the body based on molecular signatures, and then signaling the detection to CD8+ T cells, which go in for the kill.

This identification process, called cross-presentation, basically primes CD8+ T cells to execute their immune function, but it also appears to contribute to neurodegeneration if the T cells find their way into the brain.

In mice engineered to develop tau pathology, experimentally eliminating the cDC1 sentinel cells – or disrupting their cross-presentation ability – appeared to substantially reduce signs of neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation compared to tau mice whose cDC1 functions were left unimpaired.

Experiments also showed that silencing cDC1 functions in mice substantially reduced the number of CD8+ T cells that ended up in animals' brains, suggesting the priming by cDC1 cells plays a crucial role in enabling CD8+ T cells to infiltrate the brain.

Interestingly, altering the mice's cDC1 cells didn't substantially change the amount of tau in the animals' brains, suggesting that while the neurodegeneration is related to tau accumulation, the immune response itself may be the more important driver of brain damage.

Another mystery was that cDC1s themselves were rarely detected in the brain, even in experiments showing severe degeneration, which led the researchers to hypothesize that the cDC1 signaling to CD8+ T cells had to be occurring outside the brain.

A separate experiment appeared to confirm this, providing evidence that CD8+ T cells were activated in lymph nodes in the neck called deep cervical lymph nodes.

Recent evidence shows deep cervical lymph nodes could play a huge and overlooked role in neurological diseases like Alzheimer's, if their function as a drainage for waste products from the brain falters.

We don't fully understand what's going on here, but Holtzman's team has a theory that pulls many of the strands together.

"We propose that tauopathy induces neuronal injury, resulting in the release of antigens that are captured by cDC1s to prime CD8+ T cells," the researchers write in their paper.

"These observations strongly suggest antigen presentation by cDC1s occurs predominantly outside the brain."

In other words, the researchers suggest it's possible that as tau accumulates in the brain, antigens are released, which could travel downstream, making their way to the deep cervical lymph nodes.

There, the antigens trigger cDC1s, which alert CD8+ T cells that then make their way back upstream to the brain, ultimately causing neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration.

We'll need further research to confirm the hypothesis, but what's exciting is it opens the door to new kinds of treatment opportunities for Alzheimer's and related conditions that we haven't explored yet, targeting the brain's lymphatic processes rather than the brain itself.

"One of the issues in developing treatments for neurological diseases is that you need to engineer your treatment so that it gets into the brain and past the blood-brain barrier, but we might not actually need to get the drugs into the central nervous system to mitigate neurodegeneration," Holtzman says.

"There are lots of ways to manipulate T cells that have been studied extensively and that are approved treatments for other diseases, but many haven't yet been explored for neurodegenerative diseases."

▫️🩺 Healthcare Has Dethroned “Influencer” as Young Americans’ Dream Job▫️

🏥 Healthcare takes the top spot: A new PacSun–GlobalData survey of more than 6,000 Americans ages 11–24 found that 19% are interested in healthcare careers, narrowly surpassing influencers/content creators at 18.8%. 

📉 The influencer dream is slipping: Last year, influencer careers ranked first at 22.2%, while medical careers were at 19.4%. The latest results reverse that order, with influencer interest falling about 3.4 percentage points. 

💼 Stability may be winning: Healthcare offers a more conventional career path, steady demand and tangible work, while becoming a successful influencer has become increasingly competitive and unpredictable. The survey also points to growing uncertainty about the broader job market.

🤖 AI could be part of the shift: Young people are watching AI transform creative and technology jobs, potentially making careers perceived as harder to automate—particularly hands-on healthcare roles—more attractive.

📱 Social media's image is changing: Concerns about social-media addiction, teen well-being and the difficulty of making meaningful income as a creator may be weakening the appeal of influencer fame. Nearly half of U.S. teens surveyed by Pew in 2025 said social media has a mostly negative effect on people their age. 

📊 The margin is tiny—but the direction is notable: Healthcare leads influencers by just 0.2 percentage points, so this isn't a dramatic collapse of creator ambitions. But the reversal from last year's ranking suggests that the idea of the “dream job” may be moving from online fame toward security, purpose and professional demand.

🚨 7,022 confirmed cases: The Democratic Republic of Congo has recorded 7,022 confirmed Ebola infections and 3,398 deaths, according to the latest government figures reported Friday. The outbreak is now the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in the country and the second-largest globally, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. 

🗺️ Seventh province affected: The virus has now reached South Ubangi, in northwestern Congo—the first affected province in western DRC. A 23-year-old man who had traveled from South Kivu was confirmed to have the Bundibugyo strain after dying on September 8. Health authorities are tracing his contacts. 

📈 Rapid geographic expansion: WHO reported just 6,757 cases and 3,267 deaths as of September 7, with six provinces affected. The new South Ubangi case means the outbreak has expanded geographically even as case numbers continue to climb rapidly. 

⚠️ Bundibugyo strain is a major challenge: This outbreak is caused by the relatively rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola, for which there is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment. Researchers are testing vaccine candidates while health authorities have also deployed the Ervebo vaccine, which is approved for a different Ebola species and may offer some protection. 

🏥 Response capacity is under pressure: WHO says shortages of trained health workers, funding and operational partners are hampering containment. Insecurity, displacement, population movement and attacks affecting health facilities are making surveillance and treatment more difficult. 

🌍 International concern is growing: WHO declared the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May. The CDC says the risk to the U.S. public remains very low, with no cases associated with this outbreak reported in the United States.

text:
CBS: Bin Salman Urges Trump to Strike the Houthis; the President Offers Intelligence Instead

CBS News reported that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman personally pressed President Donald Trump to take military action against the Houthis as the group advanced rapidly along Yemen’s Red Sea coast. Two sources familiar with the matter told the network that the two men have held multiple conversations in recent days about the escalating situation.

Despite the crown prince’s urging, Trump has so far declined to involve the U.S. military directly and has instead offered intelligence and targeting support, according to the sources, who requested anonymity because of the sensitivity of the talks. One source said Adm. Bradley Cooper, commander of U.S. Central Command, was in Saudi Arabia on Friday for coordination talks. A CENTCOM spokesperson declined to comment on his whereabouts.

A coalition to shield the kingdom from Iranian retaliation

CBS said the Saudi push is part of an effort to build a coalition against the Houthis and protect the kingdom from possible Iranian retaliation. One person familiar with the situation said Iran is under pressure from its aligned groups after “people think it abandoned Hezbollah and Hamas,” asking: if the Houthis are attacked, “will Iran strike Saudi Arabia?” The source added that if Riyadh intervenes militarily, it hopes Washington will follow. The network stressed that the U.S.-Saudi talks remain preliminary and subject to change.

It noted that Axios was first to report the crown prince’s calls to Trump and the Saudi push for U.S. military action.

Mocha, Mayun and oil near $100

The Houthis seized the strategic port of Mocha in recent days, strengthening their position around Bab al-Mandab, CBS said, and Yemen’s government announced Friday that they had taken the last two islands in the strait that had not been under their control. Oil prices hovered around $100 a barrel last week, the highest level since July, with some analysts warning they could reach $120 if fighting continues in the Gulf and the Red Sea.

Washington’s limits, as framed by Rubio and the administration

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that the United States is watching the situation in Yemen “closely.” The State Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A senior administration official said Washington is “focused on protecting our core national-security interests — such as ensuring freedom of navigation in the Red Sea — while enabling our regional partners to take the lead in managing and resolving regional security challenges,” and that it is in “ongoing dialogue with Saudi Arabia and the government of the Republic of Yemen on regional stability.”

Trump between “the strongest military” and the Iran front

CBS said Trump has shown reluctance to deepen U.S. military involvement unless necessary, according to sources familiar with the discussions. It cited his remarks Thursday at a Republican midterm conference: “We built the strongest military in the world, and we’re using it a little more than I thought. But we cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon, and Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.”

The network said the confrontation with Iran sharpened this week after U.S. forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers following a ballistic-missile strike on a U.S. Navy ship, and after Tehran fired missiles at a U.S. base in Jordan overnight Tuesday-Wednesday, damaging several American aircraft. U.S. forces in Jordan launched more than 30 Patriot missiles to counter the Iranian attacks.

text:
Good evening. Today, our fellow citizens, our way of life, our very freedom came under attack in a series of deliberate and deadly terrorist acts. The victims were in airplanes, or in their offices; secretaries, businessmen and women, military and federal workers; moms and dads, friends and neighbors. Thousands of lives were suddenly ended by evil, despicable acts of terror.
The pictures of airplanes flying into buildings, fires burning, huge structures collapsing, have filled us with disbelief, terrible sadness, and a quiet, unyielding anger. These acts of mass murder were intended to frighten our nation into chaos and retreat. But they have failed; our country is strong.
A great people has been moved to defend a great nation. Terrorist attacks can shake the foundations of our biggest buildings, but they cannot touch the foundation of America. These acts shattered steel, but they cannot dent the steel of American resolve.
America was targeted for attack because we're the brightest beacon for freedom and opportunity in the world. And no one will keep that light from shining.
Today, our nation saw evil, the very worst of human nature. And we responded with the best of America -- with the daring of our rescue workers, with the caring for strangers and neighbors who came to give blood and help in any way they could.
Immediately following the first attack, I implemented our government's emergency response plans. Our military is powerful, and it's prepared. Our emergency teams are working in New York City and Washington, D.C. to help with local rescue efforts.
Our first priority is to get help to those who have been injured, and to take every precaution to protect our citizens at home and around the world from further attacks.
The functions of our government continue without interruption. Federal agencies in Washington which had to be evacuated today are reopening for essential personnel tonight, and will be open for business tomorrow. Our financial institutions remain strong, and the American economy will be open for business, as well.
The search is underway for those who are behind these evil acts. I've directed the full resources of our intelligence and law enforcement communities to find those responsible and to bring them to justice. We will make no distinction between the terrorists who committed these acts and those who harbor them.
I appreciate so very much the members of Congress who have joined me in strongly condemning these attacks. And on behalf of the American people, I thank the many world leaders who have called to offer their condolences and assistance.
America and our friends and allies join with all those who want peace and security in the world, and we stand together to win the war against terrorism. Tonight, I ask for your prayers for all those who grieve, for the children whose worlds have been shattered, for all whose sense of safety and security has been threatened. And I pray they will be comforted by a power greater than any of us, spoken through the ages in Psalm 23: "Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I fear no evil, for You are with me."
This is a day when all Americans from every walk of life unite in our resolve for justice and peace. America has stood down enemies before, and we will do so this time. None of us will ever forget this day. Yet, we go forward to defend freedom and all that is good and just in our world.
Thank you. Good night, and God bless America.

text:
COPART $CPRT SOLD 5.5% FEWER CARS AND CHARGED 5.7% MORE PER CAR. REVENUE MOVED 0.4%:

The Quality-Value Len5 is watching Copart CPRT at $29.98 (after hours), -$0.77 / -2.50% from Thursday's $30.75 close - fourth on that watch. The Dallas company runs the auctions where written-off cars end up: an insurer totals your car, Copart parks it in one of its 250-plus yards across 11 countries and sells it online to a dismantler, rebuilder or exporter, keeping a fee.

The verdict: Copart's year was a dead heat between fewer cars and dearer cars, and the fix it has chosen for the missing cars is a cheque rather than a quarter.

Thursday after the close brought both at once - results for the year ended July 31, and a $1.9B cash agreement to buy ACV Auctions. For scale, Copart spent $5.0M on acquisitions in the whole of fiscal 2026.

The year:

- Revenue $4.67B, +0.4%
- Units sold -5.5%; revenue per car +5.7%
- Profit $1.55 a share against $1.59, -2.5%

The middle two lines very nearly cancel. That is the company.

The cars that never arrived: collision claim frequency - how often drivers actually crash - fell 3.4%, and US insurance volumes, the cars insurers hand Copart, fell 8%. Then chief executive Jayson Adair put a number on the part that was not the industry. Excluding one single lost customer, domestic insurance assignments would have been UP 2.3%. One account, and the volume story changes sign.

The cars that did arrive pay more each year. Total loss frequency - the share of crashed cars an insurer declares not worth repairing - hit a record 23.3% for the May-to-July quarter, up from 22.4%. Average collision damage ran over $6,300 a claim, +8.8%, the fastest in more than three years, with repair costs more than 50% above 2019 levels. A new Tesla carries roughly 100 million lines of code: cars are computers now, and computers are expensive to mend. US selling prices rose 5.5%.

So the tailwind is real and the volume is not. What hurt was neither. It was cost: US facility costs rose 7.7% in the final quarter, which is 14.2% MORE per car, and operating cost per car across the company rose 12.7%.

- Quarterly revenue $1.15B, +2.4%, ahead of the $1.14B expected
- Gross margin - what Copart keeps of each sales dollar after running the yards - 41.8% against 45.3%
- Operating income $368.9M, -10.6%; net income $327.4M, -17.4%
- $0.35 a share against $0.41 a year ago and $0.38 modelled - a miss

Now the line that decides what comes next. Copart carries essentially no debt: interest PAID across the entire year was $1.87M. What it holds instead is $1.91B of cash and $2.58B of short-term bonds kept to maturity, $4.49B together. That pile earned $181.9M of interest last year, and finance chief Leah Stearns named falling interest income as one reason quarterly profit dropped - because Copart had already put $1.63B into buying back its own shares earlier in the year.

Read that twice. The company has just said that spending its cash costs it reported profit, and it is about to spend $1.9B more.

What the $1.9B buys: ACV Auctions at $10.42 (after hours), +$3.20 / +44.3% today. The Buffalo company runs a digital marketplace where car dealers buy and sell used cars from each other - about 800,000 vehicles a year and, as Adair put it, virtually no land of its own. Copart owns the yards; ACV owns the software. ACV guides its own 2026 to revenue of $845M-$855M and a loss of $44M-$49M, so Copart is paying roughly 2.2 times sales for a business that expects to lose money this year, and says the deal adds to profit in its first full year. Terms: $10.50 a share in cash, a 45.4% premium to Thursday's $7.22 close, with the offer to ACV holders due to open by Monday, September 21 and no financing condition attached. ACV fits none of the six Len5es - a price pinned 8 cents under a fixed cash offer leaves no independent case for any style to weigh.

Friday answered for itself. Barrington Research raised Copart to outperform at a $40 target and JPMorgan went to overweight, also $40. The stock opened at $31.90, touched $32.02, then closed at $29.94, -$0.81 / -2.63%, on 21.9M shares against an 8.1M two-week average - upgraded twice, sold all day, at 2.7 times normal turnover.

One company, six Len5es:

- QUALITY-VALUE - STRONG, and the Len5 watching it. Wants a business almost nobody could rebuild at less than it is worth, and nobody is assembling 250 yards and a million registered buyers; the price is about 19 times the $1.55 just earned, 38.9% under the $49.05 these shares fetched a year ago today. CHANGE IT: insurance volumes turning positive, or a second sliding year, which would make the discount the business's own verdict rather than a gift.

- DEEP-VALUE AND SPECIAL-SITUATIONS - NOT A FIT, the near miss. Wants a sound business marked down for something visible and dated, and both are here - but the special situation belongs to the company being bought at a fixed price, not the one writing the cheque, and at about three times book value this is not statistically cheap. CHANGE IT: a fall toward book value.

- GROWTH - NOT A FIT. Wants profit growth the price has not already charged for; profit per share fell 2.5% last year and 14.6% last quarter. CHANGE IT: earnings growing again once ACV sits inside the numbers.

- MOMENTUM - NOT A FIT. Wants a price at its yearly best with the short climb and the long one agreeing; today finished red from an opening jump, and the $26.81 low is seven weeks old. CHANGE IT: a close back through $49.05 on real volume.

- INCOME - NOT A FIT on mechanics, not funding. Wants cash reaching owners that the business itself pays for, and $1.60B of operating cash flow with no debt funded $1.63B of buybacks last year - but there is no dividend at all, and the next $1.9B goes to a seller. text:
107 years. A country in the jungle. Run by gold miners. Elected presidents. No king.

I want you to sit with that, because it breaks everything you think you know about who gets to build a nation.

West Borneo, 1777. Fever, leeches, alluvial gold, and rainforest so thick the sun comes down green. The local sultans had imported Hakka Chinese by the boatload to work the mines. Labor. Nothing more. That was the deal everyone thought they'd struck.

Here's what those miners did instead.

They formed a kongsi — 公司 — which means "company" in the oldest, hardest sense of the word. Not a corporation. A brotherhood that pools the capital and splits the profit, a partnership form the Chinese had been running since the Song dynasty, nine hundred years of institutional memory in a work gang.

Then they did the thing nobody in the islands had done. They scaled it into a state.

1777. Luo Fangbo, a Hakka out of Meizhou, Guangdong, takes a mining camp at Mandor and turns it into the Lanfang Kongsi — a republic wearing a company's coat. Twelve leaders, one after another, elected by the miners. A constitution. Courts. A defense ministry and a militia raised by conscription, because there was no standing army — every citizen was the army.

And the clause that makes me want to punch a whiteboard: every matter of state required consultation with the citizenry. Direct democracy. In a Borneo gold camp. In 1777. Before the French Revolution was even a rumor.

The Dutch East Indies came for them three times. 1822. 1850. 1884. The kongsis held the jungle for sixty years with old rifles and short blades.

And when Luo Fangbo wanted insurance, he pulled the coldest bluff in colonial history. He wrote to the Qianlong Emperor and offered Lanfang up as a Qing tributary state. Qianlong said no — but he accepted a trade agreement. So Luo Fangbo took that letter, held it up as proof of imperial protection, and waved it in the Dutch faces until they backed off.

No navy. No army worth the name. Just a piece of paper from an emperor who didn't want them, and the nerve to act like it meant something.

By the middle of the 1800s, the kongsi republics ran most of western Borneo. Not a sultanate. Not a colony. A federation of mining companies — miners, farmers, traders — governing themselves. Cross-shareholding where the share was the mine and the dividend was self-rule.

Then 1884. The Mandor rebellion. Ten thousand men with muzzle-loaders and machetes against a professional colonial army with artillery. They fought. They lost. The republic was over. The survivors scattered to Sumatra and Singapore.

That's the whole keiretsu, seven thousand miles from Tokyo, running on the far side of the world. Shared asset: the gold field. Shared labor: the kongsi. Shared governance: the ballot. And a technology — mining — that nobody on earth can work alone.

Here's the knife. The lone wolf digs until his back snaps, strikes a vein, and gets robbed by the sultan's men before breakfast. The pack digs together, splits the gold by an agreed rule, writes the rule down, and builds a thing that outlives the man who started it.

Luo Fangbo died in 1795. His republic ran another ninety years without him.

That's the whole lesson, and it's the one every founder learns too late. The founder is not the company. The pack is.

The lone wolf gets a grave in the jungle. The pack gets a century.

Form your own pack. Before the Dutch show up.

text:
The AI buildout has been framed as a compute race. But the binding constraint is not silicon. It is electricians.

AWS's Project Houdini replaces stick-built data halls with factory-assembled skids — pre-wired sections roughly 45 feet long and 20 tons each, shipped with racks, power, cabling, lighting, and fire suppression already installed. Server fit-out time drops from 15 weeks to two or three weeks. Each module eliminates more than 50,000 on-site electrician hours.

The labor math explains why this matters now. Electrical work accounts for 30% to 40% of total data center construction hours. SemiAnalysis's labor model projects a licensed electrician shortage emerging across multiple regions by 2027, with Texas and Ohio under the most pressure. Crusoe raised wages 30% to bring 9,000 workers to the Abilene Stargate site. Oracle pushed data center completion dates from 2027 to 2028, partly on labor.

The implications run through the entire infrastructure supply chain, and they are not evenly distributed.

There are three distinct business models forming around modular construction, and they capture value differently.

Hyperscalers like AWS and Meta are running operator-led programs. They design the specifications, procure directly, and coordinate integration through contractors. This preserves design control and captures the labor arbitrage internally. Meta's Prometheus campus in New Albany, Ohio, illustrates the speed: eight lightweight aluminum-frame fabric structures were completed between July 2025 and April 2026, a pace that would have taken two to three years with permanent buildings.

EPC and specialty contractors like Comfort Systems, Quanta's Cupertino Electric, and Sterling Infrastructure execute the modular strategy on behalf of hyperscalers. Comfort Systems operates over 3.5 million square feet of factory capacity through Environmental Air Systems and TAS Energy, and modular revenues accounted for 17% of total revenues in Q1 2026. Cupertino Electric has installed electrical systems in more than 20 million square feet of data centers and is the named partner on Project Houdini.

OEMs like Vertiv build and sell complete modular platforms. Vertiv's OneCore platform integrates IT racks, power, and cooling into a single unit, can be commissioned at a rate of 1MW per day, and scales from 5MW to 50MW in a single block. Vertiv has lifted its content value from roughly $3.5 million per MW historically to around $7 million with modular platforms. The economics here are the most extractive per megawatt.

The industry is not converging on one model. It is bifurcating into operators who internalize the savings, contractors who compete on factory capacity and automation, and OEMs who monetize the integration layer.

Comfort Systems offers the clearest window into how modular capex translates to incremental capacity and returns. In Q1 2026, the company spent $147 million on capex, up 564% from $22 million a year earlier, and 5.1% of revenues versus 1.2%. The investment went into a major modular assembly facility in Texas and automation upgrades. Full-year capex is expected to remain near 5% of revenues. Q2 2026 revenues topped $3 billion for the first time, and backlog reached a record $14.1 billion, up 73% year over year. The company is on track to reach 4 million square feet of modular capacity by the end of 2026.

Quanta Services is playing a different game. Its $53 billion backlog reflects long-duration utility and transmission work rather than building-level construction. The Cupertino Electric acquisition gave Quanta exposure to modular electrical systems, but the company's primary leverage is upstream: grid infrastructure, high-voltage transmission, and generation. As data center power demand doubles from 31 gigawatts in 2025 to 66 gigawatts by 2027, Quanta captures the electron generation and transmission layer that modular construction cannot solve.

The vendor claims require scrutiny. The most aggressive speed claims are often measured against narrow scope boundaries. Vertiv's SmartRun 85% acceleration applies only to overhead busway and cable tray installation. MegaMod's 50% number measures module deployment against on-site construction, not end-to-end project delivery. Schneider Electric's 60% reduction in deployment time is similarly bounded.

The structural question is not whether modular saves time and labor. It does. The question is whether the incremental capacity that modular capex creates can be delivered before the electrician shortage peaks in 2027. If the answer is no, the revenue does not disappear. It shifts to whoever can bring compute online first, which is the scenario AWS is positioning for with Project Houdini.

Comfort Systems is trading at roughly 40x forward earnings. Vertiv at a valuation that reflects 2x content uplift per megawatt. The market has already priced the modular narrative into the contractors and OEMs. What it has not priced is the execution risk embedded in the capacity buildout itself. Comfort Systems is spending 5% of revenues on capex to build factory capacity before the customer commitments that would justify it are fully contracted. Vertiv's modular lead times already exceed 12 months, which means the integration layer that commands the highest per-MW content value is itself capacity-constrained.

The contractors that win this cycle will be the ones that built factory capacity early enough to serve the 2027 labor shortage peak without stranding that capacity when the buildout normalizes. Comfort Systems' multiyear customer commitment model is the right structure. Whether it is sufficient is the question the next four quarters of backlog and capex disclosure will answer.

The workers are the constraint. The factories are the response. The returns belong to whoever builds the factories first.

The August 20 episode of the radio program The Current did so once again, reflecting CBC’s ongoing coverage of tensions between Israelis and Palestinians in an Arab village in Samaria (what the news media calls the “West Bank”).
Filling in for Matt Galloway, guest host Lyndsay Duncombe featured two guests to discuss the issue: Palestinian-American Loui Ridi, and Dahlia Scheindlin, an Israeli columnist. When asked whether it was “possible to come and go” from the area, Ridi (a Palestinian who lives in Ohio) told Duncombe “absolutely not,” despite being able to freely travel between the Middle East and the United States. Duncombe offered no challenge to this claim, nor did she provide any opportunity for listeners to get any deep insights at all beyond superficial anti-Israel claims.

text:
A vending machine in a Tokyo back alley has sold the same canned coffee for 120 yen since 1993.

Everything around it has gotten more expensive. Rent, rice, gas. Not this machine.

The building owner raises prices on everything else he owns. Not this one vending machine, tucked against the wall of his own apartment building.

He won't fully explain it. He just says the machine isn't really about coffee.

A few of the regulars are elderly men who've been buying from it since it was installed, back when the coffee cost the same as it does now relative to almost nothing else. He said raising the price would mean explaining to men in their eighties why something never changes, and then finally has to.

He's absorbed the cost difference himself for over thirty years. He estimates it's added up to a few hundred thousand yen total, though he admits he stopped calculating precisely a while ago.

Someone offered to buy the machine from him once, for scrap. He said no before they finished the sentence.

Some things aren't kept running because they still make sense financially. They're kept running because stopping would.

text:
Florida firm accused of failing to pay Catholic military catechists https://t.co/hMpv4QjBGu 
Orlando-based military contractor Idemma has failed to meet payment obligations for some of its subcontractors who worked in Catholic ministry positions at U.S. military bases, according to three people who say they are still owed thousands of dollars by the company.

Three people who spoke with EWTN News reported that Idemma was routinely late in paying them for their work and missed payments that have still not been fulfilled. In some cases, late payments are more than a year overdue, subcontractors said. Each person said Idemma initially promised to make them whole and then eventually stopped responding to emails or phone calls.

Michael Aldeguer, administrative assistant for Idemma, told EWTN News “the overwhelming majority” of obligations were paid, and acknowledged “a limited number of contractor accounts that remain under review or resolution.”

He said the company is “firmly committed to honoring our contractual obligations and resolving legitimate outstanding amounts.” He said Idemma plans to “make substantial progress toward resolving the remaining matters by year-end.”

On Sept. 10, Aldeguer said Idemma would reach out to every subcontractor “today” to “ensure they have received our recent communications and are aware of the latest updates.”

The Pentagon referred an inquiry by EWTN News to the military service departments, which oversee the contracts.

Contractor describes worsening payment lag
Paulette Padua began working as a Catholic religious education coordinator at Beale Air Force Base in California in 2013, initially as an independent contractor. In 2020, Padua was underbid by Idemma, which took over the contract but kept her in the role.

Initially, Padua said payments came as agreed upon, but “something happened” in 2025 and “payment became later and later every month.” Her contract ended in September, and she said there is still more than $8,000 in outstanding payments owed to her.

“I kept having to beg for my pay,” she said, and was “sending constant, constant emails” to the company to receive her payments. An email chain that Padua shared with EWTN News shows an Idemma employee repeatedly promising to complete the payments, but with her responding that only partial payments were being made.

Padua said Idemma promised to pay her back in increments in 2026, but she only received a $200 check. She said the company no longer responds to her emails about payments, complaining that “they just ghost [me].”

“It was causing me so much stress that it was making me sick so at a certain point I had to let go and let God have his way,” Padua said. “I can’t let them give me a heart attack.”

Padua, who was crying when recalling the situation, said losing payments “was very difficult physically, emotionally, and financially,” adding: “I worked for them for so long and I love that military community and I was good at my job and just to be done so dirty it feels terrible.”

She said she was “counting on” those payments and was reassured “you’re going to get paid.”

“Should I tell that to my mortgage company? For my car loans? For my bills?” she asked.

Another subcontractor who said she faced similar issues is Dianne Hodges, who had two contracts with Idemma, one of which was paid late and the other which is still not paid off. She said most of it was paid off by June 2026, about a year after she’d completed the initial contract.

Hodges said they still owe her $3,200 for the other contract she worked but that Idemma did not respond to her most recent emails in August about the remaining balance, saying “they’ve gone radio silent on me” and worrying “I guess I’ll never see it.”

“It’s been a nightmare,” Hodges said. “It’s been an absolute nightmare.”

Hodges said the delayed payments led to trouble with creditors and late fees on credit cards that she couldn’t pay off. She had to pull money out of her 401K to pay her bills and shop for Christmas gifts in 2024.

“It was tough for me sometimes to make ends meet,” she said, adding that when she called Idemma about the financial struggles she faced that year, “I broke down in tears, I was telling them this is not how a business works.”

Morgan Loftis, who worked as a director of religious education at the Marine Corps Air Station New River from September 2025 through May 2026, told EWTN News she is also still owed thousands of dollars in payments from Idemma.

Loftis said she was owed $12,300 but was only paid $4,875, which leaves $7,425 unpaid.

In May 2026, before she left the role, she said Idemma “offered to pay me in full … if I stayed onto the next year because they were about to lose the contract.” She said she considered the offer and requested “an actual payment plan in writing” but never received one. Now, she said “they won’t take my calls.”

“I think they know our numbers and they’re just not going to respond,” she said, referring to the subcontractors who are still owed money.

Loftis said she took the role even though she heard other subcontractors were not getting paid, but “I wanted there to be a faith formation program and it looked like there wasn’t going to be one.”

Yet, as she and her husband are expecting their fifth child and bought a new car, she said, “it would be really nice to have had the full pay. That could really alleviate how hard that car payment hits.”

They give you a false choice. Sit home and wait for Christ or become a confessional state in America.

Roger Williams was not hostile to Christianity. He was a Puritan minister of intense religious conviction who founded Rhode Island after being banished from Massachusetts. His defense of liberty of conscience came not from indifference to Christianity but from his understanding of Christianity. He believed that forced religion corrupted both civil government and the church. His famous formulation was that “forced worship stinks in God’s nostrils.” For Williams, separating civil coercion from faith was not surrender to secularism. It protected the purity of faith because genuine worship had to be offered to God voluntarily.

John Leland, the eighteenth-century Baptist minister and one of the strongest evangelical advocates of religious liberty, made the same argument. Leland was hardly asking Christians to become politically passive. He preached constantly, participated in public controversies, defended religious liberty, and exerted political influence. Yet he attacked government-established Christianity because he believed Christianity had been harmed whenever it became dependent upon civil power. In his 1791 Rights of Conscience Inalienable, Leland criticized Constantine’s establishment of Christianity and Protestant establishments alike. His concern was specifically Christian: the church should operate according to Christ rather than through the coercive machinery of government.

James Madison argued that religion could be directed only by “reason and conviction, not by force or violence.”

Washington ignored the language of mere “toleration,” because toleration implies that a dominant group graciously permits a subordinate group to exist. Instead, he wrote that Americans possessed “liberty of conscience” as an inherent right and elevated the idea that the United States government “gives to bigotry no sanction, to persecution no assistance.”

Preach the Gospel. Publish the sermon. Build the church. Establish the school. Debate your opponent. Persuade your neighbors. Raise your children. Organize charities. Form associations. Argue from Scripture. Stand in the public square and make your case.

But if your Christianity can only survive only by preventing someone else from disagreeing with you, you already lost. 

Christianity is true, it does not need Caesar to manufacture Christians.

Christ Himself refused that. When the rich young ruler rejected His demand, Christ let him walk away (Mark 10:21–22). When a Samaritan village rejected Him and His disciples wanted judgment called down upon it, Christ rebuked them (Luke 9:51–56). When people attempted to seize Him and make Him king, He withdrew (John 6:15). When Peter reached for the sword, Christ commanded him to put it away (Matthew 26:52). Before Pilate, with His life literally in the hands of the state, Christ still distinguished His kingdom from kingdoms maintained by force (John 18:36).

“Go therefore and make disciples of all nations” (Matthew 28:19)

You want more Christian nation then why don’t you start by being a better Christian. And then why don’t you go and take that and apply it to your family your community your church your state. 

You want a more Christian nation learn how to be more persuasive, make disciples and vote for policies that allow you to live your Christian life.

text:
Fender Modern Player Coronado review
A cult-classic electric rebooted

While it wasn't a roaring success on its initial release, the guitar has found enough favour among a range of leftfield musicians and alternative rockers over the last couple of decades to keep interest bubbling away, and the prices of vintage examples on a steady upward trajectory.

Unlike the original hollowbody Coronado, the Modern Player features an alder centre block to help minimise feedback, and a pair of Fideli'Tron humbucking pickups - Fender's Gretsch Filter'Tron-style units developed for its Mexican-made Cabronita Telecasters.
Although dispensing with some of the quirks of the original design may irk fans of the vintage model, these largely pragmatic changes help Fender to deliver the guitar at a price, and in some cases arguably make for a smoother ride for the contemporary player.

Aesthetically, it's as cool as you like; the timeless Candy Apple Red is our preferred finish. As is customary, there's an upcharge for 'Burst and Natural finishes, which will set you back an extra £48 on the retail price.
With front strap-button position at the heel, Strat and Tele players may find that the standing playing position of both instruments takes a little adjustment, but it's far from a deal-breaker.

Predictably, Filter'Tron-style pickups in a semi-acoustic chassis make for a Gretsch-like set of tones - it just begs for a Bigsby and lashings of spring reverb. Fideli'Trons don't quite have the aggressive midrange growl or the level of harmonic complexity offered by Gretsch's Japanese-made Filter'Trons or aftermarket TV Jones pickups, but they certainly get in the right ballpark for a variety of styles, from rockabilly and indie jangle, or even to overdriven classic-rock rhythm playing.

If you're a tonehound looking for a guitar for Texas blues or a metalhead who craves bottom-end definition, this instrument is unlikely to be for you. It is, however, a great guitar for indie rock players who love effects, with the Coronado having a decent range at the 1950s rock 'n' roll end of the spectrum thanks to its Gretsch-inspired core sounds.

text:
Real serious talk time. This will be a long post - but I am sickened and heart broken. 

If you are gate keeping 9/11 memorial posts. Please get of the internet, take a step back and re-evaluate your life and have some fucking compassion. 

Today I came across a post that someone made honoring 9/11 and then they were complaining because someone else made a 9/11 remembrance post and it sickened me to my core. 

I was 10 years old. 

September 11th 2001 is a day about remembering those who died in the attacks. On the planes, in the towers, the pentagon and the rural field.  It's about those who jumped from the towers, those who never made it down the stairs. Those who spend their last minutes calling loved ones to say their last goodbyes. 

It's about the firefighters who, when MANY people were running down the stairs, went UP the stairs, knowing THEY were never going to come back down.  They WILLINGLY and SELFLESSLY gave their lives. It's about the countless people who worked ground zero, tirelessly pulling survivors and the dead from the rubble. 

It's remembering the innocent people whose lives were stolen that day and those who fought so hard to help. 

It's the mothers, fathers, sons and daughters who were lost that day or lost a loved one that day. 

Thousands of lives were lost that day and Thousands more where forever altered. 

It's a little town called Gander in New found land Canada who offered their homes, food, water, phone lines, shelter too complete  strangers on planes who were diverted to their airport and ordered to be grounded. 

It's my 5th grade French teacher walking into our classroom, sitting down in silence and saying nothing for his sister was on the plane that hit the north tower. 

It's the lady who lives in the town 20 minutes from me who kissed her husband goodbye, not knowing the next day he would be murdered. 

And to those who developed health problems in the years following due to the smoke and chemicals. 

For the countless EMT's first responders, nurses, doctors, firefighters, police officers, military and so much more. 

Canine units who sniffed the ground - Dogs who worked tirelessly to also find those trapped in the rubble. Some of our most loyal workers those days had four legs. 

A nation ripped apart, which the world mourned with. 

We honor and remember those. We all maybe be different skin colors, different backgrounds - but we bleed one color and our hearts beat the same. 

I personally want to thank those who sacrificed their lives that day, and to those who continue to serve. Thank you so much for your service. 

Be you Army, Navy, Air Force. 
EMT, First responder, or what have you. 
Thank you.

And to the disgusting people gate keeping 9/11 memorials - Sit your fucking ass down and learn some respect for man-kind. The world doesn't revolve your sorry ass.

text:
I was AGR T-32. Got force fed to recruiting. There were 16 authorized 79T positions that could receive pro-pay as recruiters. 

I was the 17th recruiter. No pro-pay for me unless someone left recruiting or died.

I put in my T-10 AGR packet to go to NGB. The admin folks at HQ STARC were told to sit on my packet.  I missed the NGB board in June/July. I pitched enough of a fit that they finally submitted my packet to NGB. 

About a week before I was scheduled to report to recruiting school, I got a call. I was offered a good position. Something I had never done but it sounded like a good move for me.

The “leadership” in recruiting wanted me working every weekend possible prior to a PCS to NGB. I ended up taking 39 days of leave to prep our house for sale.  

Best move I ever made was to get out of the state.  

I never looked back. 

Three years later, I was at mob station to go to Iraq. 

Even though I was T-10 and fell in under AGR organizations at NGB and in the MDW area, that state level mentality of the Guard remained. The best gig I had, short of flying, was when I was assigned to an active duty base in a DA civilian coded position. 

If that base’s TDA had not been decimated by force management and the division I was in had not been removed, I would’ve applied for that job when I retired.  

You would not believe the bullshit I put up with as the only female Army aviation mechanic and air crew member in that state. 

I’m sure you saw it as a male but it always felt like the harder I tried the more folks wanted to see me fall flat on my face. In the end, it didn’t matter how good I was at my job.

BTW. I had a really good boss when I was T-32. He had asked our COL if they could send me to flight school.

The COL’s response was “Not only no but fuck no”. 

There is no way in hell I could’ve stayed in that state as a recruiter as I would have had a hard time selling something I just didn’t believe in.

Keep the composition steady with tiny, irregular handheld tremors and gentle breathing drift. Use ordinary household lighting, natural skin texture and stable exposure. No cuts, zooms, camera orbit, dramatic shaking, beauty filters or cinematic color grading.

EMOTIONAL PERFORMANCE:
0~6 seconds — Forced smile.
The listener asks a brief question about the situation. The MAIN CHARACTER gives a short reassuring reply while hiding their distress. Their mouth smiles, but their eyes remain sad. They blink slightly faster, briefly look down and restore the strained smile.

6~12 seconds — Unable to explain.
The listener gently recognizes that something went wrong. The MAIN CHARACTER quietly acknowledges it, then starts to explain but cannot continue. Their smile fades, gaze drops and throat makes a small swallow. One hand briefly touches the back of their own neck, then lowers.

12~20 seconds — Emotional release.
The listener offers a short line of understanding. The MAIN CHARACTER begins a brief reply, but their voice falters. Clear tears gather at the lower eyelids and roll down the cheeks. Breathing catches, lip corners pull downward, the chin trembles and the shoulders shake slightly. Natural soft sobbing.

20~28 seconds — Relief.
The listener offers a final brief reassurance. The MAIN CHARACTER releases a long shaky exhale, closes their eyes briefly and relaxes their shoulders. Fingertips lightly touch their own temple without covering the face. ONLY AFTER the exhale ends, they give a quiet short reply and a tiny tearful smile. Preserve the wet tear tracks.

Keep the MAIN CHARACTER's natural skin tone stable, including during crying. No exaggerated blush, red face, pink makeup patches or facial distortion. Express emotion through tears, breathing and muscle movement.

Use two distinct natural voices matching the characters. Write short, conversational lines in the selected language, leaving time for silent reactions. Accurately synchronize the MAIN CHARACTER's speech with their mouth; never swap speakers. Include room ambience, breathing and soft sobs. No narration, music, subtitles, on-screen text, labels, logos or extra people.

text:
Goshuin—Why Do the Japanese Find Such Romance in Them?

When visiting shrines and temples in Japan, you will often see people cherishingly holding a special book known as a *goshuin-cho* (seal book).

Inside, they collect *goshuin*—calligraphic seals or stamps.

To a foreign observer,
it might look like nothing more than collecting stamps.

But for the Japanese, a *goshuin* is far more than just a stamp.

It captures the specific "time" and "memories" of having visited that place.

Take, for instance, a shrine encountered while traveling.

You pass through a beautiful *torii* gate, walk through the quiet grounds, and offer a prayer to the deity or Buddha.

Finally, you receive the *goshuin*.

Just by looking at that single page,

"I went there."
"It was raining that day."
"I traveled with this person."

Such memories come flooding back.

That is why the *goshuin-cho* serves as both a travel album and a small narrative recording one's encounters with Japanese culture.

There is also a romantic allure to *goshuin* rooted in the concept of *ichi-go ichi-e*—the idea that every encounter is a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

Even at the same shrine or temple, the character of the calligraphy varies depending on who writes it.

The shading of the ink, the vigor of the brushstrokes, the vermilion seal.

Each one is a unique creation born of that specific moment.

Perhaps the romance Japanese people find in *goshuin* lies in

"traveling to a distant place and keeping something in one's own hands that could only be found there."

With a smartphone, you can store thousands of photos.

But a *goshuin* cannot be obtained unless you physically travel to that location yourself.

That is precisely why a single *goshuin* stands as proof that "I was there."

You open your *goshuin-cho*.

Laid out before you are your past journeys.

With every page you view, the atmosphere, the scenery, and the encounters with people from those places come back to life.

It is not merely a collection.

The *goshuin* is a cultural tradition through which Japanese people preserve their travels, prayers, moments in time, and memories within the pages of a single book. And when that notebook is finally full—

what you hold is not merely paper,

but the completed story of your own unique journey through Japan.

text:
Washington Links Chinese Satellite Imagery to the Jordan Strike That Killed Three U.S. Troops

The Wall Street Journal

U.S. officials have linked high-resolution satellite imagery obtained by Iran from Chinese entities to the July 17 missile strike on Muwaffaq al-Salti Air Base in Jordan, which killed three American soldiers and wounded several others. The account, as reported by The Wall Street Journal from officials familiar with the matter, offers the clearest evidence yet that Chinese support for Tehran had lethal consequences for U.S. forces.

The officials did not identify the Chinese entities and did not accuse Beijing of direct involvement. They said Iran obtained the imagery both before and after the attack. China rejected the allegations and demanded proof. The disclosure comes ahead of a planned Sept. 24 meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.

The base that is no longer safe

The base in eastern Jordan hosts U.S. forces and air-defense systems as part of the American deployment in the region. As the war widened after late February, it became a repeated target, then a turning point after American troops were killed there. Ballistic missiles struck prefabricated housing units where soldiers from air-defense units were living. Footage that appeared within hours showed the moment the missiles fell inside the military compound.

Images before launch and after impact

The heart of the account is not the strike alone, but the source of the eye that saw the base before the missile was fired. Fresh images before an attack make it possible to pinpoint shelters, aircraft and living quarters; images afterward allow an assessment of the damage. That is how a satellite picture moves from a commercial product to a link in the targeting chain.

Washington had already sanctioned Chinese satellite companies, including entities accused of providing imagery that enabled Iran to strike U.S. forces. The new account goes further: it ties a specific image to a specific strike and to specific dead.

The sea is under the lens as well

The concerns do not stop at land bases. U.S. officials fear the imagery could help Iran track naval vessels. Those fears come as Tehran’s ability to hit moving ships has appeared to improve. A ship is not a fixed runway; if repeated images and analysis of position and speed are available, the time between detection and launch shrinks.

Between denial and the date of the meeting

Beijing rejects the charge. Washington distinguishes between the state and “Chinese entities.” Yet the commercial imagery market, and the artificial intelligence that reads runways and carriers, have made claimed neutrality less persuasive after three soldiers were killed at an allied base. The coming Trump-Xi meeting puts the file on the table: oil, sanctions, sea lanes and dual-use technology. The question is no longer whether Chinese images reached Tehran, but whether an image helped kill Americans on Jordanian soil.

text:
WAR OR CHEAP GAS

At the BRICS summit in New Delhi, Putin walked past the Kremlin press
pool and took one shouted question — from Kommersant's Andrei
Kolesnikov, who asked what he made of the AfD's win in Saxony-Anhalt.
Putin opened by saying he would not comment on another country's
domestic politics. He then commented for eight minutes.

The framing was familiar: what is happening in Europe is the product
of "systemic mistakes" by Western globalist elites. The economic half
was the usual ledger — Europeans once called Russian gas at $150–180
per thousand cubic metres expensive and now pay considerably more —
with a seasonal jab attached. Germany, he noted, is trying to get its
storage to 70% and may not manage it. The Netherlands, in his telling,
is worse off.

Then he moved to security, and here the language hardened. European
governments, he argued, frighten their own populations with Russia
while steering those same populations toward a direct collision with
it. Deploying European troops to Ukraine, he said, "means war with
Russia." That is about as blunt a formulation as he has used on the
subject.

The alternative he offered is a restoration. He reached again for a
1990s conversation with Helmut Kohl, who he says told him Europe could
only endure as an independent centre of civilisation together with
Russia. Worth noting: there is no independent record of that
conversation, and Putin's own earliest version of it, in his 2000 book
of interviews, was considerably more modest — Kohl merely could not
imagine Europe existing without Russia. The story has grown in the
retelling.

He also restated the security architecture Moscow will accept.
Everything, he said, was settled by the outcome of the Second World
War; what followed the Soviet collapse was done with Russia's consent
as legal successor; anything contradicting that contradicts Russian
interests. Strip the historical dressing and this is the December 2021
ultimatum to NATO and Washington, delivered again, in a friendlier
room.

So: two futures. Stay the course, refuse the gas, put soldiers in
Ukraine, get a war. Or come back to the old arrangement and get peace
and cheap energy.

The reason this was worth eight minutes is what the second option
overlaps with. The AfD's Saxony-Anhalt platform runs on the same three
planks — lift the energy sanctions, normalise trade with Moscow,
restart Russian pipeline gas through Nord Stream. Putin was not
endorsing a German party. He was pointing at a German party already
selling his product, and telling the rest of Europe it is available.

The numbers behind the moment: AfD 43.8% against the CDU's 17.2%, 39
of 83 seats, three short of an absolute majority. First time since
1945 that a far-right party has come this close to running a German
state.

text:
I’ve spent 10 years working at tech companies in Silicon Valley
5 of those had been with Apple
Here’s what you need to know before upgrading your iPhone:

1. Make sure you know your Apple ID email and password, and you have a valid iCloud backup, if you are planning to transfer phone to phone just know that it may take a minute per gigabyte of storage, so it would take a long time, you’ll need a good WiFi, and both phone on the charger, you could also use a cable to speed up the process.

2. Think of how you use your current phone and how are you planning to use the new one, sometimes the best or the most expensive device isn’t the best for your needs.

3. If you have music that was purchased very long time ago or transferred to your iPhone, they may not come over through your iCloud backup as some permission may have expired, so you may need to transfer phone to phone.

4. DO NOT trade in your iPhone at the same transaction, unless if you are doing an iPhone upgrade program, or a carrier deal.
Apple allows you 14 days to go back to the store for the trade in, and get your money back as a refund to the same form of payment, if any hiccups in data trader occurs after you trade in the old phone, and especially if you don’t have iCloud backup up, you’ll never get your data back!

5. Check your current storage and be honest with yourself regarding how often you would upgrade, most people don’t need 1-2T but they get them because their current phone’s storage of 128 is full!
If you had your data transferred from your very first iPhone, that’s one or nearly 2 decades of data in 128, unless you’ll use your new iPhone to create video content, most likely you don’t need the extra storage, that extra $200-$400 you pay, if you don’t touch that storage by the time you trade it in, you’ll never get it back, as it doesn’t factor into your trade in value.

6. Check for the content that are using most of your storage, in your settings> General> iPhone storage, sometimes you’ve downloaded movies or podcasts and will never use them, but they take up so much of your storage, it could be duplicate media in your messages or WhatsApp, it could be offloaded apps that weren’t deleted and still have documents and data, and sometimes there’s a bug in your System data that’s causing it to occupy most of your storage, which in this case you’ll need to sync your data to iCloud (not a full backup) and restore your iPhone using a computer then setting up as new, then logging in using your Apple ID 

7. Make sure you back up your third party apps that are end to end encrypted like WhatsApp, if they aren’t set up in the app, you will lose your data.

8. If you have a watch, make sure it’s compatible with iOS 27, most watches aren’t, they only ones that are compatible are:
Apple Watch series 9-11
Apple Watch Ultra 2-3
& Apple Watch SE 3rd Gen.
Otherwise you may need to upgrade your watch too.

9. If you are going with the Apple upgrade program, don’t forget to add Apple Care, if you have multiple devices or multiple family members explore Apple Care One and Apple Family as they offer massive discounts and cover theft and loss for iPad and watch on top of the iPhone
This is because in the upgrade you don’t own the phone, when you return it back and it has damages, you’ll have to fix it,
A damaged display would be $379
A damaged enclosure would be $379
If only one glass of your 3 cameras gets cracked and the camera gets exposed that’s $408
A damaged display plus enclosure plus back glass or exposed camera would be $899 total.
Apple Care+ is $119 for the year, and if the display gets damaged that’s $29 only, the whole device gets damaged and the max you would pay is $99.

10. If you drive a Tesla make sure your key card is with you in case anything goes wrong, in fact make sure you have your it at all times.

11. Get iCloud regardless, it’s crazy to me that many people don’t have any type of back up, wedding photos, baby photos… they may lose them any minute.

text:
I had one of the biggest shockers of my life today. I have to tell this story to get it off my chest. Its personal family stuff, but Im in no way personal with extended family so who cares.

I havent talked to my sister in 15 years. My niece and my nephew are now estranged.

My nephew has had mental health problems for years. About 4 years ago, something happened to him. For some reason, and I do have a wild 6th sense, I sensed he had some sort of spiritual awakening, something cracked open. I was told it may have been drugs back then. I didnt assume that was it, but I kept an open mind.

I heard he was hearing voices and I wondered...oh no, did he get visited, has he been having interdimensional experiences? I contacted him, I tried to tell him this may be a shamanic type experience and was trying to get him to tell me if anything 'visited' him. I think he was overwhelmed by it all, and felt strange about talking about it. And he was hiding things.

Now, years later, I live in AZ, Im on bad terms with my sister for 15 years. But she has left California after retiring, and he's pretty much alone out there, has no friends, and lies about his situation all the time. Im worried about him. My dad wants to help him.

So I contact him, after not talking to him for years. Hes telling me about communication with 'gods', and he mentoned Baba Yaga and hero training, this is Baba Yaga New Age BS.....Baba Yaga is a demon, an ancient Slavic witch that cannibalized children and people. It is one of the real dark entities that DO EXIST in the other dimensions. Whether you believe it or not.

Then he gets nasty with me when I have to bring him back to reality after he tells me he has super powers, Clark Kent lives in Las Vegas, that he understands reality far beyond what I know, is somehow involved in a high level of politics and Im suddenly in a battle of gaslighting with my Millenial SCHIZO nephew.

So to summarize, my nephew had some sort of paranormal experience 4 years ago, drug induced most likely like DMT or Cartridges or Ayahuasca or I dont know. And he was demonically possessed. Thats what I personally think. But, the conversation I just had with him was much deeper, someone with occult knowledge. Baba Yaga can be a silly New Age thing, or an intense dark energy used by occult practitioners.

How did I know 4 years ago he had some paranormal experience? He obviously did because now he has occult knowledge. Did something happen to him at the Hospital he was sent to? As a kid I know he was relentlessly bullied. But 'preyed upon' he said, and he's talking dark ass Deep State occultism shit...he cant just be making this up, can he? 15 years is a long time.

He is messed up...."Clark Kent lives in Las Vegas. You dont even know. I know Kung Fu, all the hot famous women want to screw me. I live in multiple realities at the same time. I know Donald Trump. Im involved in politics at the highest level. Everyone just thinks Im Sad Bryan works at a gas station, they dont even know...."

I just found out my nephew is out of his freaking mind living a fantasy life, and hes somehow involved with occult power and tells me hes being preyed upon.

And he's talking Baba Yaga. 

And...he sounded perfectly happy and sane while he was being insane. Or was he? When I was in San Francisco for a decade, we used to hear about Bohemian Grove. Nobody called it that. I know these things are for real. And if my nephew got involved with the wrong people, could he be living a double life with some...secret society?

I dont know now. I think he's out of his freaking mind and I think he fried his brain with drugs. But this conversation I had with him....I am so confused right now. The things he mentioned and what he said and the things he chose to say to me were....strange. It was like he was trying to tell me something but couldnt tell me. he wouldnt answer direct questions.

Im literally in shock right now. Is this an 'A Beautiful Mind' scenario I just experienced with my nephew...or something deeper. Darker. Is he involved in some Society of occultists? I....wow....I have to wonder.

I cant get involved, I have my own spiritual life, and THAT can never get me. I will walk away from it and recognize it immediately. No one could ever approach me and coerce me or offer me anything to do anything. Whenever Ive felt too close to things, I avoid them. I will forget I was told things I wish I never knew. I just stay in my lane. Trust me, nobody cares anyway.

Im just gonna stay in my lane on this. If he is involved with people he shouldnt be, they own him and nothing I can do. If hes crazy, he needs to go get help.

I thought I was the only one in my family who knew anything about anything. Now...I am literally disturbed my nephew is either involved in some shit he shouldnt be, or he's like 'A Beautiful Mind'. The occult element in all of this really gives me pause to say he's completely crazy. 

It worries me enough to tell my mother and father to not trust him, dont invite him over, stay away from him.

I just dont know 100% whats going on, either way. And I refuse to talk to my sister. I have zero experience with a schizophrenic, it may just be classic schizophrenia. But damn...he literally sounded like there was some Eyes Wide Shut shit going on. Why would you create a fantasy existence like that? I am so disturbed, and I have to walk away and cant let this get near me.

I cant stand my sister more than ever, and Im wondering what she got involved in now.

But like my 6th sense is telling me...Im afraid my nephew is part of something he shouldnt be possibly. Im hoping he's a schizo, Id be happier for his soul.
