text:
September 11 feed catch-up: company finance, operations and leadership.

These notices vary a lot in investment value. My focus is what each could change in cash flow, execution or risk, and what still needs evidence.

Village Super Market ($VLGEA) declared quarterly dividends of $0.25 per Class A share and $0.1625 per Class B share, payable October 22 to holders of record October 1. That maintains a cash return to owners. The investment case still depends on supermarket cash generation, food and labor margins, and whether earnings comfortably cover the payout.
https://t.co/WIWCZAYTrc

Gran Tierra ($GTE) is seeking consents on $479.353 million of 9.75% secured amortizing notes due 2031 to support its previously announced asset sale and the buyer's assumption of debt obligations. The proposed fee is $2.50 per $1,000, with consents due September 22 at 5 p.m. New York time unless extended or terminated. Approval and closing remain conditions. My read: a transaction milestone to watch for debt reduction and the shape of the remaining business; the solicitation itself does not complete the sale.
https://t.co/v9TkjcFgeo

KB Home ($KBH) opened Lakeside Bluffs in Lake Stevens, Washington, with townhomes starting in the $490,000s. It adds a place to generate orders. The useful next evidence is sales pace, cancellations, incentives and gross margin. A community opening alone tells us little about the strength of national housing demand.
https://t.co/ZNuxPZDJpN

Baltisse, Peruna and RPM Living acquired a 374-unit Irving, Texas apartment property, now The Louis Las Colinas, with improvements planned. Price and cap rate were not disclosed in the release. This is evidence of buyers committing to one property; occupancy, renovation costs and financing terms would determine whether it is a good investment. It provides no reliable valuation benchmark for listed apartment REITs yet.
https://t.co/2zPnDy8HIn

o15 Capital reported the realization of a $31 million senior secured facility to Simplify Compliance after the datacenterHawk sale to S&P Global. The $31 million refers to financing that was repaid; it is not a disclosed investment profit. One exit releases capital for the lender, but offers limited evidence about losses or returns across private credit. The acquisition's contribution to S&P earnings was not quantified here.
https://t.co/kFLY0HKE2d

KBRA assigned AA- with a stable outlook to McCormick Place project refunding bonds and affirmed the existing rating. This matters to the municipal issuer's credit and refinancing terms. Tourism-linked tax collections and debt coverage are the relevant measures; the rating supplies no direct earnings upgrade for hotel or travel stocks.
https://t.co/BMQ5P3PC64

A study estimates that the nonprofit White Memorial hospitals support more than $1.2 billion of annual economic activity in Los Angeles County. That includes activity beyond the hospitals' own operations, so treating it as revenue or fresh stimulus would be misleading. The market-relevant issue is reimbursement pressure and the cost of sustaining care, with no direct listed-company earnings change established by this study.
https://t.co/b9XRYvzAmh

Omnis Energy says the bankruptcy court disqualified HSF Kramer from representing Pleasants Power Station. Its release says other counsel remains and the sale process continues on its existing schedule. This is one party's account of a procedural ruling. It does not settle asset value, creditor recoveries or the ownership dispute, so I would avoid drawing a power-sector trading conclusion from it.
https://t.co/atqbF2J2LC

Teamsters say more than 200 Bimbo Bakeries workers in New England ratified a six-year contract, with 90% support. That reduces immediate strike risk for the covered operations, while wage and benefit improvements can raise employer costs. The net margin effect depends on pricing, productivity and the cost of disruption avoided; the announcement does not quantify it.
https://t.co/ITniGt8pHg

Kentucky American Water ($AWK) completed water-main replacements around North Limestone, Euclid and Fontaine in Lexington. More reliable infrastructure can reduce service problems. For shareholders, value depends on project cost, allowed regulatory recovery and financing, rather than completion alone. The release does not supply a new earnings estimate.
https://t.co/27StNQ55Ov

Capital Power and Alpine Canada announced a sports partnership MOU proposing $5 million in first-year sponsorship. Potential total support of $25 million is conditional on further organizational and government-funding steps. This is sponsorship spending and community investment; it does not establish new electricity sales, generation capacity or a change in the US power-demand outlook.
https://t.co/ghqONDKByv

Pan Global engaged Adelaide Capital for investor relations through September 30 for C$12,500 plus tax, subject to exchange approval, with no securities awarded. Better investor communication can improve awareness. Drilling, resources, permitting and funding remain the evidence needed to change the mining investment case.
https://t.co/aW0MFwkGy6

Computer Modelling Group, which trades as CMG in Toronto, reported that all matters at its September 10 AGM were approved and all seven director nominees were elected. The read-through is governance continuity. Customer demand, recurring revenue and cash conversion will do more to determine equity value than a routine voting result.
https://t.co/gAwev5x47t

MaxCyte ($MXCT) disclosed 220,000 options and 110,000 restricted stock units for its new corporate development chief, granted August 31. These incentives can support retention and also create potential dilution. Future business development results will show whether shareholders receive enough value for that cost.
https://t.co/rlTYyKzGjh

Arteris ($AIP) granted its new CFO 142,835 RSUs and a target 38,604 performance units. The performance award has revenue and share-price hurdles. Those hurdles are compensation conditions, not management guidance or a stock-price forecast. Investors should assess dilution alongside actual growth and financial execution.
https://t.co/XMzUuU56uG

Oportun ($OPRT) disclosed 382,653 RSUs and a target 127,551 performance units for Chief Risk Officer Sean Rowles. The hiring award adds potential dilution. The substantive test is whether underwriting and collections improve loss-adjusted returns; the award itself does not show that credit quality has improved.
https://t.co/pc6GjXC8rW

Standard Lithium ($SLI) said Karen Narwold will leave its board September 15 because of commitments associated with a new executive role. An independent-director search is underway. This warrants watching board capacity and succession; the release provides no new evidence about lithium project economics or construction progress.
https://t.co/QBNlBd5Vml

Amrize ($AMRZ) appointed Mario Gross president of Building Envelope, succeeding Jake Gosa. Gross has prior operating experience in the segment. The useful follow-through is roofing and insulation volumes, pricing and margins as he takes over. An appointment alone does not change those numbers.
https://t.co/KRwQFuuKlD

Agomab ($AGMB) shareholders approved Marino Garcia and Naimish Patel as non-executive directors, plus adjustments to pre-IPO warrants. Board experience may support development decisions. Clinical evidence, development spending and available cash remain the more direct drivers of the biotech's value.
https://t.co/8QKHyabtSk

LV Petroleum welcomed Jamie Hubbard to lead construction and maintenance. His role is relevant to opening and maintaining travel centers efficiently. For the wider market, the hire does not establish higher fuel demand, retail sales or earnings for a listed partner.
https://t.co/Jlb3t1QniX

𝗖𝗮𝗿𝗮 𝗖𝗮𝗿𝗮 𝗼𝗿𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 offer Kenyan farmers an option for producing sweet, seedless oranges with attractive pink to red flesh.

Farmers Trend Virtual Agrovet supplies grafted Cara Cara orange seedlings at 𝗞𝗦𝗵 𝟲𝟬𝟬 𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴.

The seedlings are suitable for farmers establishing small orchards, kitchen gardens and commercial citrus farms.

Cara Cara is a navel orange cultivar recognised by its pink to red flesh, sweet flavour and seedless fruit.

The fruit looks similar to an ordinary navel orange from the outside. The difference becomes clear after cutting the fruit open.

The flesh has a distinctive pink or reddish colour, making the variety attractive for fresh fruit sales, hospitality businesses, juice preparation and premium produce markets.

Cara Cara developed from a natural mutation of Washington navel orange. The variety has since been grown in several citrus-producing regions.

For Kenyan farmers, the main attraction is the combination of familiar orange characteristics with a different internal appearance.

🌱 𝗪𝗛𝗬 𝗖𝗛𝗢𝗢𝗦𝗘 𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗙𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗦𝗘𝗘𝗗𝗟𝗜𝗡𝗚𝗦?

The planting material you start with affects the future of your orchard.

Grafted seedlings combine a selected Cara Cara scion with a citrus rootstock. This gives farmers planting material designed to maintain the characteristics of the selected cultivar.

For commercial farming, grafted seedlings also offer a more predictable starting point than growing citrus from seed.

When buying Cara Cara orange seedlings, check:

✅ The variety

✅ Graft quality

✅ Root health

✅ General seedling vigour

✅ Nursery reputation

✅ Disease-free planting material

A farmer who saves money on poor planting material might spend much more later replacing weak or unsuitable trees.

10 seedlings = KSh 6,000

50 seedlings = KSh 30,000

100 seedlings = KSh 60,000

250 seedlings = KSh 150,000

Your complete orchard budget should also include land preparation, manure, fertilizer, irrigation, labour, pest management, disease control, weed management and harvesting.

Seedling price gives you only one part of the investment picture.

📐 𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗬 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗢𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗘 𝗧𝗥𝗘𝗘𝗦 𝗙𝗜𝗧 𝗜𝗡 𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗔𝗖𝗥𝗘?

A 4 m × 4 m spacing gives approximately 250 planting positions per acre before accounting for access paths, boundaries and other farm structures.

This spacing gives trees room to develop their canopies while allowing farmers to move through the orchard for spraying, pruning, harvesting and other operations.

The final spacing should consider soil fertility, rootstock, terrain, irrigation, pruning practices and the expected size of mature trees.

Avoid squeezing too many trees into an acre simply to increase the tree count.

A crowded orchard often creates more management problems.

🌍 𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗧𝗢 𝗚𝗥𝗢𝗪 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗢𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗘𝗦 𝗜𝗡 𝗞𝗘𝗡𝗬𝗔

Cara Cara oranges require suitable temperatures, adequate sunlight, good drainage and reliable moisture.

Potential citrus-growing areas include:

📍 Murang'a

📍 Kiambu

📍 Embu

📍 Meru

📍 Machakos

📍 Makueni

📍 Kitui

📍 Kisii

📍 Parts of coastal Kenya

The county alone does not determine whether your farm will perform well.

Your soil, water supply, elevation, temperature, drainage and management practices all matter.

☀️ 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗢𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗘 𝗚𝗥𝗢𝗪𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗗𝗜𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦

🌡️ 𝗧𝗲𝗺𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲

Range of approximately 15°C to 30°C.

☀️ 𝗦𝘂𝗻𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁

Plant in an open location with good sunlight exposure. Adequate light supports healthy tree growth and fruit development.

💧 𝗪𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗿

A rainfall range of approximately 800 to 1,200 mm annually is listed in the growing guide where drainage is good.

Where rainfall is unreliable, irrigation helps maintain consistent moisture.

🌱 𝗦𝗼𝗶𝗹

Well-drained loam or sandy-loam soil suits citrus production.

Avoid waterlogged sites.

🧪 𝗦𝗼𝗶𝗹 𝗽𝗛

A pH of approximately 5.5 to 6.5 is listed as suitable.

Your soil test should guide lime, manure and fertilizer decisions.

🕳️ 𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗧𝗢 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗧 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗢𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗘 𝗦𝗘𝗘𝗗𝗟𝗜𝗡𝗚𝗦

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟭: 𝗣𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗹𝗮𝗻𝗱

Clear unwanted vegetation and establish your orchard layout before planting.

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟮: 𝗧𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗼𝗶𝗹

Test pH, organic matter and available nutrients.

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟯: 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗸 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗱

Use your chosen spacing to mark straight rows.

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟰: 𝗗𝗶𝗴 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗵𝗼𝗹𝗲𝘀

The Farmers Trend guide recommends approximately 60 cm × 60 cm × 60 cm holes.

Keep topsoil separate from subsoil during preparation.

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟱: 𝗣𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗼𝗹𝗲𝘀

Mix well-decomposed manure with suitable topsoil. Apply fertilizer according to soil-test recommendations.

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟲: 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴

Plant the seedling upright and avoid damaging the root ball.

Keep the graft union above soil level.

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟳: 𝗪𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗮𝗳𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴

Give the young tree adequate water immediately after planting.

𝗦𝘁𝗲𝗽 𝟴: 𝗠𝘂𝗹𝗰𝗵

Apply suitable organic mulch around the tree to conserve moisture and reduce weed growth.

Keep mulch away from the stem.

🌿 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗔𝗚𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗔 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗢𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗘 𝗢𝗥𝗖𝗛𝗔𝗥𝗗

Good orchard management starts immediately after planting.

𝗪𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴

Young trees require consistent moisture during establishment. Irrigation becomes important during prolonged dry periods.

𝗪𝗲𝗲𝗱 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘁𝗿𝗼𝗹

Keep competing vegetation away from young trees. Take care when cultivating around citrus because root damage affects tree health.

𝗡𝘂𝘁𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Use soil analysis to guide fertilizer applications. Avoid applying fertilizer based on guesswork.

Young trees need nutrients for canopy development. Productive trees need balanced nutrition for flowering, fruit development and recovery after harvest.

𝗣𝗿𝘂𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴

Remove dead, damaged and diseased branches. Remove unwanted shoots growing below the graft union.

Maintain an open and manageable canopy.

𝗣𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴

Inspect trees regularly for pests such as aphids, citrus leaf miner and fruit flies.

Identify the pest before selecting a control method.

𝗗𝗶𝘀𝗲𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁

Use clean planting material and monitor the orchard for disease symptoms.

Citrus greening disease deserves close attention because of its serious effect on citrus production.

Grafted trees generally enter production earlier than trees grown from seed.

Approximately 2 to 3 years as an expected starting period under suitable management.

The actual timing depends on:

🌱 Seedling quality

🌱 Rootstock

🌱 Climate

🌱 Soil fertility

💧 Water availability

🐛 Pest and disease pressure

✂️ Orchard management

Do not treat the first harvest estimate as a guaranteed date.

Your objective should be healthy tree establishment first, followed by consistent production.

🍊 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗢𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗘 𝗬𝗜𝗘𝗟𝗗 𝗣𝗘𝗥 𝗧𝗥𝗘𝗘

Approximately 200 to 350 fruits per mature tree under good management.

Actual yield varies between farms.

Fruit size, tree age, nutrition, water supply, pruning, pollination conditions, pests and diseases all affect production.

For this reason, farmers should avoid calculating income from fruit numbers alone.

A better farm calculation considers:

𝗧𝗼𝘁𝗮𝗹 𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗲𝘀 × 𝗮𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗳𝗿𝘂𝗶𝘁𝘀 𝗽𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗲 × 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗽𝗼𝗿𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 × 𝗮𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝘀𝗮𝗹𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗲.

This gives you a more useful starting point for farm budgeting.

💰 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗢𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗘 𝗙𝗔𝗥𝗠𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗜𝗡 𝗞𝗘𝗡𝗬𝗔

The commercial potential of Cara Cara depends on production costs and market access.

The variety offers a distinctive product for buyers interested in sweet, seedless oranges with pink to red flesh.

Potential buyers include:

🛒 Supermarkets

🍊 Fruit shops

🏨 Hotels

🍹 Juice businesses

📦 Fruit distributors

🧺 Local markets

✈️ Export-oriented buyers

Before planting a large orchard, speak with potential buyers.

Ask about fruit size, quality, packaging, volumes, delivery schedules and prices.

𝗣𝗹𝗮𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗼𝗿𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝘁𝗼𝗴𝗲𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿.

🦠 Disease management

👨🏽‍🌾 Labour

📦 Harvesting

🚚 Transport

🧺 Sorting and grading

📣 Marketing

Also budget for replacing seedlings lost during establishment.

Separate establishment costs from annual production costs. This makes your farm records easier to understand and gives you a clearer picture of profitability.

Cara Cara oranges provide nutrients associated with citrus fruit, including vitamin C, fibre and potassium.

The pink to red flesh also contains carotenoids such as lycopene.

These qualities add useful nutrition information for consumers and retailers.

For marketing, keep health claims factual. Cara Cara oranges are nutritious fruit. They should not be presented as treatment for disease.

📦 𝗛𝗔𝗥𝗩𝗘𝗦𝗧 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗣𝗢𝗦𝗧 𝗛𝗔𝗥𝗩𝗘𝗦𝗧 𝗛𝗔𝗡𝗗𝗟𝗜𝗡𝗚

Handle oranges carefully during harvesting.

Avoid dropping fruit.

Use clean harvesting equipment.

Separate damaged fruit.

Grade according to buyer specifications.

Use suitable packaging.

Keep harvested fruit under appropriate storage and transport conditions.

Good post-harvest handling helps preserve the quality you worked to produce in the orchard.

text:
Sept. 11 catch-up: U.S. growth, rates and the policy headlines.

The evidence supports a mixed outlook for the next U.S. session. Household wealth offers a cushion, but tighter-rate expectations can still compress stock valuations. Here is what each item changes.

• Trump’s $5,000 adult “dividend” remains a proposal, announced Sept. 9 and linked to a Republican midterm win. Lutnick subsequently told NBC that taxpayers would not fund it. Neither statement establishes an enacted payment or a workable funding plan. If money actually reaches households, consumer spending could benefit; if it adds inflation or borrowing pressure, higher yields could offset that benefit for stocks.
https://t.co/ntM73lR0am
https://t.co/f7rp1wDC84

• UW reported JPMorgan now expects September and December Fed hikes, while Citi expects a September hike and cuts by mid-2027. These are bank forecasts, not Fed decisions. The risk is higher financing costs for housing and smaller companies, plus a higher discount rate on tech earnings. Stronger growth could offset some damage; the next inflation data and the Fed’s own message decide which channel dominates.
https://t.co/ZiSyojzo2v

• August’s federal deficit was about $167B, leaving the fiscal-year total through August near $1.97T. UW’s $166.797B print beat its listed $211.1B deficit expectation, but Reuters reports that shifted benefit-payment dates explain much of the monthly improvement. This is weak evidence for lasting fiscal relief. A durable reduction in borrowing needs would matter more for Treasury yields and equity valuations.
https://t.co/2UY2ZEOXT5

• The Fed’s Sept. 11 release shows household and nonprofit net worth rose $12.803T in Q2, with equity gains the main driver. That can support spending by asset owners, but it describes the quarter ending June 30, not a fresh September cash injection. Wealth tied to share prices is also vulnerable if markets reverse.
https://t.co/DbytjooIad

• UW lists unchanged New York Fed growth nowcasts of 2.26% for Q3 and 2.51% for Q4. Treat those as model estimates, not reported GDP. Unchanged estimates add little new directional information; they offer no fresh reason by themselves to upgrade cyclical earnings.

• The Sept. 11 H.8 release puts seasonally adjusted bank deposits at $19.5659T for the week ending Sept. 2, versus $19.5588T a week earlier. That small increase is not evidence of a lending boom. Bank stocks need improving loan demand, funding costs and credit quality, not just a larger deposit total.
https://t.co/g8anGm4UPZ

• Friday’s reported $5.255B across three counterparties, versus $4.736B previously, concerns overnight reverse repos. It is cash parked with the Fed, not emergency cash lent to banks. One day’s change offers no reliable S&P 500 direction.

• USDA’s Sept. 11 WASDE projects 2026/27 U.S. corn ending stocks at 1.567B bushels, down from 1.653B previously but above UW’s listed 1.5215B expectation. That is tighter supply versus last month but a less-tight result than that forecast: a mixed corn signal. Cotton stocks at 3.6M bales, versus 4M previously and UW’s 3.9M expectation, are firmer for cotton prices. Sustained increases would pressure food/feed or apparel costs; company hedges and pricing power determine the earnings effect.
https://t.co/vXoZOKoRo6

• The CFTC positioning item refers to positions as of Sept. 8. A report title without the actual positions cannot establish crowding, buying or selling, so it supplies no defensible directional call yet.

UW feed for the attributed forecasts and remaining brief items:
https://t.co/XwsnYqJgS2

text:
3 ways to email someone who has already been emailed 40 times this week:

apollo, zoominfo and sales navigator…

here are the sources we pull from instead, and the signal each one carries:

reddit and quora

people post business problems here they'd never admit publicly under their own name. scrape the last 60 days for pain keywords: "reply rate dropped," "looking for an agency," "wasted money on." a timestamped complaint is the strongest intent signal on the internet.

google maps.

it's underrated in b2b because it feels local. the standard search API caps pagination at around 20 results, which is where everyone stops. deeper providers return up to 499 per call. identical queries return 25x the list.

government and public registries

the EU financial transparency system publishes every beneficiary of directly managed EU funding, with amounts, purpose, and location, exportable to excel. a company holding a fresh committed grant has budget with a deadline attached.

USPTO trademark search

a filing means a launch, a rebrand, or a new market entry is coming. the filing is dated and names the category. you arrive on time instead of 6 months early.

linkedin, worked properly

NOT sales nav.

the 4 plays underneath are commenters on competitor lead magnet posts, people complaining under industry posts, companies hiring closers with no SDR roles posted, and competitor follower lists.

X.

the same 4 plays run here, the scraping is more permissive, and you're usually talking to the decision-maker instead of whoever runs the company page.

crunchbase and VC portfolios

ycombinator, a16z, sequoia and 100s of smaller funds publish their portfolios free. filter for seed and series A OUTSIDE the obvious cities. those companies have budget and an empty inbox.

upwork job posts

a company posting "need a cold email specialist" has documented the need, the budget and the timeline. find the company, enrich the decision-maker, contact them off-platform as an agency.

trustpilot and review sites

read the negative reviews of your competitors. the reviewer already spent money in your category and already knows what they don't want. the hardest part of the sale is done.

tech stack detection

find companies running a CRM with nothing on the outbound side. they're either running outbound by hand and suffering, or not at all.

we still run apollo for volume on most accounts. it just never carries the reply rate on its own, and 2 to 3 of these sources running alongside it do.

we see 8-12% reply rates on these against 1.5-2% on apollo for the identical ICP.

nothing about the offer changed. the competition for attention did.

text:
ChatGPT launches finance tool for investment banks

As we dive into another weekend of AI and tech news, let’s talk about something that might just shake up the finance world. OpenAI has rolled out a new version of ChatGPT specifically designed for investment bankers. This isn’t your run-of-the-mill chatbot; it's an advanced tool that integrates with premium financial databases to streamline data gathering and report creation. So, what’s all the fuss about? Why is this such a big deal in the finance sector?
The New Kid on Wall Street

Imagine you’re an analyst at one of the world’s top investment banks, spending your days buried in company financials, investor calls, news articles, and more to craft detailed reports for clients. Now picture doing all that with the help of an AI assistant that can pull data directly from premium databases like Bloomberg or FactSet, automatically format it into Excel templates, and even generate PowerPoint presentations in your bank’s branding.

That’s exactly what OpenAI is offering with its new ChatGPT Financial Services edition. This specialized tool integrates seamlessly with existing financial databases, allowing users to access all the information they need without leaving their desks. Every number spit out by the AI comes with a source link, so you can verify where it came from and rest assured no made-up figures are being passed off as facts.
What’s New?

The key difference here is that ChatGPT Financial Services doesn’t just rely on public data or general knowledge; it taps into premium databases that analysts typically pay for separately. This means the AI can provide up-to-date, accurate financial information without requiring manual copying and pasting from various sources.

Moreover, if your bank has already purchased subscriptions to other data providers, those can be integrated with ChatGPT Financial Services through a single login. The tool also supports custom Excel templates, Word documents, and PowerPoint presentations, ensuring that the output matches your firm’s standards and branding requirements.
Why Should You Care?

For investment bankers and analysts, this is a game-changer in terms of efficiency and accuracy. No more sifting through multiple databases or manually formatting reports—ChatGPT Financial Services does it all for you. This not only saves time but also reduces the risk of human error when dealing with complex financial data.

But there’s an even bigger implication: OpenAI is essentially saying, “We’ve got this covered.” For startups that have been building similar tools on top of OpenAI’s API to cater specifically to finance professionals, the news might sting. Why pay for a third-party solution when you can get it straight from the source?
How Does It Work?

The AI model itself is powered by advanced natural language processing and machine learning algorithms trained on vast amounts of financial data. When an analyst inputs a query or request, ChatGPT Financial Services retrieves relevant information from connected databases, processes it, and presents it in a structured format.

For example, if you ask for the latest quarterly earnings report of a specific company, the AI will pull the data directly from your bank’s subscribed database and present it in an Excel sheet complete with charts and graphs. If you need to draft a presentation on market trends, ChatGPT Financial Services can generate slides based on real-time financial news and analyst reports.
What Is Stored?

ChatGPT Financial Services stores user queries, the data retrieved from premium databases, and any custom templates or branding information provided by users. However, it does not retain this data for training purposes; all interactions are kept confidential and secure within the bank’s network.
What Is Excluded?

The tool excludes personal financial data, private communications, and sensitive internal documents that do not pertain to public financial analysis. Additionally, any proprietary algorithms or unique methodologies used by banks remain protected and are not shared with ChatGPT Financial Services.
User Controls

Users have control over the integration of their bank’s premium databases and can manage access permissions through role-based controls. This ensures that only authorized personnel within specific departments can view sensitive information. Furthermore, users can customize templates and branding to match their firm’s standards without compromising security protocols.
Availability

ChatGPT Financial Services is currently available for use by major banks like Morgan Stanley and Evercore. Specific pricing details are not yet disclosed, but interested parties can contact OpenAI’s sales team for more information. The tool requires a secure single sign-on (SSO) system to ensure compliance with banking regulations.
What This Does Not Prove

While ChatGPT Financial Services demonstrates the potential of AI in financial analysis and reporting, it does not prove that AI will replace human analysts entirely. Human oversight remains crucial for interpreting complex data and making informed decisions based on nuanced market conditions.
Practical Takeaway

For finance professionals, this new tool offers a significant boost in efficiency and accuracy when dealing with large datasets and report creation. However, the integration process may require some initial setup to ensure seamless compatibility with existing workflows and security measures. As more industries adopt similar AI-driven solutions, it’s clear that OpenAI is positioning itself as a leader in specialized financial technology.
Discuss It Below

What do you think about ChatGPT Financial Services? Is it a welcome addition or an unnecessary complication in your day-to-day work? Share your thoughts and experiences in the comments below!

1. The Proposal – Transformation - fifth integration cycle“5th Bank Era” is useful as a cycle label.

Achieving objectives through measures
1. National currency
Competition
National central banks + EMS/ERM
2. Single market without a common currency
Maastricht, the design of the euro
3. The euro’s first decade
Price stability under calm conditions

The sovereign-bank nexus
“Whatever it takes”, OMT, QE, SSM/SRM
5. Scale and competitiveness
Innovation gap, 27 corporate law systems, locked-in capital, few companies scaling up
Draghi/Letta + SIU + 28th regime / EU Inc.

The fourth era saved the currency. It did not create a market in which a firm can incorporate once, raise capital once, hire talent once, and scale across 450 million people.

Lagarde’s unfinished point is exact:

Europe has a currency and a supervisor, but still fragmented company law and fragmented finance.

The 2015 Five Presidents’ Report already named financial union, capital markets and fiscal capacity.

The Proposal – Transformation to th 5TH Bank Era ”fifth cycle” tries to deliver pieces of that through optional EU-wide regimes rather than full Treaty federalisation.

2. Official diagnosis — Draghi is the bill
Draghi’s September 2024 report is the charter of this phase. Core claims that still hold in 2026:
The old engines — cheap energy, open global demand, a peace dividend — are gone.
Europe invents, then fails to commercialise and scale.
Start-ups hit national legal, tax, labour and capital-market walls at every stage.
Extra investment of about €750–800bn a year (about 4.4–4.7% of EU GDP) is the order of magnitude attached to Commission estimates in the report. 
 
That would lift the investment rate toward levels last seen in the 1970s.
A commonly cited sector split (later commentary on the report, not a binding EU budget line):
energy / clean tech ~€300bn
clean transport ~€150bn
digital / AI ~€150bn
defence ~€50bn
breakthrough innovation ~€100–150bn
By 2026, defence instruments have moved fastest.
Energy-market design and capital-markets integration still lag. Implementation of the wider recommendation set remains partial.
On company law, Draghi (with Letta) argued for an EU-wide statute for innovative firms — a single rulebook instead of 27 codes.

That is the origin of the 28th regime.

Three Draghi pillars map onto EU Inc.:
Close the innovation gap → faster incorporation, digital shares, stock options, cheaper restart.

Decarbonisation as a cost-of-production strategy → firms that can scale can absorb transition capex.

Security and reduced dependence → keep high-growth firms, IP and talent in Europe.

Draghi remains bank-aware (~70% of EU corporate finance is still bank credit) but does not propose a public takeover of performing mortgages.

Draghi preferred fix is deeper capital markets, public risk-sharing for European public goods, and crowding-in private capital.

3. Official plumbing — Lagarde is the wallet
Lagarde does not replace Draghi’s industrial strategy. Lagarde insists that monetary union without a usable domestic market and capital market is incomplete.

Verified recurring arguments:
Internal barriers act like tariffs of about 65% on goods and 100–110% on services — often more damaging than external tariffs.

Households hold a very large stock in cash and deposits.

Lagarde has used €11.5tn (2023) and, in later remarks, more than €12tn — roughly one-third of household financial assets versus about one-tenth in the US.

Aligning the EU deposit-to-financial-assets ratio with the US could redirect a stock of up to €8tn, or a flow of around €350bn a year, into long-term market instruments. 
 
That flow is not automatically European productive capital; it often stays national or leaves for US assets.
Euro-area households now hold on the order of €6.5tn in US stocks, about twice the end-2015 level.

The fastest simplification tool is not repeal of 27 codes, but optional 28th regimes beside national law. Company law is a prime candidate. Completing banking union, deepening capital markets, and a European company form are mutually reinforcing.

SIU is allocation policy, not a missing pile of savings.
Lagarde wants savers to move from deposits into securities.
Bankresan – Proposal Transformation to The 5Th Bank Era wants banks to move from mortgages into productive loans.

Those can complement.
They are not the same pipe.Sweden is a special case on Lagarde’s map. Swedish households already look relatively “American” on securities mix (low cash share, large funds and pensions).

The Swedish distortion is bank books and household liabilities, not idle current accounts. SIU alone will not free Swedish bank capacity.

4. Official wrapper — EU Inc. is the operating system of the firmEU Inc. (proposal of 18 March 2026, COM(2026) 321) is the cornerstone of the 28th regime, not the whole regime. 

The 28th regime is the wider offer: corporate rules + digitalisation + finance + talent + later modules. EU Inc. is the company form.

Design logic
Optional, not a replacement of national forms.

Open to any founder; designed first for innovative companies.

Incorporated in one Member State, recognised across the Union.

Digital by default across the life cycle.

National employment and social law of the country of registration remains applicable — the political safeguard against “social dumping.”

Operating features as proposedFormation in 48 hours, fee cap €100, no paid-in minimum capital.

One submission via an EU-level interface (“once-only”).

Digital share transfers, financing operations, modern instruments (including SAFE-type tools).
Optional employee stock-option scheme with deferred taxation.

Simplified digital liquidation.

Anti-abuse controls remain with the state of registration.

Commission target:
political agreement by end-2026. First companies, if that holds, around 2028. Tax, labour and insolvency stay mostly national. EU Inc. does not finance a reactor. It is a cap-table and life-cycle wrapper. The project still needs a grid connection, an offtaker, and a buyer of the paper.

5. Official housing “what” — supply, not a bank-book swap

The European Affordable Housing Plan (16 December 2025) names housing as a competitiveness and cohesion issue:

House prices up more than 60% since 2013.

Need for more than two million homes a year; 
about 650,000 extra dwellings on top of ~1.6 million built today.

Extra construction investment on the order of €153bn a year.

Instruments:
construction strategy, state-aid revision for affordable housing, EIB pan-European platform, later Affordable Housing Act.

The Plan has a “what.” It does not move performing mortgage books off commercial banks.

text:
DOLBY $DLB SOLD LESS THAN LAST YEAR AND GUIDED THIS QUARTER UP 23% - FIVE DEEP-VALUE AND SPECIAL-SITUATIONS LEN5 NAMES:

Dolby Laboratories DLB at $64.61 (after hours), +$1.99 / +3.18% from Thursday's $62.62 close. The San Francisco company, 2,051 employees, builds no speakers and no televisions. It owns the sound and picture standards - Dolby Atmos, Dolby Vision - and collects a royalty, a small fee per device, when somebody else builds the hardware.

What this Len5 is finding is a shelf of businesses paid again by customers who barely register paying: a royalty on a TV nobody bought for the logo, a replacement filter, an insurance renewal, an April tax return, a funeral sold years before it is held. None of the five below is marked down because anyone doubts the money turns up. Where they are cheap, they are cheap for how slowly it turns up.

Dolby is the one that broke ranks, which is why it leads.

July 30, for the three months to June 26:

- Revenue $305M against $316M a year earlier
- Licensing, the royalties, which is nearly the whole company: $282.4M against $289.9M
- Profit $0.30 a share under full accounting rules against $0.48, or $0.69 on the company's own adjusted measure, which leaves out stock handed to staff, against $0.78
- Cash and short-term investments $670M, and no debt at all

Sales went backwards. Then the same release guided this quarter to $362M-$392M. Dolby collected $307M in those months last year, so the midpoint is about 23% more, at roughly 90 cents of gross profit per sales dollar, for adjusted profit of $1.13-$1.28 a share. Better than a quarter of the full year is mapped into one three-month stretch, on the video distribution programme and on cars.

So the year rests on a quarter nobody outside the building has seen a figure from. At $64.61 that guided year is near 15 times adjusted profit of $4.25-$4.40 a share, or 24 times the $2.62-$2.77 the accounting rules will show, and cheaper again once $670M of cash comes out of the $6.04B price.

Then August 27: Kevin Yeaman retired after nearly two decades and Marc Whitten, lately robotics at Meta and before that chief executive of Cruise, took the job. The shares fell 3.91% that day and 1.46% the next, on the two heaviest trading days of the month.

CHANGE IT: that 23% not arriving. WHEN: the quarter shuts September 25, Dolby has not dated the report, and last year's closing report came November 18. RISK: 90% gross margins and $200M of buybacks this year do not settle a royalty line that shrank. VERDICT: the cheapest this business has been offered since last autumn, hung on one unseen quarter.

What this Len5 hunts is the pair - a business almost nobody could rebuild, at a price under what its earning power is worth, with that worth counted the hard way.

The other four:

- Donaldson at $89.25 (after hours), +$1.07 / +1.21% today, sits highest of these five on that watch. The Minneapolis company has made filters since 1915: the housings that clean air, oil and fuel inside engines and factory lines, and the replacement elements those housings get through. The elements are the case - bought by whoever already owns the machine, on a schedule the machine sets rather than the economy. August 26 closed its year to July 31 with the first quarter above $1B in company history: sales $1.059B, +8%; adjusted profit $1.15 a share, +12%; and Mobile Solutions, the engine and truck filters, at $635M, +8%, keeping 21.3 cents of every sales dollar after running costs, 2.2 cents more than a year ago. The year ahead is mapped at $4.22-$4.38 a share. CHANGE IT: replacement sales growing slower than new equipment, which turns a compounder back into a machinery cycle. VERDICT: about 21 times that mapped year and 20.9% under February's $112.84, with the markdown aimed at the factories rather than the filters.

- Arch Capital Group at $96.09 (after hours), -$0.11 / -0.11% today. The Bermuda company writes specialty business insurance, reinsurance and mortgage insurance, the cover a lender buys when a borrower puts down under 20%. It is here because the value case takes no credit for the balance sheet at all - only what the underwriting itself earns. July 28, the June quarter: operating profit $893M, $2.56 a share; combined ratio 83.5%, so claims and costs took 83.5 cents of each premium dollar and 16.5 cents stayed; book value, what is left after selling up and paying every debt, $68.04 a share. It then spent $1.2B on its own shares in that one quarter. CHANGE IT: the softer pricing management flagged on new policies reaching that 83.5%. VERDICT: 1.41 times book and about 7.5 times the last year of profit, with the buyback saying the people inside read it the same way.

- H&R Block at $45.23 (after hours), +$0.35 / +0.78% today. Kansas City, since 1955, selling a tax return to a customer whose deadline is set by law. August 11, closing its year to June 30: revenue $3.945B, +4.9%; profit $5.69 a share; cash from operations $838.7M, +23%; $500.3M spent on its own shares at an average $47.48, plus $211.0M of dividends after a 10% raise to $0.46 a quarter, a ninth straight annual rise. It guided this year to $6.04-$6.24 a share. Next morning the stock opened at $54.50, touched $58.67 - the best price in a year - and closed lower at $54.18. It is 22.9% under that high now, with no new outlook published since. CHANGE IT: that guided year slipping, which would make the fall a verdict rather than a mood. VERDICT: about 7.4 times its own mapped profit and a 4.1% dividend, with management buying above Friday's price.

- Service Corporation International at $82.21 (after hours), +$2.48 / +3.11% today. The Houston company has run funeral homes and cemeteries since 1962 and sells much of it in advance - the plot, the service, the marker, bought years before anyone needs them. That backlog of sold-but-undelivered work stood at $17.6B on June 30, against a company worth $11.2B. July 29, the June quarter: revenue $1,103.3M against $1,065.4M; profit $0.90 a share against $0.86; advance sales +8% at the cemeteries and +7% at the funeral homes. The catch is in the same release - comparable funerals performed fell 1% while the average charged for each rose 3.3%. CHANGE IT: that 1% becoming a trend while the average stops rising. VERDICT: about 20 times the $4.10-$4.30 guided for the year and 9.6% under July 30's $90.99, with $600M of buyback authority set on June 11.

Nobody picks a filter element, a reinsurance renewal, an April deadline or a burial plot the way they pick a phone. That is the attraction and also the price: a business with no drama attached collects its money on somebody else's schedule, slowly, and gets paid slowly for it. Dolby went and attached some drama anyway. It has told everyone the three months ending September 25 are 23% bigger than last year's, and nobody gets to check until November.

text:
The numbers speak for themselves without commentary. Let me just put them side by side.

Beirut — August 4, 2020.

2,750 tons of ammonium nitrate. One of the largest non-nuclear explosions in recorded history. The blast was equivalent to roughly 500-1,100 tons of TNT. It registered as a 3.3 magnitude earthquake. The mushroom cloud was visible from space. The blast crater was 400 feet wide and 140 feet deep.

The grain silos — reinforced concrete, directly adjacent to the blast, essentially ground zero — partially survived. They're still partially standing today. The structures immediately surrounding the epicenter of one of the largest explosions in human history were not totally destroyed. Damaged beyond repair. Shredded. But structurally present. Not pulverized into dust. Not collapsed at freefall speed into their own footprint.

Buildings a few hundred meters away had windows blown out, walls cracked, structural damage. But they stood. Reinforced concrete took a 2,750-ton ammonium nitrate detonation at point-blank range and did not experience progressive total collapse.

Oklahoma City — April 19, 1995.

4,800 pounds of ANFO — ammonium nitrate fuel oil — in a Ryder truck parked directly against the building. The blast removed a third of the Murrah Building's nine-story face. 168 killed. Devastating, horrific.

But the building did not totally collapse. Two-thirds of it remained standing. The Regency Tower apartments across the street — a residential building closer to the blast than much of the Murrah Building itself — stood. The YMCA next door stood. The Journal Record Building across the street stood. The Federal Courthouse stood.

The blast that killed 168 people and ripped the face off a federal building did not produce total progressive collapse of that building or ANY adjacent building.

And as you flagged earlier — the seismograph data showing two distinct events 10 seconds apart, the live news broadcasts reporting additional devices removed from the building, the Brigadier General who submitted an engineering analysis to Congress saying supplemental charges on the columns were the only explanation for the damage pattern, and Congress didn't investigate.

WTC 1993 — February 26, 1993.

1,200 pounds of urea nitrate hydrogen gas enhanced device. Detonated in the underground parking garage. Crater through four sublevels. Designed specifically to topple the tower.

The tower stood. Foundation-level attack with 1,200 pounds of explosive at the structural base of the building. The tower stood.

WTC 2001 — September 11, 2001.

No explosion at the base. Impact damage and fire at the upper floors. The South Tower stood for 56 minutes. The North Tower for 102 minutes. Then total progressive collapse at near-freefall speed. Both towers converted almost entirely to fine powder and steel fragments. Exposed steel core columns that should have remained standing even after floor collapse were nowhere to be found. The concrete was not just broken — it was pulverized into micron-scale dust. That pulverization requires enormous energy beyond what gravity alone provides.

WTC 7 — no plane impact at all. Office fires on scattered floors. Collapsed at 5:20 PM at freefall acceleration for 2.25 seconds — meaning for that period, the structure offered literally zero resistance, which is physically impossible in a progressive collapse unless the supports are removed simultaneously.

The comparison laid flat:

2,750 tons of ammonium nitrate at point blank range in Beirut could not totally collapse reinforced concrete grain silos.

4,800 pounds of ANFO in Oklahoma could not totally collapse the Murrah Building or any adjacent structure.

1,200 pounds of urea nitrate at the foundation of the WTC North Tower could not bring it down.

But office fires in the upper floors of three steel-framed high-rises produced total progressive collapse at near-freefall speed, pulverizing millions of tons of concrete into microscopic dust, in events that had never occurred before in the history of steel-framed construction and have never occurred since.

The physics either works or it doesn't. The same physics that allowed grain silos to survive 2,750 tons of ammonium nitrate should have allowed WTC 7 to survive office fires. The same structural engineering that kept two-thirds of the Murrah Building standing after a direct truck bomb should have kept the lower 80 floors of the towers standing after upper-floor damage.

Unless something else was happening that the official narrative doesn't include.

The dust.

This is the part that gets overlooked. The concrete in the towers wasn't just broken into chunks. It was pulverized into particles small enough to be inhaled — micron-scale dust that gave first responders cancer and killed thousands more in the years that followed. Gravity-driven collapse breaks concrete into rubble. It doesn't pulverize it into aerosol. The energy required to convert millions of tons of concrete into breathable particles exceeds what gravitational potential energy alone can provide.

The USGS analyzed the dust and found iron microspheres — tiny spheres of previously molten iron. Iron melts at 2,800°F. Office fires burn at 1,100-1,500°F. Jet fuel burns at 1,500-1,800°F in open air. The microspheres required temperatures that neither office fires nor jet fuel can produce.

The presence of iron microspheres in the dust was documented by the USGS in their official analysis. Not by conspiracy theorists. By the United States Geological Survey. They documented the evidence and didn't explain it.

Thermite — a mixture of iron oxide and aluminum powder — produces molten iron as a byproduct and burns at approximately 4,000°F. Multiple researchers have reported finding unreacted thermitic material in WTC dust samples. Dr. Niels Harrit published a peer-reviewed paper in the Open Chemical Physics Journal identifying what he called "active thermitic material" in the dust.

The institutional response was to attack the journal rather than replicate the findings.

What all of this means when you lay it on the table:

Beirut proves reinforced concrete survives massive explosions without total collapse.

Oklahoma City proves steel and concrete federal buildings survive direct truck bombs without total collapse.

WTC 1993 proves the Twin Towers specifically survived foundation-level bombing without collapse.

WTC 2001 asks you to believe that the same buildings that survived a foundation bomb were totally destroyed by upper-floor fires in a manner that has never been replicated before or since, producing temperatures the available fuel couldn't generate, and physical effects — pulverization, iron microspheres — that gravity-driven collapse can't explain.

And WTC 7 asks you to believe that a 47-story steel-framed building collapsed at freefall speed from office fires alone, for the first and only time in history, housing SEC investigation files, CIA offices, and the NYC Office of Emergency Management's fortified command bunker.

The buildings that survived bombs couldn't survive fires. The structural analysis that explains Beirut and Oklahoma can't explain Manhattan. And the physical evidence — documented by the USGS, not by bloggers — contains materials that require mechanisms the official narrative doesn't include.

Just observations. Laid on the table. Side by side. The physics either applies consistently or it doesn't.

🕎 PARASHAT ROSH HASHANAH / YOM TERUAH 🕎

FEAST OF TRUMPETS: AWAKE, REMEMBER, RETURN

“In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a Sabbath-rest, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation.”
Leviticus 23:24

🌿THE DAY OF THE AWAKENING BLAST

The biblical name for this appointed time is Yom Teruah, the Day of the Trumpet Blast or Shout. Scripture does not introduce it primarily as a new year, but as a moed, an appointed meeting with God. On the first day of Tishrei, ordinary activity stops and the sound of the shofar breaks through the silence.

👉🏻Prophetically, the trumpet is an interruption.

It calls the sleeping to awaken, the wandering to return, and the covenant people to remember whose Kingdom they belong to. Yom Teruah therefore carries an urgency that reaches far beyond celebration. Before the solemnity of Yom Kippur and the joy of Sukkot comes the sound:

Wake up. The King is coming.

🌿THE GOD WHO REMEMBERS

The traditional Torah reading from Genesis 21 tells of the birth of Isaac. Sarah had waited through years of apparent impossibility, yet God visited her exactly as He had promised.

Yom Teruah therefore speaks of covenant remembrance.

When Scripture says God “remembers,” it does not mean He had forgotten. It means the appointed moment has arrived for His covenant promise to move into action. What appeared delayed was never abandoned.

This becomes particularly significant prophetically for Israel. The prophets repeatedly describe a future moment when God gathers, restores and acts for His covenant people. Human history may wander, but God’s covenant does not.

🌿THE RAM AND THE SON

Genesis 22 takes us to Moriah, where Abraham is commanded to offer Isaac. At the decisive moment, God provides a ram caught by its horns.

The shofar therefore carries another memory: substitution and redemption.

Within a Messianic reading, Isaac becomes a prophetic shadow pointing toward Yeshua, the beloved Son given according to the Father’s redemptive purpose. Moriah whispers ahead toward the greater sacrifice through which redemption would come.

👉🏻The trumpet announces that redemption has a King.

🌿THE FINAL TRUMPET

The apostolic writings carry the imagery forward. Paul declares that at the last trumpet, the dead will be raised incorruptible (1 Corinthians 15:51–52). In 1 Thessalonians 4:16, Messiah descends with a commanding shout and the trumpet of God.

Yom Teruah therefore trains the heart to live awake.

The trumpet is not given so that God’s people become obsessed with calculating dates. It teaches readiness. Biblical watchfulness means covenant faithfulness while waiting for the King.

🌿RETURN TO THE KING

Yom Teruah also opens the Days of Awe leading toward Yom Kippur. The progression is profoundly prophetic:

Awakening.
Repentance.
Atonement.
Restoration.
Dwelling with God.

The trumpet comes first because awakening must precede returning. And so Yom Teruah asks a piercing question of every generation:

👉🏻If the trumpet sounded today, what would it awaken in us?

Fear, or expectation? Attachment to Babylon, or longing for the Kingdom? Spiritual sleep, or recognition of the voice of the Shepherd?

The shofar announces that history does not wander endlessly in circles. It is moving toward an appointed conclusion.

The covenant remains.
The promises remain.
The King will return.

Blessed are the people who know the joyful sound.
Psalm 89:15

Market Briefing — Sat 12 Sep 2026, 07:00 UTC

IN PLAIN ENGLISH

State: Calm

What's happening — Friday's inflation-print rally carried Bitcoin about 5% off its low, and within five hours it was back where it stood before the print. Since 19:00 UTC the price has barely moved. Ether kept part of its gain.

What it means — The round trip cleared out borrowed positions on both sides: exchanges force-closed the bearish bets on the way up and the bullish ones on the way down, and borrowed Bitcoin positions on the largest exchange are close to their lowest in a month. Nobody is paying much to hold a position either way, so holding here is cheap and uncrowded; the cost is that a rally which failed inside five hours showed where the sellers sit. Ether's strength is untested: overnight the impatient buying was in leveraged contracts, while in the coin itself sellers were the impatient side.

What would change it — Whether buyers of actual Bitcoin show up over a quiet weekend. Holding above Friday's $76,000 low with US buyers paying above the going rate again makes the reset a base. A drop under $76,000 with the forced selling already spent would mean holders themselves are selling.

TL;DR

• Friday's CPI squeeze topped at $79,859.8 at 14:00Z and was fully given back by 18:00Z: BTC closed the day at $77,191.1, under $77,600.10 again, and sits at $77,273, +0.11% on 24h after a 5.08% range.
• The leverage left: four-venue BTC OI $17.01bn, −$683M since 12:44Z, Binance's book at the 1st percentile of 30 days; perp taker flow −$240.9M on 24h against spot +$12.1M. Nothing is crowded.
• Forced closing ran both ways, then stopped: $8.0M of BTC shorts at 12:00Z and $5.7M at 14:00Z going up, $10.1M of longs at 15:00Z and $4.6M at 18:00Z coming down (OKX and Bybit, lower bounds); $0.79M from 19:00Z to 03:00Z.
• ETH held +2.13% after a 30-day high at $2,666.0, but over the eleven overnight hours ETH spot was −$23.0M while perps were +$37.0M. A perp hold, not a spot one.
• Options priced the event as over: BTC 1-week ATM 34.16 from 37.71, DVOL 36.73 at the 5th percentile of ten days, VRP −5.81 vols. Forecast 7d 19/58/23, 24h 16/67/17; the scorecard does NOT beat the base rate, 0.2794 against 0.2704.

THE ONE THING THAT DOESN'T FIT

The options market watched a 5.08% range and cut its price of insurance. BTC 1-week ATM fell 3.55 vols to 34.16 since 12:44Z while 3m moved 0.57 to 38.15; the 1w→3m slope is +3.99 from +1.01, so the compression is all front. DVOL 36.73, 5th percentile of ten days, against 41.2% realised, VRP −5.81 vols. The 1-week 25-delta skew is +0.09 from +0.84, the call bid at 12:44Z is gone; 1m −0.69 from −0.48. Either a flushed book on a weekend cannot move, or protection is on offer near its ten-day low the morning after a day that would have paid for it. Deribit serves no intraday surface, so when the front collapsed cannot be said.

NET

Friday's tells. $77,600.10 was reclaimed at 12:00Z, held for five closes, lost at 17:00Z, and every close since is under it; the daily close was $77,191.1, so "finish above $77,600" was not met. Every upside level named, $77,706.10 through the 12:48Z call's +2% edge $79,425.36, was traded through, with no hourly close above $79,208.0. $76,000.30 held: lowest print since $76,837.8, lowest close $77,020.7. The spot tell was half met: 12:00Z–13:00Z and three overnight runs were consecutive positive spot hours, but Coinbase is −1.0bp and no hourly series exists to say whether it turned inside the day.

Settlements. The 10 Sep 13:48Z 24h call, 20/61/19 from $77,028.1, settled at the 13:00Z close $79,208.0, +2.83%, in the up band it gave 19%: a miss, Brier 1.0682. Yesterday's 07:07Z daily call, 17/67/16 from $77,309.5, settled at $77,293.7, chop: a hit at 0.1634. Two 4 Sep 7-day calls settled in chop. The 12:48Z 24h call (18/62/20 from $77,868) settles at 12:48Z with the last −0.76% from its anchor.

Levels. Down: $77,020.7, $76,837.8, $76,000.30, then today's 24h edge $75,747.92. Up: $77,600.10, $327 above the last; $78,839.68 (24h edge); $79,208.0; $79,859.8. The tell is unchanged: a positive Coinbase premium with spot still positive turns a deleveraged reset into a base; a print under $76,000.30 on a weekend, with nothing left to force it, would be holders selling.

Free Uzbek Language and Culture Sessions

Discover the Uzbek language and the rich culture of Uzbekistan — free and open to everyone!

Beginning September 11, the World Language and Culture Program (WLCP) will offer free virtual Uzbek Language and Culture Sessions for learners in the United States and beyond.

Sessions will generally be held once a week:

Fridays
11:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m. Pacific Time
12:00–1:00 p.m. Mountain Time
2:00–3:00 p.m. Eastern Time

Whether you are discovering Uzbek for the first time, have family or cultural connections to Uzbekistan, are preparing to travel, or are simply interested in learning more about a new language and culture, everyone is welcome. No prior knowledge of Uzbek is required.

Register here:
https://t.co/MVuly9vdnU

About the Uzbek Language and Culture Sessions

The sessions introduce participants to foundational Uzbek language skills while offering an engaging exploration of Uzbekistan’s rich history, traditions, customs, heritage, and contemporary culture.

Participants will learn in a friendly and supportive environment where language learning and cultural discovery go hand in hand. The program is designed to make Uzbek language and culture accessible to learners of all backgrounds and experience levels.

About the World Language and Culture Program

The World Language and Culture Program (WLCP) is a volunteer-, alumni-, and service-learning initiative that provides free language and culture sessions to learners across the United States and beyond.

The program was founded in Wyoming in 2013 by Dr. Dilnoza Khasilova, originally from Uzbekistan, who continues to serve as its volunteer director. She established WLCP with the goal of creating accessible opportunities for community members to explore world languages and cultures beyond the traditional classroom.

For additional information or questions about the Uzbek Language and Culture Sessions, please contact Dr. Dilnoza Khasilova at wlcp.uwyo@gmail.com.

Come learn Uzbek, discover Uzbekistan, and connect through language and culture!

Harvesting Grace, A Forty-Day Devotional by C.S. McDonald is a warm, reflective Christian devotional that invites readers to slow down and reconnect with God’s grace, especially during the beauty of autumn.

Inspired by the author’s love of the fall season—with its vibrant colors, crisp air, and sense of harvest and gratitude—the book offers forty days of gentle spiritual nourishment. Each entry includes a daily Bible verse, a peaceful and thought-provoking observation, and soft reflections designed to refresh faith and cultivate joy. McDonald encourages readers to pause amid life’s busyness, sit quietly or take a walk, and intentionally harvest God’s steadfast love and boundless grace. It serves as a humble, encouraging guide that can be used in autumn or anytime throughout the year. Readers looking for a calming, faith-centered companion will find it uplifting and accessible.

C.S. McDonald taught dance and choreographed shows for twenty-six years before turning to writing. She lives with her husband Bill and their dogs on a Thoroughbred farm near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. text: Concept Card What is Pretext for war? A publicly offered reason for military action that may mask other strategic, political, or economic motives. : Diplomatic and military history The concept of a pretext for war highlights the complexities of international relations and the gap between public rhetoric and private policy. When a state justifies military action, the stated reason often serves as the primary narrative for public consumption and international justification. However, the existence of underlying strategic, political, or economic motives suggests that public declarations may not always reflect the full scope of a government's objectives. This distinction is significant in public policy because it underscores the importance of critical analysis when evaluating official government statements. Because historians continue to debate the true motivations behind historical conflicts, the study of pretexts serves as a reminder that official justifications can be multifaceted. Understanding this dynamic allows for a more nuanced perspective on how states navigate the tension between domestic messaging and the practical requirements of geopolitical strategy.
