text:
I’m 26, single, and living alone in a mini-flat that costs ₦400,000 a year in Ipaja.

Last year, I interviewed for a Content Lead role in Ikoyi with a salary of ₦300,000 per month. After four rounds of interviews, HR said during the final chat:

“You’re our pick. You can resume on December 4.”

That same week, I resigned from my ₦160,000 job and even bought a new blazer for the role.

Then on December 1, I got a message:

“Hi, we’ve paused hiring till Q2. Apologies.”

Just like that.

No job.

My rent was due on January 2, and I had only ₦62,000 saved.

I kept applying nonstop. Four interviews a week. All virtual. All draining data.

One HR team disappeared after I spent two hours completing their unpaid test project.

Another said:

“You’re great, but we need someone with agency experience.”

The funny thing? The job advert clearly said entry-level.

What broke me wasn’t the money. It was the silence.

I’d wake up every morning, send 10 applications, then sit in my room until nightfall.

My phone became my enemy.

Every notification made my heart jump, then immediately drop when I realised it was just MTN.

I stopped replying to friends because even a simple “What are you doing now?” started to feel like judgment.

Christmas came.

I told everyone I was working from home.

On December 25, I ate Indomie and eggs alone while watching people post family photos and Christmas celebrations online.

I wasn’t hungry. I just felt invisible.

I started doubting everything. Am I not good enough? Do I perform badly in interviews? Am I missing something everyone else can see?

Rejection slowly became part of my daily routine.

Then on January 3, an old freelance client sent me a DM:

“You still write? I need someone. ₦250,000 per month. A colleague of mine also needs your services. I’ve already recommended you, but I wanted to confirm you’re available first.”

No interview.

No assessment.

No five-stage recruitment process.

Just one message.

And just like that, my life started moving again.

Looking back now, job hunting as a single lady in Lagos wasn’t just about rejection emails.

It was calculating whether you could afford to stay safe while broke.

It was wondering how long your savings would last.

It was watching your confidence disappear one rejection at a time.

Nobody sends you a message saying, “You’re still smart” after the twentieth rejection email.

You have to somehow convince yourself to keep going when you’re no longer sure what you’re fighting for.

The biggest lessons?

Never resign because of a verbal offer.

Never leave a job without a signed contract and a clear resumption plan.

Keep building relationships because opportunities often come from people who already know your work.

And please, have an emergency fund.

Even a small one can save you from making desperate decisions when life suddenly changes.

I’m okay now.

But I don’t wish that kind of quiet loneliness on anyone.

What's your toughest job-hunting experience? 

Let's hear it, please 🤲🏾

Old Flame (Gambler's Folly Book 4) by Mellie Miller is a heartfelt second-chance paranormal shifter romance that blends emotional healing, mature love, and the magic of fate. Billionaire and bear shifter Kort Behrens has been lucky in business but unlucky in love—after two failed marriages and a string of gold diggers, he’s given up hope of finding a real connection. Elizabeth Murphy, a widow for four years, has rebuilt her life through her Reiki practice and the quiet companionship of her cat, Puzzle, still carrying the quiet ache of a long marriage that never fully satisfied her deeper desires. When these old college friends (who never dated) unexpectedly reunite on the way to the enchanted world of Gambler’s Folly, sparks fly and a full-blown romance blooms. Will they seize this second chance at a happily-ever-after, or will doubts and fears snatch it away? On Gambler’s Folly, every love story is a gamble—and Fate always deals the final hand. A slow-burn friends-to-lovers tale full of heart, sensuality, and the series’ signature fantasy charm.

About the author
Mellie Miller first fell in love with writing in a high school creative writing class. Married to her one and only, Steve, they began their journey through life in 1976 and, after two children and many moves, she finally has the time to devote to this love. She mainly writes fantasy romance, often with a paranormal twist, though she also has a short book sharing her struggle with breast cancer. Mellie feels her background in music, martial arts (2nd-degree black belt), and Reiki gives her a broad palette to draw on for her character development. Many of her stories incorporate one or more of these talents. As a lover of fantasy, Mellie hopes the worlds and stories she creates will give others a bit of escape from the hectic world around us and offer hope for a happy outcome. She and her husband live in rural Georgia and share their lives with cats, dogs, and a flock of chickens. She also writes under the pen name Sultonna Nadine.

text:
This UK Kitten May Be the First Recorded Cat With No Reproductive Organs

Everyone should meet Beans, the little kitten who has quite literally gone and broken the whole binary. This special one was actually born without any sixual organs at all, meaning it is neither strictly male nor female. Originally named Hope, the tabby-and-white kitten arrived at a Cats Protection centre in Warrington at fifteen weeks old, part of a sadly abandoned litter.

The centre staff had initially all just assumed that the young kitten was female, right up until the vet exam actually happened. It turned out there were simply no external genitals at all to be found on the kitten anywhere. There were also no internal reproductive organs there either, with vets performing careful exploratory checks only to find absolutely nothing at all inside.

Fiona Brockbank, then a senior field veterinary officer with Cats Protection, called the very rare condition sixual organ agenesis. It essentially means the complete failure of those particular organs to properly develop during the early embryonic growth stage. Hermaphrodite cats with both sets are already rare, but a cat with neither was unheard of, and her team found zero documented cases at all.

The very best part of it, though, is that Beans was otherwise a perfectly healthy, playful little kitten. The cat could go about completely normally and remained full of pure energy, so vets soon offered a strong prognosis for a long life. Adoption interest then poured in from across the UK and even distant California, before Beans found a forever home with a student named Jessi Bennett.

15. Science is a means to economics, and the order cannot be reversed. Printing a rocket is science. Producing rockets faster is economics, and it is the point. Great science that is not economic is research, and research is not a venture asset. Put the economics before the science, he says, and you end up understanding neither.

16. Learning is the sourcing strategy. Access is temporary; a good founder will meet ten investors, not one. What survives is understanding the risk better than the other nine. Watch how that compounds: Speciale started in electric vehicles, which taught them storage, which taught them lithium, which sent them to hydrogen for trucks and ships, then to sodium-ion and zinc-air for energy held over time — and now to generation, because nuclear has opened to private companies. “Access is a short-term advantage.”

17. Capital is more intellectual than speculative. On the AI build-out he pushed back on the framing rather than the question. Capital mostly understands what it is doing; it only looks speculative when everyone crowds the same trade and game theory takes over. The risk is not that AI is unproductive. It is that five players spending trillions to win the same race can make a good technology into a bad business. Which is not a technology question at all.

18. Run a different race. He does not want India chasing general intelligence, because arriving second at someone else’s race is a plan to finish second. Build small models that are excellent at one domain: aerospace, defence, automotive, drug discovery. “Why do I need general intelligence? I am the general intelligence. I need specific intelligence.” A model that speeds up drug discovery does not need to be good at poetry.

And the one to leave with. Asked what someone in a completely different field should steal from his, he did not offer a framework. “You just have to assume you don’t know anything and be willing to learn.” Then, unprompted: he is not an engineer. He studied commerce and economics. He has come a long way toward appreciating technology without ever practising it, and thinks the distance is available to anyone who bothers to walk it.

Most retellings reduce the Sirens to beautiful voices that no sailor can resist. Homer gives us something more disturbing. When Odysseus' ship comes within hearing distance, the Sirens do not simply begin singing into the air. They address him directly by name before he has spoken to them: "Odysseus…"

Then they attach two highly charged titles to that name. They call him polyainos, "much praised" or "much sung of" and mega kudos Achaiōn, "great glory of the Achaeans."

Those expressions matter because they point backward toward the world of the Iliad. Polyainos is used of Odysseus in the Iliad and appears only here in the Odyssey. The second title also belongs strongly to the heroic vocabulary of Troy. Scholars have therefore argued that the Sirens are not simply flattering Odysseus. They are summoning an earlier version of him, the celebrated warrior whose fame was made at Troy.

Then they sharpen the temptation. They tell him that they know everything the Greeks and Trojans suffered at Troy and that they know what happens across the earth. Whoever listens, they promise, leaves knowing more than before.

Seen this way, the Sirens do not merely offer beautiful music. They offer Odysseus a song about the world that made him famous. They know his name. They know his war. They know the identity he built there and they promise access to knowledge no ordinary mortal possesses. That may help explain why the scene becomes so psychologically precise.

Odysseus' crew cannot hear any of this because their ears are sealed with wax. Only Odysseus is exposed to the message. When he signals for them to release him, they do not listen to his new command. They follow the one he gave before hearing the song and tighten the ropes instead. 

The mast therefore protects him from more than a beautiful voice. It protects him from a temptation designed around who he already believes himself to be. We cannot prove that Homer imagined the Sirens composing a different song for every passing sailor. The poem never tells us that.

But the one song Homer allows us to hear is unmistakably specific to Odysseus. That makes the Sirens far more interesting than the later image of seductive monsters singing indiscriminately from the rocks. Their weapon is not simply song. It is recognition.

Our Sirens Case File explores this deeper psychological structure and why Odysseus survives in a completely different way from his crew.

Harvesting Grace, A Forty-Day Devotional by C.S. McDonald is a warm, reflective Christian devotional that invites readers to slow down and reconnect with God’s grace, especially during the beauty of autumn.

Inspired by the author’s love of the fall season—with its vibrant colors, crisp air, and sense of harvest and gratitude—the book offers forty days of gentle spiritual nourishment. Each entry includes a daily Bible verse, a peaceful and thought-provoking observation, and soft reflections designed to refresh faith and cultivate joy. McDonald encourages readers to pause amid life’s busyness, sit quietly or take a walk, and intentionally harvest God’s steadfast love and boundless grace. It serves as a humble, encouraging guide that can be used in autumn or anytime throughout the year. Readers looking for a calming, faith-centered companion will find it uplifting and accessible.

Buy links

- Also check Amazon and other retailers for paperback or additional formats as they become available.

About the author
C.S. McDonald taught dance and choreographed shows for twenty-six years before turning to writing. She lives with her husband Bill and their dogs on a Thoroughbred farm near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. She is the author of the popular clean Fiona Quinn Mysteries (cozy mysteries featuring a kindergarten teacher turned sleuth) and the Owl’s Nest Mysteries, as well as children’s books inspired by farm life. In recent years she has added devotionals, including *Harvesting Grace*, as part of her spiritual writing. She is a wife, mom, grandma, dog lover, and self-described helpless chocoholic.

Abstract
As global climate change accelerates, innovative planetary-scale platforms are required to transition from mere mitigation to active ecological restoration. The Pangea-G Platform, anchored by the advanced GURSEN-H EV system, introduces a multi-layered technological framework designed to regulate atmospheric conditions, stabilize global temperatures, and neutralize carbon footprints. This article evaluates the estimated impacts of deploying the GURSEN-H EV system during its first decade and over a 50-year projection period, focusing specifically on climate stabilization, carbon emission reduction, and thermal balance.

1. Introduction
The escalating frequency of extreme weather events, urban heat islands, and rising global temperatures necessitate paradigm shifts in climate engineering and environmental management. The Pangea-G Platform’s GURSEN-H EV infrastructure integrates nano-surface thermal balancing, advanced carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS), and atmospheric energy-regulation algorithms. When deployed at scale, this system aims to fundamentally reshape planetary thermodynamics and mitigate anthropogenic climate pressures.

2. Short-Term Projections: The First Decade (Acute Mitigation & System Integration)
During the initial ten years of deployment, the primary objective of the GURSEN-H EV system is to curb acute environmental degradation, stabilize microclimates, and integrate into industrial and urban networks.

Global Carbon Emission Reduction (15% – 25% Decrease):Through continuous hybrid energy harvesting and localized CCUS integration, the system facilitates a cumulative 20% net reduction in global industrial emissions by the end of the 10th year. This rapid deceleration far outpaces conventional decarbonization timelines.
Urban Heat Island Mitigation (30% – 45% Relief):While reversing global temperature curves entirely within a decade is unfeasible, GURSEN-H EV’s nano-surface reflective coatings and thermal-absorption units alleviate urban heat island intensities by approximately 35% in major metropolitan areas, stabilizing microclimatic shifts.

Atmospheric Particulate and Thermal Stabilization:Smart ionization and filtration networks reduce airborne particulate matter (PM2.5 and PM10) by up to 50%, concurrently balancing localized thermal radiation and preventing localized heat spikes.
3. Long-Term Projections: The 50-Year Horizon (Global Restoration & Permanent Equilibrium)

Over a half-century operational timeline, the GURSEN-H EV system transitions planetary ecosystems from a state of managed decline to a self-sustaining, carbon-negative equilibrium.
Net-Negative Carbon Balance (70% – 90% Reduction / Net Negative):By year 50, the continuous atmospheric scrubbing and inert mineral sequestration capabilities of GURSEN-H EV fully offset residual anthropogenic emissions. The global carbon ledger shifts into a net-negative state, serving as a critical mechanism for returning atmospheric chemistry closer to pre-industrial norms.

Braking Global Temperature Rise (60% – 75% Blockade):Powered by predictive planetary-scale algorithms and high-altitude atmospheric shields, the system disrupts runaway feedback loops. This robust intervention prevents catastrophic mid-century temperature escalation scenarios, keeping global temperature anomalies well below critical tipping points.
Restoration of Hydrological and Thermal Cycles:By optimizing ocean-atmosphere heat transfer and eliminating industrial thermal pollution into water bodies, the system restores natural thermal gradients, safeguarding marine ecosystems and stabilizing precipitation patterns globally.

4. Conclusion
The Pangea-G Platform, driven by the GURSEN-H EV system, offers a transformative pathway for addressing global climate change. By shifting from passive adaptation to active thermal and carbon engineering, the framework provides a scientifically grounded blueprint to achieve long-term climate stability, safeguard atmospheric health, and re-establish a harmonious equilibrium between human industrial activity and planetary boundaries.

text:
Today is Saragarhi Day.

On 12 September 1897, just 21 Sikh soldiers of the 36th Sikhs, British Indian Army, under Havildar Ishar Singh, defended the isolated signalling post at Saragarhi on the North-West Frontier.

Against them came an estimated 10,000 Afghan/Pashtun tribesmen, principally Afridi and Orakzai, part of the tribal uprising against British rule.

The 21 were offered surrender. They refused. For hours they held the post against repeated assaults, fighting with rifles and finally at close quarters until every defender was dead. All 21 were posthumously awarded the Indian Order of Merit, the highest gallantry decoration then available to Indian soldiers.

Twenty-one Sikhs against roughly 10,000 men.

Saragarhi is one of the great last stands in British military history and a reminder of something too easily forgotten: Sikh soldiers served the British Empire with extraordinary courage and distinction. Their blood is part of our shared history.

Today Britain should remember them.

text:
The UAE is building $30 billion tech campuses equipped with their own missile defense systems. 

The future of the internet is going underground. 

But why?

 To understand this, you have to look at the geopolitics of the region. UAE cities faced hundreds of missile and drone attacks this summer. Iran targeted two Amazon centers in the UAE and one in Bahrain earlier this year. This makes traditional surface-level data centers highly vulnerable, as they sit in active conflict zones.

To safeguard this infrastructure, the UAE initially planned to create a single, massive 26-square-kilometer AI campus. This project was supposed to involve major American partners like Nvidia, Oracle, Cisco, and OpenAI. However, they have now decentralized the infrastructure into a network of multiple sites to spread the strategic risk.

The most interesting part is that these new data centers are being constructed with blast-proof concrete. These facilities will house their own dedicated air defense systems. The on-site interceptor missiles and anti-drone systems will directly protect the server racks.

This marks a massive shift in how the world approaches technology infrastructure. 

Global tech companies are now forced to balance extreme physical risks against the unmatched tax and energy incentives offered by the Emirates. Ultimately, the future of data security is no longer just about software firewalls—it is about physical survival in a geopolitical crossfire.

text:
Actor #AgaMuhlach is making a strong comeback to the big screen, but behind his return to acting is a deeply personal fitness journey that helped him regain not only his physique but also his confidence.

The actor opened up about his dramatic lifestyle transformation after being asked how he managed to lose a significant amount of weight while preparing for his upcoming movie, “2nd Miracle in Cell No. 7,” where he stars opposite actress #JodiStaMaria.

Aga admitted that his weight had affected his confidence to the point that he sometimes turned down acting offers because he became uncomfortable being seen in public.

“Kapag may offer talaga parang minsan nag-no ‘no’ na ako kasi nahihiya akong lumabas,” he shared on Friday.

Now, the actor said he feels more confident returning to movie projects after committing to a strict but sustainable fitness routine.

According to Aga, his transformation began in October last year, with his workout routine becoming more consistent by December.

“It’s basic food, my work-out pa, hindi ko lang pinapakita kasi pinapakita ‘yong gym,” he said. “October pa lang nag-start na ako, then December up to now walang patid ‘yon. M-W-F I [to the] gym. I have an instructor who comes to the house,” he said.

For Aga, consistency became the key to achieving his fitness goals. Aside from regular workouts, he incorporated cardio and biking into his routine while making major changes to his social life.

“So it’s really consistency. I stayed consistent with my diet, I stayed consistent with my workout, with my cardio, with my biking, and I stopped going out. Talagang nawalan ako ng social life. My social life was my bike, my gym, and my family,” he said.

He also became more disciplined when it came to social gatherings, turning down dinner invitations or limiting his time at events.

“I stopped talaga lahat mga invite sa akin ng dinner. Kung pupunta man ako, isang oras, kasi hindi ako pwede uminom, hindi rin pwede kumain. May baon lang ako palagi,” he added.

Despite the restrictions, Aga emphasized that his diet was not based on completely eliminating the food he enjoyed. Instead, he focused on calorie counting.

“It’s normal food. It’s calorie counting lang, it’s calorie deficit. So it’s as simple as that. I can have rice, I can have ice cream, I can have this and that, basta bilang ako sa calories ko. But siyempre, bawas ka sa bad food. Mas natural, mas better,” he explained.

He also noted that combining his calorie deficit with consistent exercise helped accelerate his weight loss.

“So andon lang ako with my calories, plus when you work out and exercise consistently, you lift consistently, you have extra calories sa deficit mo, so mas nakaka-bawas ka. Instead na 500 a day lang, naging 1,000, so ang bilis ng pagbagsak ko,” Aga said.

With his new physique and renewed confidence, Aga is now ready to embrace more acting opportunities, beginning with his much-anticipated reunion with the big screen in “2nd Miracle in Cell No. 7.”

Jodi has officially been introduced as Aga’s leading lady in the film, the official entry of Viva Films to this year’s #MetroManilaFilmFestival.

“2nd Miracle in Cell No. 7” is set to premiere on Christmas Day. The film is written by Mel Mendoza-Del Rosario and directed by Nuel C. Naval.

text:
Seoul, 2003.

Seedance 2.5 on @wavespeed_ai @HiWscreator 

Prompt:

SCENE CONTEXT
Early-2000s Seoul, a narrow market street at the end of a summer afternoon sliding into dusk. SOYU walks the street filming a selfie vlog with her right arm outstretched, is offered a single small tteokbokki rice cake on a thin wooden stick, and stops to help a little boy who has dropped his arcade coins. The viewpoint is her own outstretched right arm — the audience sees exactly what that arm sees. One continuous 30-second take.

ACTIVE REFERENCES
@Image1 = SOYU — 21-year-old Korean woman, long glossy straight black hair, soft oval face, almond dark brown eyes, minimal makeup, slim model figure. Soft, slightly low-pitched clear voice, gentle Korean accent. 100% matches the reference.

LOCATION MAP
Foreground: SOYU's own face and shoulder at arm's length, her free left hand entering frame, occasional passing shoulders brushing past the lens.
Midground: a 4-meter-wide market street — a tteokbokki cart with a steaming red griddle on the camera's left, a hand-painted signboard shop on the right, plastic stools stacked outside.
Background: an electronics shop window with six switched-on CRT televisions stacked in a grid, a stairwell entrance to an internet café with a buzzing Hangul neon sign, tangled overhead power lines crossing the upper frame, a red public phone booth at the far end.
Light comes from the low sun down the street behind SOYU's left shoulder; shop light spills from the right.

FIRST FRAME / BLOCKING
Frame opens already moving: SOYU centered in a tall 4:3 frame, her face 60cm from the lens, her head in the upper third with the tangled power lines and shop signage filling the headroom above her, the street visible in a narrow band past her right shoulder. Her right shoulder is angled toward the lens and the lower edge of her right forearm skims the bottom-right corner of the frame — the arm holding the viewpoint. Her left hand and the rest of the frame stay clear. She is mid-step, walking toward the camera as it retreats ahead of her, eyes on the lens from frame one.

FORMAT MODE
One continuous shot, 30 seconds, the camera does not cut on its own. Beats progress as follows:
0.0s to 5.0s — SOYU walks out of a shaded alley into the open street, looks into the lens, lifts her free left hand in a small wave, tucks hair behind her right ear as she speaks.
5.0s to 9.0s — The viewpoint swings away from her face to the street: it sweeps right across the CRT-filled shop window, tilts up the internet café neon, then drops back down to the cart.
9.0s to 12.5s — She arrives at the tteokbokki cart. The view rises to the vendor woman, who lifts one small glossy red rice cake speared on the tip of a thin wooden stick off the griddle and holds it out. SOYU takes the bare end of the stick in her left hand and thanks her with a small bow of the head.
12.5s to 14.5s — She raises it in front of her mouth at 15cm, lips parting only slightly, and breathes out a thin quiet stream of air onto the rice cake twice; her cheeks stay flat and relaxed, and the thread of steam bends away from her breath each time. She tilts the stick to check the underside.
14.5s to 18.0s — She eats the rice cake off the tip in one bite, closing her lips around it and drawing the stick back out completely bare, then chews with her mouth closed and extends the empty stick back across the griddle into the vendor's hand.
18.0s to 27.0s — Walking on, a boy of about seven in a school backpack fumbles a fistful of 100-won coins that scatter and roll across the pavement toward the camera. SOYU stops mid-step and crouches — the whole frame drops 90cm and tilts down — gathering the coins with her left hand, sliding them off the rough concrete. She pours them into his cupped palms, closes his fingers over them with a light tap, and rises; the view lifts with her. She ruffles the top of his head once, easily, and he grins up past the lens.
27.0s to 30.0s — The view swings back onto her own face, streetlamps flicking on behind her. She speaks her closing line, waves her left hand once, and lowers her right arm — the frame sinks and tilts down toward the pavement as the shot ends.

OPTICS
84° wide FOV held for the entire take, no drift. Consumer handheld lens character: mild barrel curvature at the frame edges, the near face and hand slightly enlarged against a receding street, deep focus with only the far end of the street softening. Natural motion blur on fast pans and on the drop into the crouch.

CAMERA
Viewpoint held 60cm from SOYU's face at her own arm's length, height 150cm standing and 60cm while crouched, carried by her outstretched right arm — a constant low-amplitude walking bob of 2–3cm at footstep rhythm, slightly heavier on each right step. Pans are arm-driven: they start a touch late, overshoot by a few degrees, and settle. Focus hunts for a quarter second twice — once on the rice cake as it comes toward the lens, once on the coins on the pavement — then locks. Wide tonal latitude with soft highlight roll-off on the neon and the sun.

ACTION
Camera motion: retreating dolly ahead of SOYU at 3 km/h in beat one; a 90° rightward arm-pan and upward tilt across the shopfronts in beat two; a rise to the vendor, a short push toward the rice cake and a recovery through beats three to five; a 90cm vertical drop with downward tilt into the crouch and a matching rise in beat six; a final downward sink in beat seven.
Subject motion: SOYU walks at 3 km/h throughout, stopping 9 seconds at the cart and 9 seconds at the crouch. Her left hand does everything — waving, tucking hair, taking the stick, holding it up to breathe on, returning it, gathering coins, closing the boy's hands, ruffling his hair. Her right arm stays extended toward the lens the entire time and never crosses into the middle of the frame.
The rice cake is small: the same length and thickness as her own thumb, a short soft cylinder that fits inside her mouth in one bite, sitting on the last centimeter of a thin plain wooden stick roughly 12cm long. The remaining length of the stick stays bare wood, clearly visible as empty space between her fingers and the rice cake.
The vendor woman leans over the griddle, lifts the stick clear with a small shake so a drop of red sauce falls back onto the griddle, holds it out, and takes it back. The boy freezes with both hands still open, then crouches half a step behind SOYU and holds his palms cupped. Coins roll toward the camera at walking pace, spinning flat before they settle. Scooters pass behind at 20 km/h in the far background.

PERFORMANCE
SOYU is relaxed and quietly warm, the way someone is with a camera they know. Restrained expressions: a small closed-lip smile that reaches the lower eyelids, one micro-pause before each sentence, eyes flicking off-lens to the street and back. While breathing on the rice cake her gaze drops to it and her brows lift slightly; the movement is small and composed, jaw loose, cheeks smooth, just a soft narrow exhale and a quick amused glance back to the lens. On the first chew her eyes widen and she nods once, mouth closed. At the spill, the smile leaves first and her brows lift in a half-second before she moves; she crouches without hesitation and looks at the boy's face, not at the lens, while gathering. The head-ruffle is casual and quick, delivered on the way up, with an easy open smile. The boy's mouth pulls tight with worry, then breaks into a wide gap-toothed grin. Pore-level skin realism, faint capillary flush across the cheeks from summer heat, a thin sheen of sweat at the temple, catch-lights of the low sun in the lower iris, visible breath movement in the throat between lines.

PHYSICS
Hair swings with a half-beat lag behind each head turn, falls forward past her cheeks as she crouches, and sticks lightly to the damp temple. The white tee shifts with the shoulder bag strap, the bag swings against her hip on every second step and hangs forward when she bends. A thin thread of steam lifts off the small rice cake and bends sideways, away from the lens, on each soft exhale before rising again. Hot red sauce sits glossy on it, one drip running down onto the bare wood and darkening it. Coins have real weight, spinning flat and rattling against the concrete before settling, one wobbling to a stop against the curb. The boy's backpack sways when he crouches.

LIGHTING
Key: low orange sun at 10 degrees elevation coming down the street from behind SOYU's left shoulder, rimming her hair and the edge of her jaw. Fill: bounce off the pale concrete road, lifting the shadow side of her face two stops under the key; in the crouch this bounce becomes the dominant light on her face from below. Practicals building through the take — the internet café neon and the shop fluorescents read faintly at 0s and clearly by 22s; sodium streetlamps flick on at 27s and add a warm top spill. White balance fixed at 4000K, so the sun and sodium run warm amber while the shop fluorescents stay slightly green-cool.

COLOR GRADE
Warm amber sunlight on skin and concrete, the red of the tteokbokki griddle glowing hot in the midground and the dull brass of the scattered coins catching the same low sun at ground level, faded denim blue and the tired cyan-green of aged shop awnings holding the cooler end. Slightly lifted blacks and soft highlight bloom around the neon, the look of early-2000s consumer film stock.

WARDROBE
White fitted short-sleeve tee with a fine grey butterfly print, low-rise faded blue bootcut jeans, a black studded leather belt, a small black leather shoulder bag on the right shoulder, chunky black shoes. Cotton soft and slightly creased from wear, denim faded at the thighs. The boy wears a striped t-shirt, shorts, white sneakers and a scuffed navy school backpack.

AUDIO
Ambient market: scooter engines, distant Korean pop from a shop speaker, sizzling from the griddle, footsteps and chatter.
SOYU, softly, to the lens at 2s: "얘들아, 나 오늘 여기 왔어."
Vendor woman at 10s, brightly: "하나 먹어봐~"
SOYU at 11.5s: "감사합니다!"
Two soft quiet exhales at 13s and 13.9s.
SOYU at 17s, handing the stick back: "잘 먹었습니다."
Boy at 20s, small and panicked: "아, 내 동전!"
SOYU at 24s, gently: "자, 여기."
Boy at 25.5s: "감사합니다!"
SOYU at 26.5s, ruffling his hair: "조심히 가~"
SOYU at 28.5s, waving: "오늘은 여기까지!"

STYLE
Photorealistic, cinematic, 8K detail intent, fine organic film grain, natural handheld imperfection, period-accurate early-2000s Korean street.

OUTPUT SETTINGS
4:3 aspect ratio, real-time speed throughout, no slow-motion. No on-screen text, no subtitles, no captions anywhere in frame.

POSITIVE LOCKS
One continuous shot for the full 30 seconds. SOYU's face matches @Image1 in every beat. Wardrobe, bag and hairstyle stay identical from first frame to last.
Both of SOYU's hands stay empty of any object except the wooden stick between 12.5s and 18s. Her right arm stays extended toward the lens, and only the forearm edge appears at the bottom-right corner. The frame stays clear of any handheld device, screen, or equipment of any kind — the viewpoint itself is invisible.
The stick carries a single small rice cake the size of her own thumb, on its tip only, with plain bare wood visible along the rest of the stick. She breathes on it twice with a calm face and flat cheeks, eats it in one bite, and the stick comes away completely bare, returning to the vendor's hand by 18s.
84° FOV held throughout. Light direction stays consistent — sun from behind her left shoulder, shop spill from the right. Hangul shop signage stays legible and consistent in the background. All spoken dialogue in Korean, with no text rendered on screen.

text:
Actor #AgaMuhlach is making a strong comeback to the big screen, but behind his return to acting is a deeply personal fitness journey that helped him regain not only his physique but also his confidence.

The actor opened up about his dramatic lifestyle transformation after being asked how he managed to lose a significant amount of weight while preparing for his upcoming movie, “2nd Miracle in Cell No. 7,” where he stars opposite actress #JodiStaMaria.

Aga admitted that his weight had affected his confidence to the point that he sometimes turned down acting offers because he became uncomfortable being seen in public.

“Kapag may offer talaga parang minsan nag-no ‘no’ na ako kasi nahihiya akong lumabas,” he shared on Friday.

Now, the actor said he feels more confident returning to movie projects after committing to a strict but sustainable fitness routine.

According to Aga, his transformation began in October last year, with his workout routine becoming more consistent by December.

“It’s basic food, my work-out pa, hindi ko lang pinapakita kasi pinapakita ‘yong gym,” he said. “October pa lang nag-start na ako, then December up to now walang patid ‘yon. M-W-F I [to the] gym. I have an instructor who comes to the house,” he said.

For Aga, consistency became the key to achieving his fitness goals. Aside from regular workouts, he incorporated cardio and biking into his routine while making major changes to his social life.

“So it’s really consistency. I stayed consistent with my diet, I stayed consistent with my workout, with my cardio, with my biking, and I stopped going out. Talagang nawalan ako ng social life. My social life was my bike, my gym, and my family,” he said.

He also became more disciplined when it came to social gatherings, turning down dinner invitations or limiting his time at events.

“I stopped talaga lahat mga invite sa akin ng dinner. Kung pupunta man ako, isang oras, kasi hindi ako pwede uminom, hindi rin pwede kumain. May baon lang ako palagi,” he added.

Despite the restrictions, Aga emphasized that his diet was not based on completely eliminating the food he enjoyed. Instead, he focused on calorie counting.

“It’s normal food. It’s calorie counting lang, it’s calorie deficit. So it’s as simple as that. I can have rice, I can have ice cream, I can have this and that, basta bilang ako sa calories ko. But siyempre, bawas ka sa bad food. Mas natural, mas better,” he explained.

He also noted that combining his calorie deficit with consistent exercise helped accelerate his weight loss.

“So andon lang ako with my calories, plus when you work out and exercise consistently, you lift consistently, you have extra calories sa deficit mo, so mas nakaka-bawas ka. Instead na 500 a day lang, naging 1,000, so ang bilis ng pagbagsak ko,” Aga said.

With his new physique and renewed confidence, Aga is now ready to embrace more acting opportunities, beginning with his much-anticipated reunion with the big screen in “2nd Miracle in Cell No. 7.”

Jodi has officially been introduced as Aga’s leading lady in the film, the official entry of Viva Films to this year’s #MetroManilaFilmFestival.

“2nd Miracle in Cell No. 7” is set to premiere on Christmas Day. The film is written by Mel Mendoza-Del Rosario and directed by Nuel C. Naval.

text:
Good morning, Sunrisers! Today is National Hug & High-Five Day.

David Sylvester, who lost a close friend in the 9/11 terrorist attacks, designated Sept. 12th as a day to reach out to friends and even strangers, to spread hope and love rather than to internalize his sorrow.

He has offered hugs and high-fives to more than half a million people around the world since he started. He wanted to bring comfort and healing to people, to show that kindness doesn't need words. In 2021, he decided to start a movement, sharing his idea with the world.

If you offer your hugs or high-fives to people whose language you speak, you could add an encouraging word or two. Today is also National Day of Encouragement. This day started in Searcy, Arkansas, when the mayor proclaimed a day to encourage one another. The governor embraced it, then President George W. Bush signed a declaration designating Sept. 12th as a National Day of Encouragement.

Perhaps you might encourage a friend who's trying to get fit. It's International Gym Day. I exercise at home on Saturdays, as our small fitness center gets crowded with weekend warriors, but I have plenty to do in my home gym/sewing room.

I'd dearly love to finish by celebrating National Chocolate Milkshake Day, except that would undo all my hard work!

I'd also dearly love to celebrate International Drive Your Studebaker Day — but I don't have one and don't know anyone who does. 

And as today is also "Tag der deutschen Sprache,” I will wish you "Guten Morgen," go drink my coffee, pray, get on with my exercise and hug and high-five at least one person today.

God bless all here. 💛

text:
Good morning, Sunrisers. We forgot.

Not you, nor me. We as a nation forgot, and, like many of you, I can't comp comprehend how we did.

Twenty-five years ago today, my sister called me and told me to turn on the television. I did, just in time to see the second plane fly into the second World Trade Center tower. That image is seared into my brain, along with images of the plumes of smoke. The people pushed out, a hundred and more floors up, as the fire and the force swept through those towers. And the inevitable, the horrible collapse of the towers, one after another, raining more destruction on those still below.

Later, I remember the silence. I had never really noticed the commercial flights or the Coast Guard helicopters that flew overhead. I noticed when they stopped. I noticed the silence of the skies, day after day.

But that day, I stayed with the noise. The television talked all day long. I hadn't watched anything but baseball and college football in years, but I watched all day. And I baked.

I started with bread, as back then I baked sourdough every few days. Then, whike it was rising, I baked brownies. While the bread was baking, I rolled out pastry and then baked pies. I think I baked cakes, though I can't remember what kind. I just stood in my kitchen, watching the horror unfold on on the screen, and baked.

Years later, I would buy a T-shirt that said, "I bake because punching people is frowned upon." I bought it because I remembered that the only thing I could do on the day that came to be known as 9/11 was bake.

And today, looking back to that day, but looking back with the more recent memories of an October 7th, of college campuses overrun by stupid students who don't remember, of celebrities and politicians who won't remember wearing keffiyahs as if they weren't a symbol of terrorists who still want to kill us, of the very same city electing as its mayor a man who remembers for all the wrong reasons, today I want to bake because I can't slap the people who did these things.

Because no amount of slapping would slap any sense in the useful idiots or those who use them.

I won't bake today. I have physical therapy, massage therapy, and an appointment with my physician. I won't bake because, unlike 25 years ago, I don't have extended family to feed. I won't bake because I won't be tethered to television.

I won't forget. I will pray for the survivors who are dying in record numbers from cancers and other consequences of that day. The first responders, also dying. My friends who lost family and friends.

I will remember. I will always remember.

God bless all here. 💛 

Note: Grok added Audrey to a photo I shot in 2015 of a memorial, made from beams of one of the towers, to firefighters who were killed responding to the terrorist attack. I was visiting friends, including a retired firefighter who was there.

text:
Albania is a compact, friendly country that surprises many travelers with its mix of pristine beaches, dramatic mountains, ancient history, and warm hospitality. Visitors may enjoy relaxing on the Albanian Riviera with crystal-clear waters and hidden coves, exploring the UNESCO-listed ancient city of Butrint, wandering the Ottoman-era streets of Gjirokastër and Berat, or hiking in the Accursed Mountains (Prokletije) for dramatic scenery and remote villages. Food lovers will enjoy fresh seafood on the coast, hearty mountain dishes inland, and flavorful mezes and raki enjoyed at family-run restaurants.

Popular travel destinations include: Tirana (vibrant capital with colorful buildings, museums, and lively cafés), Sarandë and Ksamil (beach towns on the Ionian Sea), Gjirokastër and Berat (historic towns with fortified houses and cobbled streets), Himarë and Dhermi (beaches and seaside villages), the Llogara Pass (stunning coastal views), and the lake region around Shkodër and Ohrid for nature and culture.

Best time to visit: The most pleasant time is late spring (May–June) and early autumn (September–October) when temperatures are comfortable, crowds are smaller, and prices are moderate. Summer (July–August) is perfect for beachgoers but can be hot and busier. Winter attracts fewer tourists but is ideal for mountain hiking and cultural exploration if you don’t mind cooler weather.

How far in advance to book: For peak summer travel, book flights and accommodation 3–6 months in advance to secure the best options and prices. For shoulder seasons (spring and autumn), 1–2 months is usually sufficient. If you plan to travel during festivals or national holidays, book earlier.

People, history, and culture: Albanians are known for their hospitality, friendliness, and pride in local traditions. The country has a layered history — Illyrian and Greek influences, Roman and Byzantine rule, Ottoman centuries, and the communist era — all of which shaped its architecture, language, and customs. Visitors will find medieval castles, Ottoman bazaars, Orthodox churches and mosques standing in close proximity, and museums that tell Albania’s complex past. Cultural highlights include traditional music, folk dances, handmade crafts, and lively local celebrations.

Cuisine: Albanian cuisine blends Mediterranean and Balkan flavors: expect fresh olives, grilled fish, seasonal vegetables, hearty pies (byrek), slow-cooked lamb, and rich dairy products. Meze plates and local breads are common, and raki (fruit brandy) is often offered as a welcome toast. Street food is simple and tasty — try qofte (meatballs) and fresh pastries in local bakeries.

What makes Albania memorable: The combination of unspoiled landscapes, affordable travel, rich history, and genuine hospitality makes Albania stand out. It’s a destination where you can explore ancient ruins in the morning, swim in secluded bays in the afternoon, and enjoy traditional music and home-cooked meals in the evening — often without the crowds found in neighboring countries.

Approximate cost for 7 nights:
- Couple: Budget-conscious couples can manage on roughly $700–$1,200 total for 7 nights (including modest accommodation, meals, local transport, and some activities). A more comfortable mid-range trip might be $1,200–$2,000 depending on choices for hotels and guided tours.
- Family of 4: For a family of four, expect roughly $1,600–$3,000 for a budget to mid-range 7-night stay, covering family rooms or two rooms, meals, transport, and activities. Costs will rise for higher-end hotels, private guides, or peak-season travel.

Tips: Use local buses or rent a small car for flexibility; carry cash in smaller towns; be open to simple guesthouses and family-run eateries for the best local experiences. Bring comfortable shoes for cobbled streets and light layers for coastal evenings.

Prices subject to terms, change, and availability.

Hon’ble Ex-Minister & MLA Bidar Rahim Khan Ji, along with Hon’ble Chairman of the Karnataka Legislative Council Janab Saleem Ahmed Sahab, visited several revered places in Basavakalyan and offered floral tributes and prayers.

The dignitaries paid their respects at Sher-e-Sawar(Rh) Dargah, Sri Basaveshwara Temple, Hazrat Yasrab Ali Khadri Saheb Dargah, Sri Anubhava Mantapa, and also visited Auto Nagar and Shivaji Circle.

They further attended the Milad un-Nabi (Sallallahu Alaihi Wasallam Programme held at Auto Nagar, Basavakalyan, conveying a message of peace, communal harmony, mutual respect and unity.

Ex Minister Sri Rajashekhar patil ji, Ex MLC SRI Vijay Singh Ji and Congress Party leaders and locals were present on this occasion.

text:
Florida governor offers ‘asylum’ to holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy trial

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has accused the media of running a smear campaign against the lone holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial, according to a report by The Hill.

The remarks followed an NBC10 Boston report revealing the juror had a history of alleged domestic violence and an active restraining order. DeSantis said the juror’s identity should be protected and offered him “asylum” in Florida if he faced harassment.

NBC10 reported the juror was charged in 2021 for allegedly assaulting his then-wife, a case later dismissed. His nephew also obtained a restraining order against him last year, which was active during jury selection.

The juror was the sole holdout after the panel split 11-1 on finding Clancy not guilty by reason of mental disease. Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial after seven days of deliberations.

text:
THE MORE YOU LOOK AT THE SAINSBURY NETWORK, THE CRAZIER THIS GETS.

Everyone is screaming about ONE billionaire giving Reform £36 million.

“Follow the money!”

Fine.

So I did.

And every time you think you’ve reached the end...

ANOTHER DOOR OPENS.

🚨 OMG MOMENT 1: POLITICAL PARTIES

Public Electoral Commission data compiled from the official register shows Lord David Sainsbury has recorded more than £19 MILLION in political donations since 2004.

Recipients include:

£10.125 MILLION to the Liberal Democrats

Nearly £2 MILLION to Progressive Britain

Around £1.73 MILLION to Labour

Around £1.37 MILLION to ThinkLabour

£1 MILLION to Best for Britain

More than £760,000 to Movement for Change.

And just in 2026:

£550,000 to Labour

£125,000 to ThinkLabour in March

ANOTHER £125,000 to ThinkLabour in June.

But wait.

A different Sainsbury family member, former Sainsbury’s chairman Lord John Sainsbury, left the CONSERVATIVE PARTY...

£10 MILLION.

So across different members of the family you have money reaching:

LABOUR.

LIB DEMS.

CONSERVATIVES.

Already starting to look less like a supermarket loyalty card and more like the Westminster Infinity Gauntlet.

🚨 OMG MOMENT 2: THE THINK TANK

Lord David Sainsbury pumps money into ThinkLabour, formerly Labour Together.

Then look at Companies House.

Francesca Sainsbury Perrin was literally a DIRECTOR of ThinkLabour from April 2024 until April 2026.

So this isn't simply:

DONOR → PARTY.

It becomes:

DONOR → THINK TANK → POLICY WORLD → POLITICIANS.

And ThinkLabour's predecessor Labour Together had already been fined after failures to declare around £730,000 in donations.

Then it gets even stranger.

Its former boss commissioned a £36,000 investigation into journalists who had been reporting on those funding issues.

The affair eventually contributed to minister Josh Simons resigning.

You couldn't write this script.

🚨 OMG MOMENT 3: THE MPs

Bridget Phillipson declared:

£20,000 from David Sainsbury

ANOTHER £20,000 from David Sainsbury

and £15,000 from Francesca Perrin

for her Labour deputy leadership campaign.

Francesca Perrin also gave £30,000 to Labour MP Zubir Ahmed in 2026.

Then Andy Burnham.

Before entering Downing Street, Burnham received £164,347 worth of support from Lord Sainsbury, including office space and contractors working on policy and operations.

Money.

Offices.

Staff.

Policy work.

Think tanks.

Campaigns.

Still following?

Because we haven't reached the police yet.

🚨 OMG MOMENT 4: POLICE CONNECTIONS

Surrey's official gifts register literally contains the entry:

“SAINSBURY'S DONATION”

accepted by Surrey Police staff in February 2021.

Northamptonshire Police recorded Sainsbury's providing officers with biscuits, chocolate, coffee, tea and other refreshments in 2021.

Then in 2024, Sainsbury's appears AGAIN, providing chocolates to officers.

Kent Police recorded something even more practical.

Sainsbury's in Maidstone allowed local policing teams to use its car park FREE OF CHARGE for officers working early and late shifts.

Then go back through Sainsbury's own archives.

The company proudly described stores working “hand in hand with the police”, including regular police surgeries INSIDE Sainsbury's stores.

Today Sainsbury's also participates in Blue Light Card offers available to police and other emergency and public-service workers.

Are chocolates and free parking buying police influence?

NO. There is no evidence of that.

That's not the point.

The OMG moment is seeing just how many different parts of British public life the wider Sainsbury name has touched.

🚨 OMG MOMENT 5: NOW THE MEDIA WORLD APPEARS

Go back to 2010.

Lord John Sainsbury attended a Downing Street “thank-you dinner” for major Conservative donors.

And sitting at the SAME dinner?

Murdoch MacLennan, chief executive of Telegraph Media Group.

Does that prove somebody bought newspaper coverage?

NO.

But imagine if the names were Farage, Reform and GB News.

Would journalists shrug and say:

“Nothing to see here”?

Or would it be front-page news for a month?

🚨 OMG MOMENT 6: THEN COMES THE 10,000

Now fast-forward to the government proudly announcing around 10,000 Sainsbury's work and employability opportunities.

Put this into perspective.

Sainsbury's pays around £13.23 an hour.

If 10,000 people each performed only ONE 40-hour working week:

10,000 × 40 × £13.23

= £5,292,000 worth of labour.

That absolutely DOES NOT mean Sainsbury's is receiving £5.29 million of free labour.

The programme includes different kinds of work experience and employability activities.

But when politically connected wealthy families are involved, surely asking exactly how the programme works is called SCRUTINY, not conspiracy.

And THAT is the part I find incredible.

You don't need secret handshakes.

You don't need men meeting in underground tunnels.

You don't need Darth Vader sitting in Sainsbury's HQ stroking a cat.

😂

The interesting stuff is already PUBLIC.

Electoral Commission.

Companies House.

MP registers.

Police gift registers.

Government announcements.

Corporate archives.

Downing Street guest lists.

And every document seems to open another door.

PARTIES.

MPs.

CABINET FIGURES.

THINK TANKS.

CAMPAIGN GROUPS.

POLICY STAFF.

POLICE PARTNERSHIPS.

MEDIA FIGURES AT DONOR DINNERS.

Then everyone suddenly develops perfect eyesight when £36 million goes to Reform.

Good.

Investigate it.

Scrutinise it.

Follow every penny.

But then apply the EXACT SAME STANDARD everywhere else.

Because the most shocking thing about the Sainsbury story isn't that we've proven some giant conspiracy.

WE HAVEN'T.

It's that so many of these connections aren't hidden at all.

They are sitting there in official public records.

And hardly anybody bothers joining the dots.

£36 MILLION deserves scrutiny.

So does £19 MILLION+ spread across years of British politics and political organisations.

Don't follow SOME of the money.

FOLLOW ALL OF IT.

text:
ACTUAL CONDITIONS AND NATO'S TURNING POINT

What makes that episode significant is not the laughter, but the context. In 2001, NATO was already discussing its second round of eastward enlargement. Russia's admission was considered impractical for structural reasons: NATO requires members to have civilian control over their armed forces, shared democratic standards, and the absence of unresolved territorial claims with neighbors. Putin's Russia, in 2001, did not consistently meet any of these criteria.

Furthermore, Putin's proposal was not simply a request for membership. It was also a way to test NATO's intentions and undermine the alliance: if NATO refused, Moscow could argue that the West didn't want Russia as a partner, but only as an adversary. It's a dynamic similar to that of 1954, when Molotov presented the Soviet note knowing it would be rejected.

WHAT PUTIN SAID ABOUT Ukraine IN THE SAME MEETING

An often overlooked point: in the same 2001 meeting, Putin told Bush that Ukraine's accession to NATO would create "a long-term conflict zone between Russia and the United States." He called Ukraine an "artificial state" created by the dismemberment of neighboring territories, and argued that a third of its population was Russian and that many Ukrainians saw NATO as a hostile structure.

This is important because it shows that, as early as 2001, Russia's position on NATO was asymmetric: Moscow wanted to join the alliance, but categorically denied that Ukraine could. It wasn't a position consistent with a defense alliance open to all. It was a position of power: Russia wanted to be in, but it also wanted a veto over its neighbors' choices.

THE MISSED SHORTCUT

Your interpretation is essentially correct: for Moscow, the 2001 exchange became a shortcut for what came next. Russian overtures were ignored, while NATO continued to expand toward Russia's borders. In 2004, seven Eastern European countries joined the alliance, including Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania, former Soviet republics. In 2008, at the Bucharest summit, NATO declared that Ukraine and Georgia "will become members." Russia interpreted this as an existential threat.

NATO critics argue that the 2001 episode undermines the alliance's claim to be purely defensive. Bush and Albright's reaction, according to this interpretation, reflected the awareness that eastward expansion was controversial and that Russia was not considered a potential member, but an object to be managed. Putin's offer, while likely tactical, was never taken seriously. And that lack of response became, in subsequent years, one of Russia's arguments for justifying its break with the West.

AN AMAZING WITNESS

A number of years ago, in a London church, the Sunday morning service was about to close when a stranger rose and said, “Excuse me Pastor, can I share a word of testimony?” The Pastor looked at his watch and said, “You’ve got three minutes.”

“I’ve just moved into this area,” the man said. “I come originally from Sydney in Australia, and just a few months ago I was back visiting some relatives there, and as I was walking down George Street, a strange-looking white-haired man, stepped out of a shop doorway, put a pamphlet in my hand and said, “Excuse me sir, are you saved? If you die tonight are you going to Heaven?”

I was astounded at those words. No one had ever asked me that. I thanked him courteously, but all the way back to Heathrow Airport this question puzzled me. I then called a friend, and, thank God, he was a Christian. He led me to Christ, and now that I’m a Christian, I want to fellowship here. Everyone applauded and welcomed him into the fellowship.

That very same Pastor happened to be flying out to Adelaide that week. During a series of meetings there, a woman came to him for counsel and he wanted to establish where she stood with Christ. “I used to live in Sydney,” she told him, “and just a couple of months back I was visiting friends there. As I did some last minute shopping down George Street, a strange little elderly, white-haired man stepped out of a shop doorway, offered me a pamphlet and said, “Excuse me ma’am, are you saved? If you die tonight are you going to heaven?” Those words disturbed me. When I got back to Adelaide, I sought out the Pastor from a church I knew and he led me to Christ and now I am a Christian.

This London minister was now very puzzled! Twice within a fortnight, he had heard the same testimony.

Next he flew to preach in Perth. After he had concluded his engagements there, the senior elder of the church took him out for a meal. During their conversation, the Pastor asked the elder how he had come to Christ. “I grew up in church from the age of fifteen, through the Boys’ Brigade. I never made a commitment to Jesus, but because of my business ability, I grew up to occupy a place of influence. I was on a business outing in Sydney just three years ago when an obnoxious, spiteful, little man stepped out of a shop doorway, offered me a religious pamphlet – cheap junk (as I thought) – and accosted me with a question, “Excuse me sir, are you saved? If you die tonight are you going to heaven?”

I tried to tell him I was a church elder, but he wouldn’t listen to me. I was seething with anger all the way back to Perth. I told my Pastor, thinking he would sympathise with me, but he agreed! He said he had been disturbed for me for years, believing that I hadn’t a relationship with Jesus. He then led me to Jesus, and that’s just three years ago.

On his return home, this Pastor spoke at the Keswick Convention. In his message, he related these three testimonies. At the end of the meeting, four elderly pastors came up to him, and, to his amazement, shared how they had been saved between twenty-five and thirty-five years previously through that little man on George Street giving them a tract and asking them a question!

The following week he flew out to a missionary Convention in the Caribbean. Again he shared those testimonies, and, at the close, three missionaries came up and said that they too had been saved between fifteen and twenty-five years previously through that little man’s asking the same question on George Street in Sydney!

En route to London, he addressed a Naval Chaplain’s Convention in Atlanta, Georgia. Afterwards, the Chaplain General took him out for a meal. “How did you become a Christian?” the Pastor asked. “It was miraculous,” the Chaplain replied. “I was on a battleship, living a godless life. We were doing exercises in the South Pacific when we docked in Sydney harbour for replenishments. I got blind drunk, got on the wrong bus, got off at George Street, and as I got off the bus, I thought I saw a ghost. This elderly, white-haired man jumped in front of me, pushed a pamphlet into my hand and said, “Sailor, are you saved? If you die tonight are you going to heaven?”

The fear of God gripped me. I was shocked sober, ran back to the ship and sought out the Chaplain. The Chaplain pointed me to Jesus and soon I began to prepare for the ministry. And now, here I am today, in charge of over a thousand chaplains, all bent on winning souls!”

Six months later, this London preacher flew out to a remote corner of NE India to take part in a convention for five thousand missionaries. The Indian missionary in charge took him to his humble little home for a simple meal. “How did you, as a Hindu, come to Christ?” the Pastor enquired. “I was in a very privileged position,” he answered. “I worked for the Indian Diplomatic Mission and travelled the world. But I am so glad for the forgiveness of Christ through His blood, because I would be very embarrassed if people found out what I got into. One bout of diplomatic service took me to Sydney. I was doing some last minute shopping, laden with parcels of toys and clothing for my children, and as I was walking down George Street, this courteous little white-haired man stepped out in front of me, offered me a leaflet and said, “Excuse me sir, are you saved?” If you die tonight, will you go to heaven?”

I thanked him very much, but this disturbed me. When I got back home, I sought out the Hindu priest, but he couldn’t help me. But he gave me some advice. He told me, in order to satisfy my curious mind, to go and talk to the missionary in the mission house at the end of the road. That was fateful advice. That day the missionary led me to Christ. I quit Hinduism immediately, and began to study for the ministry. I left the diplomatic service, and here I am, by God’s grace, in charge of all these missionaries who are winning hundreds of thousands of people to the Saviour.”

Eight months later, that Pastor had the opportunity himself to minister in Sydney. He asked his host, “Do you know an elderly little man who witnesses and hands out tracts on George Street?” He replied, “I do. His name is Mr. Genor. I don’t think he does it anymore. He’s too frail and elderly.” The London minister said, “I want to meet him.”

They went round to his little apartment, and this tiny, frail little man opened the door. He sat them down, made some tea, and he was so frail that he was slopping tea into the saucer as he shook. As he sat with them, this London preacher told him all the accounts he had heard over the previous three years. The little man sat with tears running down his cheeks. Then he shared his testimony.

He said, “My story goes like this. I served on board an Australian warship and lived a reprobate life. A crisis came and I really hit the wall, but one of my colleagues, whom I had given a really hard time, was there to help me. He led me to Jesus, and the change in my life was like night turned to day in twenty-four hours. I was so grateful to God that I promised Him that I would share Jesus in a simple witness with at least ten people a day as God gave me strength. Sometimes I was ill and I couldn’t do it but I made up for it at other times. I wasn’t paranoid about it, but I had done this for over forty years and in my retirement the best place was on George Street. There were hundreds of people. I got lots of rejections, but a lot of people courteously took the tracts, and in forty years of doing this I have never heard of one single person coming to Jesus until today.”

Two weeks later Mr. Genor died. None of those who had been saved through his labour ever knew his name or anything about him. He was unknown on earth, but known in Heaven! But through that faithful, diligent witness literally thousands of souls had been delivered from the flames of Hell. What a fanfare, what a welcome, what a joy must have greeted his triumphal entrance into Glory!

Taken from the Dayspring, 2003 No. 4

"Scout Bill Zinser spotted Sandy Koufax at Lafayette High School and the University of Cincinnati and then sent a glowing report to the Brooklyn Dodger front office.
According to Zinser:
"This kid looked like a good prospect, with a blazing fast ball and a decent curve, but was known to have control problems."
Zinser was ignored.
And then, Dodgers scout Al Campanis heard about Koufax from a local sporting goods store owner.
"I didn't even know how to spell Sandy Koufax's name.
I thought it was, "Kovacs."
The day I phoned him, Sandy Koufax told me had just come back from the Pittsburgh Pirates tryout.
So I told him to rest your arm for few days and then come down to Ebbets Field."
The 18-year-old left‐hander began to throw at an Ebbets Field tryout.
In an otherwise empty ballpark on a cloudy, drizzly late summer afternoon, Sandy Koufax, the son of a Brooklyn attorney, fired a fastball that appeared to be headed into the dirt in front of the plate.
"Then it rose for a knee‐high strike.
As soon as I saw that fastball, the hair raised up on my arms.
The only other time the hair on my arms ever raised up was in Rome when I saw Michelangelo's paintings on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
I looked around the ballpark to make sure nobody else was there who might have seen that fastball.
But the ballpark was empty.
I signed Sandy Koufax for fourteen grand and a hot dog."
Al Campanis.
Sandy Koufax had a tryout with the Giants and with the Pirates.
Sandy Koufax got a tryout at the Polo Grounds with the Giants;
He got off to a bad start by forgetting his glove and then it got worse as he zipped the ball everywhere, but over the plate.
No interest from Pittsburgh even though during his Pirates’ tryout, Sandy Koufax’s fastball broke the thumb of coach Sam Narron, who caught the tryout.
Branch Rickey, then the GM of the Pirates, said at the time that this kid had the:
"Greatest arm I’ve ever seen."
But the Pirates failed to offer him a contract.
It was a big fail for Pittsburgh.
Imagine Sandy Koufax with Vern Law and Bob Friend as the top of the rotation with ElRoy Face to close.
The Pirates ponied up when they gave Dick Groat $35-40,000 in bonus money back in 1952 and Lauren Pepper $35,000 in 1954.
For that amount or less, they could have had Sandy Koufax!
"Ebbets Field"

Irish historian Kevin Kenny wrote “Throughout the Empire Irish Catholics served as soldiers and administrators, or worked as policemen, doctors, engineers, lawyers, journalists, or businessmen.” 

In 1830, when Ireland accounted for around 30 per cent of the UK’s population, it supplied (according to a study by Peter Karsten) 42 per cent of the soldiers in the British Army.
Ireland also provided around half the East India Company’s recruits prior to the 1857 Mutiny. 

When, following that bloody business, the Crown assumed more or less direct control of India, Irishmen were no less prominent in the new administration. 

Universities in Cork, Galway and Belfast offered courses in Indian languages, history and geography, as did Trinity College Dublin. It wasn’t long before some English officials were grumbling that the Indian Civil Service was run by and for Irishmen.

Duck Hunt: Oregon-Oklahoma State Value

Oregon is a massive favorite, but the spread discrepancy between these two books offers a unique opportunity to capitalize on the line movement. We are looking at the numbers to see if the Ducks can cover the big number or if the Cowboys have enough fight to keep it close.

When you see a spread gap like this, your eyes should immediately go to the hook. FanDuel is hanging Oregon at -23.5, while Caesars is offering Oklahoma State at +22.5. If you believe Oregon wins by exactly three touchdowns, you are essentially getting a free pass by shopping these lines.

From an analytical standpoint, laying over three touchdowns is always a risky proposition in college football, especially with potential garbage-time scores. Oklahoma State has enough talent to find the end zone late, which makes the +22.5 look like the much safer play. By grabbing the points at Caesars, we avoid the dreaded hook and give ourselves a cushion if the Ducks take their foot off the gas in the fourth quarter.

Harvesting Grace, A Forty-Day Devotional by C.S. McDonald is a warm, reflective Christian devotional that invites readers to slow down and reconnect with God’s grace, especially during the beauty of autumn.

Inspired by the author’s love of the fall season—with its vibrant colors, crisp air, and sense of harvest and gratitude—the book offers forty days of gentle spiritual nourishment. Each entry includes a daily Bible verse, a peaceful and thought-provoking observation, and soft reflections designed to refresh faith and cultivate joy. McDonald encourages readers to pause amid life’s busyness, sit quietly or take a walk, and intentionally harvest God’s steadfast love and boundless grace. It serves as a humble, encouraging guide that can be used in autumn or anytime throughout the year. Readers looking for a calming, faith-centered companion will find it uplifting and accessible.

C.S. McDonald taught dance and choreographed shows for twenty-six years before turning to writing. She lives with her husband Bill and their dogs on a Thoroughbred farm near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. text:
There is something deeply contradictory about the way India handles religious figures in its foreign policy.

The Indian state has, for years, objected to foreign powers inserting themselves into Kashmir, particularly when that intervention acquires a religious or political character. Yet we now appear perfectly comfortable facilitating precisely the kind of engagement that we would object to if another state were doing it independently.

The question is not whether an Iranian president can meet an Indian citizen. Of course he can. The question is whether the Indian state should facilitate meetings between foreign heads of state and religious or political figures when the same foreign state has a history of intervening rhetorically in an issue as sensitive as Kashmir.

This is where the BJP’s foreign policy often appears strangely disconnected from its domestic rhetoric. At home, its political language can be uncompromising, particularly on issues involving Israel, Palestine, Kashmir or Islamist politics. Yet in dealing with foreign states, the policy frequently looks far more pragmatic, even when that pragmatism creates contradictions with the positions articulated domestically.

The Taliban offer another example. The BJP’s political ecosystem spent years portraying the Taliban as the very embodiment of Islamist extremism. Yet once geopolitical realities changed, India began engaging with the same Taliban leadership, eventually receiving senior Taliban officials with considerable ceremony. Engagement with a de facto authority can be justified by statecraft. Turning that engagement into a political spectacle is another matter altogether.

The same principle should apply here. Iran is a state. India is a state. Its president is a state guest. The natural interlocutors are therefore representatives of the Indian state. Why should the fact that Iran is governed by a religious establishment lead us to conclude that Indian religious leaders must consequently be brought into the equation?

There is a historical lesson here. Sheikh Abdullah’s invitation to address the United Nations in 1948 remains a reminder of how easily the Indian state can create political complications by elevating individuals whose politics do not necessarily align with the larger national interest. Today, we seem to be repeating the broader habit of confusing political accommodation with strategic wisdom.

The problem is not that a religious leader meets a foreign president. The problem is when the state itself facilitates such encounters without adequately considering what political legitimacy, symbolism or future leverage it may confer.

Foreign policy inevitably involves compromises. But contradictions should not become policy.

A state should know the difference between engaging another state and inadvertently empowering the very political or religious constituencies whose external influence it claims to oppose.

An underground forum post alleges the sale of full administrative access to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) of India's Agniveer recruitment portal, https://t.co/iE0RTimOQ5. The listing, posted on a darkweb marketplace, claims to offer verified admin credentials that provide unrestricted control over the government infrastructure.

- Full admin panel access covering User Management, Org Management, Police Station, Reports, Grievance, Job Applications, Letters, and Import/Export functions
- 2,500+ Agniveer personnel records across 47 government departments
- API decryption keys for all traffic
- SSO integration details and a complete backend route map
- Ready-to-use scripts for exploitation

The seller is demanding $500, with a minimum negotiable price of $300, payable exclusively in cryptocurrency (BTC, LTC, or ETH). The Ministry of Home Affairs is a critical cabinet-level ministry in the Government of India responsible for internal security, law and order, and the administration of central armed forces. The Agniveer scheme is a major national initiative to recruit young soldiers into the Indian Army, making the portal a high-value target for both cybercriminals and state-sponsored actors. Exposure of personnel data and administrative controls could potentially compromise sensitive military recruitment processes and individual privacy.

At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by the Ministry of Home Affairs or other cybersecurity authorities. The existence of such listings on underground forums does not confirm successful compromise; however, the specificity of the claimed access (e.g., specific module names, record counts) warrants immediate investigation by Indian cyber defense agencies.

text: Today is Saragarhi Day.  On 12 September 1897, just 21 Sikh soldiers of the 36th Sikhs, British Indian Army, under Havildar Ishar Singh, defended the isolated signalling post at Saragarhi on the North-West Frontier.  Against them came an estimated 10,000 Afghan/Pashtun tribesmen, principally Afridi and Orakzai, part of the tribal uprising against British rule.  The 21 were offered surrender. They refused. For hours they held the post against repeated assaults, fighting with rifles and finally at close quarters until every defender was dead. All 21 were posthumously awarded the Indian Order of Merit, the highest gallantry decoration then available to Indian soldiers.  Twenty-one Sikhs against roughly 10,000 men.  Saragarhi is one of the great last stands in British military history and a reminder of something too easily forgotten: Sikh soldiers served the British Empire with extraordinary courage and distinction. Their blood is part of our shared history.  Today Britain should remember them

text:
ELON MUSK IS FINALLY BRINGING THE TESLA SEMI TO EUROPE.

IF ITS NUMBERS HOLD, IT COULD REWRITE THE ECONOMICS OF TRUCKING.

IF THE TIMELINE SLIPS AGAIN, IT BECOMES ONE OF TESLA’S LONGEST-RUNNING PROMISES.

Musk unveiled the Semi in 2017 and targeted production for 2019.

That did not happen.

Limited deliveries to customers including PepsiCo began in late 2022. Tesla said the first Semi from its high-volume Nevada line rolled out this April, but its July update removed an earlier forecast for volume production this year.

Now Tesla is preparing its European launch.

The specifications are serious:

40-tonne gross combination weight.
Up to 550 kilometres of range.
About 1 kWh per kilometre.
Three independent rear motors.
Up to 800 kW of drive power.
A tractor weight of roughly 9,100 kilograms.
Up to 60% of range recovered in 30 minutes.

That means approximately 330 kilometres added during one half-hour stop.

But fleet operators do not buy headlines.

They buy cost per kilometre.

Tesla’s efficiency claim makes the calculation simple: 1,000 kilometres would consume roughly 1,000 kWh.

At €0.20 per kWh, that is €200.

For illustration, a diesel truck using 30 litres per 100 kilometres at €1.60 per litre would cost €480 over the same distance.

Potential difference: €280 per 1,000 kilometres—before taxes, charging losses, grid fees and financing.

At 100,000 kilometres per year, that theoretical saving reaches €28,000 per truck.

Electric motors also eliminate the traditional transmission and diesel exhaust-treatment system. Regenerative braking can reduce brake wear.

Tesla offers a 25 kW electric power take-off that can run equipment such as trailer refrigeration.

On paper, this is not merely a cleaner truck.

It is designed to remove categories of operating cost.

But the hard questions begin where the specification sheet ends.

What will it cost?
How much payload remains?
How does range change in winter or mountains?
Can depots power several 800 kW chargers?
How quickly can a damaged truck return to service?

Every idle freight truck is lost revenue and a disrupted route.

Europe is not an empty market. Mercedes-Benz, Volvo, Scania and others already sell electric heavy trucks and understand local fleets and service networks.

Tesla is arriving late.

Its opportunity is to arrive better.

The strongest argument for Semi is integration: truck, charging, route planning, software, diagnostics and energy storage controlled as one system.

The biggest weakness is simple:

Much of the European promise still exists on a webpage rather than at scale on European roads.

Tesla has not published a final regional price or firm delivery schedule. It plans to reveal more at the IAA Transportation show in Hanover.

Watch Musk present the Semi at Tesla’s original delivery event:

https://t.co/3ZFv0C4iwB

The Semi does not need to replace every diesel truck. Regional routes, depot charging and predictable daily mileage could create a large market.

But after nine years, Tesla is no longer being judged on whether the prototype looks possible.

It is being judged on whether thousands of trucks can work profitably, reliably and repeatedly.

That is the real test of Musk’s method: announce an impossible future early, survive years of ridicule, then make the missed deadline irrelevant by delivering something competitors cannot ignore.

Would you trust a Tesla Semi with your company’s freight—or wait until the promises become real fleet data?
