text:
Nellie Wood: Leo Frank, the Indecent Proposal, and the Questionable Defense Affidavit

Nellie Wood’s story in the Leo Frank case is not just about a witness who's story was disputed

It starts with a young working woman saying Leo Frank requested to speak with her alone in his private office, made her sit down, told her nobody was coming into the office, put his hands around her, tried to touch her breast, tried to lift her “lower limbs” and her dress, and caused her to quit the National Pencil Company.

Then, after the murder trial, Wood found herself dealing with investigators, lawyers, offers of work and money to support the defense, questionable affidavits, attacks on her character, and questions about whether she had been arrested or dragged into police court.

By May 1914, she was twenty-two years old, engaged to be married, and telling a courtroom that testimony given about her had “just ruined me.”

That is the side of Nellie Wood’s story I do not want lost because the Frankites often omit those details and dismiss such information more broadly and vaguely as rumors and false accusations.

What Nellie Wood Said Leo Frank Did to Her

Wood said the incident took place about March 1911, roughly two years before the Mary Phagan murder investigation.

She had worked at the National Pencil Company for only two days.

Frank’s private office was on the second floor of the National Pencil Company factory on South Forsyth Street in Atlanta. Wood later specifically said that during the incident:

“nobody was present in his office except Leo M. Frank and myself.” (Official Legal Record, 4)

On Thursday, May 8, 1913, Wood testified under oath at the Mary Phagan coroner’s inquest.

Her testimony survives in the Georgia Supreme Court case files on Microfilm Slides 1772 and 1773.

Wood was asked whether she had seen Frank put his hands on any girls.

Q. Well, tell us what it was.

She answered:

A. Well, he would come around and put his hands on me when it was all uncalled for. (Coroner’s Inquest Record, 1)

She said Frank called her into his office.

Then Wood said something that should not be watered down into “she sat down.”

She said:

“he made me sit down”

and:

“I asked him not to.”

According to Wood, Frank answered that she did not need to be afraid because:

“there wasn’t anybody coming in his office.”

Then, she said:

“he got too familiar with me”

and:

“I thought he got too close to me and I didn’t like that.” (Coroner’s Inquest Record, 1)

The questioning became more direct.

Wood said:

“I resisted him so he didn’t overpower me in any way; just put his hands around me.”

Then came the question about her breast:

Q. Did he put his hands on your breast at all?

A. No, but he tried to, and I guess he would if I hadn’t resented it. (Coroner’s Inquest Record, 1)

The questioning continued:

Q. On your hips at all?
A. No.

Q. Well, did he make any effort at all to pick up your lower limbs?
A. Yes sir.

Q. And your dress?
A. Yes, sir, while I was sitting down talking to him. (Coroner’s Inquest Record, 1)

That is not just Frank being friendly.

That is Wood describing unwanted sexual touching and an effort to get his hands under or around her clothing while the two of them were alone in his office.

When Wood was asked what she did afterward, she said:

“Why, I just quit. I didn’t go back any more until Saturday, and I went back for my money and I found out it didn’t suit me. I thought he had the wrong girl.” (Coroner’s Inquest Record, 1)

That last sentence says a lot in very few words:

“I thought he had the wrong girl.”

She quit.

The Newspapers Reported the Same Basic Story

The next day, Friday, May 9, 1913, the Atlanta Journal and Atlanta Georgian reported Wood’s sworn testimony.

The Atlanta Journal reported Wood saying Frank wanted to close the office door, told her nobody was coming, became too familiar with her, and put his hands on her when there was no reason to do so (AJ, 2).

The Atlanta Georgian reported her saying:

“Well, his actions didn’t suit me. He’d come around and put his hands on me, when such conduct was entirely uncalled for.” (AG, 3)

The Georgian also printed:

“He barely touched my breast.” (AG, 3)

The exact wording differs from the surviving official inquest transcript, which says Frank tried to touch her breast and Wood believed he would have done so had she not resisted.

But both records point in the same direction.

Wood was saying Frank’s conduct toward her was sexual, unwanted, physical, and bad enough that she walked away from the job.

Wood Later Called It an “Indecent Proposal”

The later Georgia Supreme Court record gets even plainer.

Wood stated:

“I told the Solicitor-General before he put me on the stand that I was in the office of Leo M. Frank on one occasion when the said Frank made an indecent proposal to me.” (Official Legal Record, 4)

She added:

“My experience as a trained nurse enabled me to fully understand and know what the said Frank intended.”

Then she described what happened:

“He said, ‘You know I am not like other people’, and drawed his chair closer up to me; says, ‘I don’t think you will understand me’, and put his hands on me, and I resisted and got up and opened the door.” (Official Legal Record, 4)

Frank, according to Wood, then told her he was not going to hurt her and tried to convince her she had misunderstood what he meant.

Again, Wood said the two of them were alone.

This was not the story of Frank accidentally brushing against her in a crowded factory aisle.

Wood placed him alone with her in his private office, moving his chair closer, putting his hands on her, and making what she herself called an:

“indecent proposal.”

Judge Roan Kept Those Details From the Murder Jury

Something else has to be understood.

People sometimes read Wood’s brief appearance during the murder trial on Wednesday, August 20, 1913, and ask why she did not simply stand there and tell the jury all of this.

Solicitor Hugh Dorsey tried.

Frank’s lawyers objected.

The jury was sent out.

Dorsey told Judge Leonard S. Roan exactly what he wanted to prove:

“We want to show that Frank made an indecent proposal to this lady.” (AG, 5)

Dorsey argued that he should be allowed to show what Frank had done to women in the factory.

Judge Roan shut that line down.

The official record says:

“I’ll let you show by this woman or by any other person, bad character on the part of this man, but no specific acts or any specific crimes. That’s the law.” (Official Legal Record, 4)

Dorsey protested:

“Then we are absolutely shut out.”

Roan answered:

“Well, I don’t care, then the law shuts you out, if that’s the case.” (Official Legal Record, 4)

So there it is.

The jury was allowed to hear general reputation evidence about Frank’s character.

They were not allowed to hear Wood stand there and give every detail of what she said Frank personally did to her.

Frank’s Character for Lasciviousness Was Put Directly Into Evidence

Wood was not standing alone.

The official Brief of Evidence lists ten women, most of them former National Pencil Company employees:

Myrtie Cato, Maggie Griffin, Mrs. C. D. Donegan, Mrs. H. R. Johnson, Marie Carst, Nellie Pettis, Mary Davis, Mrs. Mary B. Wallace, Estelle Winkle, and Carrie Smith.

The legal record summarizes their testimony in one sentence:

“Leo M. Frank’s character for lasciviousness was bad.” (Brief of Evidence, 6)

That word, lasciviousness, was not invented a hundred years later.

It is right there in the official trial record.

Lascivious means sexually lustful, lewd, inclined toward improper sexual behavior.

Other words people might use to describe the same kind of conduct are licentious, lewd, or libertine.

I would not pretend the testimony of these women legally proved every specific sexual accusation ever made against Frank.

But I also would not pretend Nellie Wood was some lone woman making an isolated complaint.

The State presented a group of female witnesses who said Frank’s reputation for lasciviousness was bad.

Specific Conduct From Other Women

There was specific testimony behind some of this reputation evidence.

Mamie Kitchens, another National Pencil Company worker, testified that she was in the women’s dressing room with Irene Jackson, who was undressed, when Frank opened the door without knocking, stuck his head inside, stood there and laughed, and then shut the door after Jackson protested. 

On cross-examination Kitchens acknowledged it was during business hours and said Frank asked why they were not working. That qualification belongs in the record, but so does what Kitchens said she saw (Brief of Evidence, 6).

Dewey Hewell testified that she had seen Frank talking to Mary Phagan two or three times a day in the metal department, that Frank called her “Mary,” put his hand on her shoulder, stood close to her, and leaned toward her face. Hewell admitted on cross-examination that other girls were present and that she did not know what they were discussing (Brief of Evidence, 6).

Myrtice Cato and Maggie Griffin testified that they had seen Frank go into the fourth-floor dressing room with forelady Rebecca Carson. Cato said twice. Griffin said three or four times. Carson denied it. So this was disputed testimony, but it was testimony the State put forward as part of the larger character fight (AG, 5).

Nellie Pettis, who was sixteen when her 1914 affidavit was published, continued to say Frank had looked at her in what she called a sly way and once stood close to her and said quietly:

“How about it?”

Her sister-in-law disputed whether the meetings could have happened as Pettis described them, so that conflict also belongs in the record. Pettis herself did not back away from the core allegation (AJ, 7).

Taken one at a time, somebody can argue about each incident.

Taken together with Wood’s own detailed testimony, they are at least evidence from which the prosecution argued that Frank’s behavior around women was not always innocent or proper. 

Then Frank’s Defense Came Back for Nellie Wood

This is where Wood’s experience gets worse.

After the murder trial, she did not just go back to her life.

She became one of the people Frank’s defense wanted an affidavit from.

Wood later said an unidentified man came to see her in an automobile.

She recognized it as the same automobile later used when C. W. Burke, working around the Frank defense investigation, came to see her.

Wood was careful not to accuse Burke of personally making the first money offer.

She said:

“C. W. Burke did not himself ever offer me any money to swear for Leo M. Frank.”

But she said the unidentified first man:

“did make me a proposition to pay me money if I would swear to certain things in favor of Leo M. Frank.” (Official Legal Record, 4)

That is an allegation of an attempted paid inducement to change or shape testimony favorable to Frank.

Then Wood said Burke himself came to see her.

Her words were:

“C. W. Burke afterwards came to see me and told me that the court had ruled out my evidence, and insisted that I should give him an affidavit.” (Official Legal Record, 4)

I keep coming back to one word:

“insisted.”

Wood did not say Burke casually asked whether she wanted to make a statement.

She said he insisted that she give him an affidavit.

The March 1914 Denial Affidavit

Then comes the affidavit published by the Atlanta Journal on Sunday, March 15, 1914.

All of a sudden Nellie Wood’s story is turned upside down.

The woman who had sworn that Frank put his hands around her, tried to touch her breast, tried to lift her lower limbs and dress, and caused her to quit now supposedly said Frank had done nothing improper at all.

The affidavit said Frank had merely patted her shoulder while calming her down.

It described Frank as a:

“perfect gentleman”

and said:

“nothing had taken place during that time upon the part of Mr. Frank that was ungentlemanly, and that Mr. Frank had in no way insulted her.” (AJ, 7)

That is not a small correction.

It is a complete reversal.

The March affidavit even says her dealings with Frank had been:

“upright and manly.” (AJ, 7)

So now we have to ask a simple question.

Which Nellie Wood was telling the truth?

The woman under oath on May 8, 1913, describing unwanted touching in detail?

Or the affidavit obtained by Frank’s defense in 1914, saying Frank was a perfect gentleman?

They cannot both be right.

Was the March Affidavit Pressured, Falsified or Possibly Suborned? It's highly likely because many witnesses came forward to say they were induced into signing false affidavits. 

I think the record gives us good reason to describe the affidavit as pressured.

Wood herself said Burke “insisted” that she give him an affidavit.

She also said another man offered to pay her money if she would swear to things favorable to Frank.

Then there was L. P. Eubanks.

Wood testified that Eubanks telephoned her at home while she was nursing her sick little brother.

Her father and the doctor were there when Eubanks arrived in an automobile.

Wood said Eubanks wanted to speak privately, so he got her into the automobile and drove her to her cousin’s home.

The next day Eubanks introduced her to Burke.

According to Wood:

“Eubanks told me I was a working girl and here was an opportunity for me to make some money if I would go to work on the Frank case for Burke.”

She said Eubanks told her she could make:

“lots of money”

and that she “needed the money and ought to take the work.” (AJ, 8)

That is hard to ignore.

A working woman who had already testified against Frank was being approached privately, taken for a ride in an automobile, introduced to a defense investigator, told she could make “lots of money,” and then asked for an affidavit.

Later, when Frank’s attorney Rosser was questioning her about her work history, Wood snapped:

“Not for you all! I didn’t take what Burke offered me.” (AJ, 8)

Again, I would not write as a proven fact that Burke bribed Nellie Wood or produced a false signature affidavit.

Wood herself specifically said Burke did not make the first money offer.

But I think it is fair to say the circumstances raise a serious question whether the March defense affidavit was pressured, procured under inducement, falsified, or possibly suborned.

The word suborned should be used carefully because it means getting somebody to give false sworn testimony.

We have evidence of pressure.

We have allegations of money.

We have Wood saying Burke “insisted.”

We have Eubanks telling her she could make “lots of money.”

We have Wood later saying:

“I didn’t take what Burke offered me.”

What we do not have is proof that Wood actually accepted money and knowingly swore to a lie.

So I would call it a possibly suborned affidavit, not a proven act of subornation.

Wood Goes Back to Her Original Story

And here is the part that makes the questionable March denial even harder for me to accept at face value.

Wood did not stay with it.

On Friday, May 1, 1914, the Atlanta Georgian reported that Wood and R. P. Barrett had made additional charges that they had been offered money to make statements favorable to Frank. It also reported that Wood repeated her assertions concerning Frank’s bad character and gave more detail concerning the circumstances behind them (AG, 9).

Then on Tuesday, May 5, 1914, Wood appeared in open court during the extraordinary-motion hearing.

She was sworn.

Dorsey asked:

“Why did you quit the pencil factory?”

Wood answered:

“Because I was insulted by Mr. Frank.”

Dorsey asked:

“What was the proposition that Frank made to you?”

Wood hesitated.

Then she said:

“I think the details are unnecessary.” (AJ, 8)

There it is.

In March 1914, the defense's questionable affidavit had Wood saying Frank had “in no way insulted her.”

On May 5, 1914, under oath in open court:

“Because I was insulted by Mr. Frank.”

Both statements cannot be true.

Wood Paid a Price for Getting Involved

Wood’s problem was no longer simply what she said Frank did to her in that second-floor office years earlier.

Now her own name and character were being dragged through the case.

The day before her May 5 appearance, L. P. Eubanks had attacked her character.

The Atlanta Journal reported that Wood went to Solicitor Dorsey’s office in tears and asked permission to answer him publicly.

When asked whether she was engaged to be married, Wood’s voice reportedly became husky.

She said:

“Mr. Eubanks’ false testimony just ruined me.” (AJ, 8)

Then Rosser went after her.

Had she ever been arrested?

Had she ever been taken into police court?

Had she signed anybody’s bond?

Where had she lived?

Where had she worked?

Wood became angry.

At one point she said:

“I am hurt, this morning. I am scandalized.” (AJ, 8)

Wood was twenty-two years old.

She said she was a milliner.

She had worked as a Southern Bell telephone operator and had worked in a cotton mill from a young age.

She was engaged.

And now a sexual complaint she said had happened when she worked only two days at the pencil factory had followed her into one of the most famous criminal cases in Georgia history.

The Defense Went After Her Credibility Hard

The next day, Wednesday, May 6, 1914, Frank’s lawyer Luther Rosser attacked Wood’s credibility before Judge Benjamin Harvey Hill.

Rosser asked the judge to compare Wood’s coroner’s-inquest testimony with her later statements.

Then Rosser said:

“After your honor has made that comparison, then you wouldn’t convict a mosquito on her testimony!” (AJ, 10)

So Wood went from saying Frank had put his hands on her and tried to get under her dress, to being approached for affidavits, to being told she could make money, to being publicly attacked as unreliable.

That is the course of her experience.

Was Leo Frank Lascivious, Licentious, Lewd or Libertine?

The safest historical word is lascivious because that is the word used in the trial record itself.

Ten women were summarized in the official Brief of Evidence as saying:

“Leo M. Frank’s character for lasciviousness was bad.” (Brief of Evidence, 6)

I think the record gives a fair basis to argue that Frank had a reputation among a number of women connected with the factory for lascivious, licentious or lewd behavior.

Nellie Wood’s account is one of the strongest specific examples because she did not just say his reputation was bad.

She described, what she said, he actually did.

She said Frank got her alone.

He made her sit down.

She asked him not to.

He told her nobody was coming.

He put his hands around her.

He tried to touch her breast.

He tried to lift her lower limbs and dress.

She resisted him.

She quit.

She later called it an:

“indecent proposal.”

Then the defense came looking for affidavits.

Wood said somebody offered her money for favorable testimony.

She said Burke “insisted” that she give an affidavit.

Eubanks told her she could make “lots of money.”

A defense affidavit then appeared saying Frank was a “perfect gentleman.”

Within weeks, Wood was back under oath saying:

“Because I was insulted by Mr. Frank.”

I do not think the March 1914 denial affidavit should be allowed to wipe the slate clean.

If anything, its circumstances make me want to look further at how it was obtained.

text:
On this day in history - September 12, 1995 

In Vienna, the Harlem Globetrotters tip off the third game of an 11-game exhibition series in Europe against a team of retired basketball stars led by Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, aptly named “Kareem’s All-Stars.” Unlike the previous 8,829 games, the Globetrotters lose, 91-85—the team’s first loss since 1971. The Globetrotters' games are usually scripted, but this game is not.

Despite being 48 years old, Abdul-Jabbar put the team on his back, scoring 34 points. Bo Kimble, a former college standout and New York Knick, scored 13 points and grabbed eight rebounds. Abdul-Jabbar and Kimble were aided by a handful of other former NBA standouts such as Artis Gilmore, Jo-Jo White, Nate “Tiny” Archibald and 40-year-old Cedric “Cornbread” Maxwell.

The victory had additional significance for Abdul-Jabbar, who was no stranger to the Globetrotters. In 1969, the Globetrotters—known primarily for their on-court antics—reportedly offered him a $1 million contract to play with them after his historic collegiate career at UCLA. Abdul-Jabbar turned the deal down and went onto become the No. 1 pick of the 1969 NBA Draft by the Milwaukee Bucks.

After the win, Abdul-Jabbar complimented the Globetrotters, saying they were “a very good basketball team” and that “they impressed our team with their poise in this loss.”

Meanwhile, the Globetrotters, who had won the first two games of the 11-game series in Switzerland and Germany, took the loss fairly hard. “The guys are really upset,”  Reggie “Regulator” Phillips told the media. “After being part of the team for over 300 straight wins, it is a strange feeling to lose a game.” The Globetrotters defeated the All-Stars in their next “game.”

At the end of this somewhat strange series featuring basketball entertainers and NBA has-beens, Maxwell summed up the experience humorously, telling the New York Times: “You look at us after these games, we are on Tylenol, Excedrin, Advil—all kinds of painkillers, anti-inflammatories. We’re one big pharmaceutical shop. If they do this next year, they ought to look at one of those drugs companies sponsoring it. They can call it the Kareem-Harlem Globetrotters Pain Tour."

HOW TO WRITE A TASK
[] Outcome: what should be finished
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): Grok Bot meters agent steps and tokens, not messages — vague tasks wander and burn the week; scope with Task / Work in / Context / Done means / first N items then stop

[] Next task: one real tool, read-only, with a sign-in handoff if needed
[] After a good result, name the lasting format preference in chat
[] Then save it as a skill or routine
[] Official bot examples: email cleanup, Starlink-likely flights, build a site then buy the domain and deploy, meeting notes, sales prospecting, refunds, podcast audio digest
[] Testers: paste a viral video link and ask the Bot to recreate it
[] Testers: start from an org chart or make one Bot the boss of a repo, not a long to-do list
[] Testers: one clear job, explicit allowed sources, no-guessing rule, approval gate before any real action
[] Testers: 5 calibrations - confidence threshold, checkpoint long tasks, show negative examples, gate destructive actions separately, test edge cases first
[] Testers: one Bot, one job - two jobs claimed worse at both; put recurring work on a schedule
[] Testers quoting claimed SpaceXAI employee: version prompts and tool configs like code; scratchpad separate from the user-facing answer; retry with a different strategy; measure cost per successful outcome; review failure logs on a schedule
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Compound Engineering - force a plan first; three-layer instructions (base, role, current focus); screenshot instead of retyping what's on screen; ping only on a real hit
[] Testers (AlexFinn): anything you are about to do on your computer, ask Grok Bot first
[] Testers (AlexFinn): example week - Reddit microSaaS, 3D digital office to watch Bots, Omarchy setup, product returns, daily AI news post, Cursor cloud-agent bug fixes, X model-release watch, brand-deal negotiation, contract redlines
[] Testers (Michael_Fenech_): give it business responsibilities (checking, chasing, updating, coordinating), not just questions
[] Testers (mattyp, Sep 11): Bot responses now support diagram rendering and LaTeX

AGENT COMPUTER AND LOGINS
[] Open Agent Computer from the conversation to watch the desktop
[] Testers (techdevnotes, Sep 9): Grok Bot Desktop now has Network Debugger
[] SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Sep 10): chat right pane coming — Media, Computer (watch the bot’s screen), and Routines (not live yet)
[] Take over for password, passkey, 2FA, CAPTCHA, payment, or human-only pages
[] Complete only the blocked step, then return control
[] Never paste passwords or one-time codes into chat
[] Official (bot, Sep 8): fill out forms and logins for your Bot without ever leaving the chat, with support for any password manager
[] Testers (XFreeze): when a site needs your account, Bot pauses; you auth with 1Password / Apple Passwords / any manager; Bot continues — no pasting credentials into chat
[] Testers (LaceyPresley / muskonomy): in-chat logins/forms also cover checkouts and booking flights
[] Grok Bot team (poteto, Sep 9): account switching is finally here
[] Official (bot, Sep 9): Share a file directly with Grok Bot on mobile
[] Use a secure secret request when the app offers one
[] Browser sessions persist and are shared across all your Bots
[] Prefer a connector/plugin when one exists; use the browser when it does not
[] Coinbase (coinbase, Sep 9): Coinbase for Agents on Grok — connect Coinbase at https://t.co/aL6KKYjGXH; tell Grok to trade, analyze, automate; no MCP setup
[] Testers (XFreeze, Sep 10): sales/GTM connectors — Salesforce, HubSpot, Gong, Clay, Granola + other GTM tools so Bots can pull account context, research prospects, prepare follow-ups
[] Official (bot, Sep 11): Grok Bot can now search and act across Microsoft Teams for you
[] Testers (SamSokolin): for repeated web-app clicks, reverse-engineer browser-use into scripts (capture network once, call APIs next)
[] Keep durable files in /workspace with clear project folders
[] Settings → Beta: Update Agent Computer (preserve state), Recover, or Reset (can lose recent work)
[] The cloud computer is not your Mac or Windows machine
[] Local-computer execution is separate: Settings → General → Agent → Execution on Local Computer
[] Default local policy is Ask every time; use Never allowed unless you need local files
[] Bookmark testers: give a Bot full local Mac/iMessage access only on a spare machine
[] Testers: local Mac access can write local Python scripts on your Mac
[] Testers (Av1dlive / mvanhorn): Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor claimed runnable on the Bot's own computer
[] Testers (XFreeze): take over that same cloud computer from your phone without being at the laptop
[] Testers (Damir_Akaza): group-chat Bots can reach a local Mac Mini via Tailscale for project files and local scripts
[] Testers (farzyness): a Bot can exclusively use Grok Build in CLI with the latest Grok models at highest thinking
[] Testers (AlexFinn): a 3D digital office on a second monitor to watch Bots work

PLUGINS AND CONNECTORS
[] Settings → Plugins, then Add, then authenticate in the browser
[] Grok Bot team (poteto): tinkabot helps build MCP/skills plugins and submit them for approval so all users can use them
[] Type @ to attach a connector; type / to reference a saved skill
[] Installed connectors are account-wide, not isolated to one Bot
[] Official: you can connect multiple accounts to the same plugin
[] Official bot (Aug 26): SuperGrok and Cursor Pro now included; weekly limits reset. Testers quoting SpaceXAI: also Plus/Heavy/Pro+/Ultra/Teams
[] Testers: give a Bot its own email address so it can send and receive on its own
[] Testers (mvanhorn): give a Bot its own inbox, not your Gmail (one mistake should not flag your domain); Twilio number so a Bot can make calls
[] Testers: app v0.23.0 adds creating new channels
[] Official bot: improved X support - connect your X profile; a developer account is auto-created with included credits
[] Testers (blankspeaker): Plugins, add X, authenticate; $100 in X API credits good for a year (new and existing devs)
[] Testers (GrokInsider): if credits did not land, ask Grok Bot to connect X so the Authorize card opens the browser; tester's manual plugin add failed
[] Follow the Connect card when a Bot asks for a plugin
[] Bookmark testers: X connector may still need a paid X API key in some setups (official path now auto-creates a developer account with credits)
[] Bookmark testers: image generation works; testers now also claim video editing (music sync). Video generation still unconfirmed. Testers (XFreeze): dedicated video-editor Bot for footage → clips/cuts/sound/titles
[] Bookmark testers: Grok Bot can now read your X bookmarks
[] Testers (testerlabor): you can link your X Premium+ subscription to Grok Bot
[] Testers: Higgsfield x Grok Bot; 100 free credits for new users
[] Testers: send a YouTube link with start/end timestamps and get an HD clip in chat (Google login claimed)
[] Testers: give a Bot Grok Build + Cursor CLI so weekly limits can be spread across Cursor and Grok

[] Grok Bot team (poteto) + testers (XFreeze): Microsoft connectors live - Outlook, Outlook Calendar, OneDrive (search/send email, drafts, schedules, meetings, browse/upload files)
[] Testers (XFreeze): Bot can natively generate images with Grok Imagine Image 2.0 inside the workflow (no separate Imagine tab)
SKILLS AND ROUTINES
[] Skill = reusable how-to (steps, rules, output, approval boundary)
[] Routine = when to run that work (schedule or event)
[] Do the task once, make it reliable, save a skill, then automate
[] Teach a task: open computer view, choose Teach a task, demo up to 10 minutes, review the draft skill
[] Teaching records the screen, not microphone audio; do not expose secrets while teaching
[] If Teach a task is missing, ask the Bot to write a skill from the completed work
[] Create a routine on the Bot that should own the job
[] Confirm owner, schedule, time zone, input, result, approval, and missing-data behavior
[] Event triggers (Slack, GitHub) are separate from plugins and need their own connection
[] Keep event matchers narrow; avoid every new message
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): never trigger on every new message (docs warn broad listeners eat usage); pick one channel and one keyword; audit forgotten dailies
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): add to every routine — if the source is unavailable, report the failure instead of using old data; test run before you schedule
[] Test run does real work; use safe inputs
[] Testers quoting docs: Test can send real emails to real clients; Stop is a brake, not a rewind
[] View conversation details → Routines to pause, edit, inspect, or delete
[] A Bot can own 50 routines; last 20 run records are kept
[] Deleting a routine has no undo
[] Testers quoting docs: delete a Bot and every routine on it dies; no undo
[] Long absence can pause unattended routines until you confirm
[] Bookmark testers: Teach a task from + in the browser, record yourself, then let the Bot replay it
[] Testers: skills taught to one bot claimed available across the account team on the same computer
[] Official Elon: how to share your Grok Bot design with others
[] Testers: a reusable-skills source claimed (BrianRoemmele)
[] Testers quoting Grok Bot team (0xMorlex): keep recurring routines off the main agent's context
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Teach by recording and respect the 10-minute cap

MULTI BOT TEAMS
[] Start with one Bot that owns an end-to-end outcome
[] Add a specialist only when the role is stable
[] Use a group chat when the handoff itself should be visible
[] SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker): v0.44.0 worked on using a Grok Bot with more than one person
[] Bots can message each other and pass ownership
[] Do not treat separate Bots as a security boundary (they share the computer)
[] Keep sending, buying, deleting, publishing, and production changes behind approval
[] Bookmark testers: a Bot may create other Bots before it can delete them
[] Bookmark testers: tell a hub Bot to loop a specialist every few minutes and watch it
[] Testers: put Bots in one group chat, appoint a Chief of Staff, and stop being the router
[] Testers (farzyness): one master agent owns specialists + chat rooms and pings you one action item at a time
[] Testers: isolate each Bot's job and add a supervisor; a crew without that can perform worse
[] Testers: night-shift crews (chief, scout, forge, critic, ship, ledger) share one computer; human gate for merge, production, spend, send, delete
[] Testers: one group chat per job/post, not per Bot; you only message the Chief of Staff
[] Testers: show the workflow once on screen rather than writing a long spec
[] Testers: add a RED TEAM Bot whose job is to disprove the thesis; no single source closes a claim
[] Testers quoting Grok Bot team (0xMorlex): specialist roles (designer/engineer/PM); organize projects without a new Bot for everything; a Chief of Agents that creates and manages the rest
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Bot Advisor whose only job is building and tightening other Bots; files are the memory bus between Bots
[] Testers (Damir_Akaza): 4 Bots in one group chat split a Meta ads campaign (creatives, fact-check, deploy) with autonomous handoff

[] Testers (cminshall): overnight group of five Bots one-shotted an admin UI from PRD/FRD/prototype PNGs
IOS
[] Same Bots, chats, routines, plugins, and cloud computer as desktop
[] Testers (mattyp): Grok Bot supports 21+ localized languages on mobile
[] Send text, dictate, attach photos/files, mention Bots, reply in threads
[] Take over the computer for login/2FA from the phone
[] You can pause or resume a routine on iOS
[] Editing schedule, run history, test, delete, and teach-by-demo still need desktop
[] Enable notifications for results, questions, and approvals
[] Testers: phone notification shows the proposed action; approve or deny
[] Testers (XFreeze): you can operate and take over the Bot's computer from your phone as long as it has internet
[] Grok Bot team (poteto, earlier): had pointed at Play pre-registration; superseded by Official bot Sep 2 Android launch

APPROVALS AND SAFETY
[] Put the stop line in the request: draft, do not send; ask after showing current vs proposed
[] Official (bot, Sep 9): ask your Bot to draft messages inline for you to approve before sending
[] Official Elon (elonmusk, Sep 10): amplify Grok Bot draft-before-send QoL
[] Desktop: Allow once, Deny, or Always allow a matching rule
[] iPhone: Approve once or Deny
[] Auto Review: Settings → General → Auto-review
[] Require Approval beats Always Allow when both match
[] Write narrow rules, not allow everything in the browser
[] Do not approve an action you cannot identify
[] Connect only the tools the workflow needs
[] Start read-only; keep spend, send, publish, delete, and production behind approval
[] Sign out and revoke connectors when access should end
[] Deleting a Bot does not wipe shared files or browser sessions
[] Bookmark testers: delay standing inbox/CRM access until you trust the beta
[] Bookmark testers: one person burned a 7-day quota in about 8 hours
[] Testers (daveginvesting): burned a week of tokens in about 2 hours on first try
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): check Weekly usage in the account menu before any big run; one long job can eat an entire trial credit
[] Bookmark testers: SuperGrok may offer one-off usage resets in settings; use before they expire
[] Testers: gate destructive actions (delete, overwrite, irreversible send) as their own confirmation, not lumped with routine tool use
[] Testers quoting docs: Test run does real work; Stop does not unsend
[] Testers quoting Elon (cb_doge): connecting a Bot to a bank account; Elon said any loss from a bot mistake would be covered. Still keep spend behind approval
[] Official bot Link shopping: keep purchases behind approval even though the Bot can complete them on your behalf
[] Official Elon: Grok Bot buys a Tesla
[] Testers (mvanhorn): unsupervised crews claimed to multiply their own errors ~17x; draft-then-approve anything that sends; most Bots that don't own an outcome fail
[] Testers (antpalkin): end every agent's job with a hard never-without-asking list; give one Bot veto/kill power whose no beats the rest of the desk

FIRST BOTS WORTH CREATING
[] Inbox manager for email and Slack triage
[] Calendar and reservation Bot
[] Research and daily brief Bot
[] Coding Bot that can launch Cursor cloud agents
[] Testers (AlexFinn): pair a developer Bot (Cursor cloud agents + PRs) with a PM Bot on Notion/Linear that feeds tasks and grants permission — software-factory loop
[] Chief-of-staff hub that routes work to specialists
[] Personal errands Bot (tickets, food, travel, forms)
[] Content Bot that drafts in your voice for approval
[] Chief-of-staff that researches you, organizes the other Bots, and can turn the digest into a morning podcast
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Bot Advisor; own-inbox Bot; a call Bot with its own number
[] Testers (techdevnotes): default Bots circulating - Night Shift (overnight digest), Inbox Triage, Chief of Staff, Negotiator, Prototyper, Researcher, Shopper, Apartment Scout, Lookout, Competitor Watcher
[] Testers (techdevnotes): also tool-specific sales/ops/dev roles (CRM scribe, pipeline scout, ticket triager, QA, dashboard watcher)
[] Official bot + Link: Shopper Bot can now complete online purchases once link is connected (keep approval on)
[] Testers / SpaceXAI (kiaraplds): flights, tickets, groceries - delegate errands safely to your Bot
[] Testers (minchoi): one-person-company setups - money, appointments, running ops from the phone
[] Testers (niccruzpatane): Accounting Bot (invoices, spending, bills); Personal Bot (flights, rides, Airbnb, Google Calendar, Amazon orders/returns); Home Bot (lights, robots, speakers, thermostats)
[] Testers (GrokBotDev): Jess (email/calendar/Notion/Slack recap), Marketing Bot, Prospecting Sheet Builder, Reaper (kill unused subs/meetings), Human Copywriter
[] Testers (JasonL_Capital): 8 options-trading Bots (scan puts, price LEAPS, run the wheel) with copy-paste prompts
[] Testers (Michael_Fenech_): start in recruitment, e-comm, real estate, accounting, legal, SaaS, agencies, trades, founder ops

EVENTS
- Testers (cb_doge): Grok Bot Galaxy three-day event Sep 15–17 at The Howard, 661 Howard St, San Francisco (in person or livestream, 8:45am–6:00pm): create/customize Bots, teach style/goals, workflows by role, meet the team

🎿❄️ THE MOST IMPORTANT PIECE OF SKI EQUIPMENT ISN'T ALWAYS ATTACHED TO YOUR FEET.

Your skis can be incredible.

Your boots can be perfectly fitted.

Your goggles can cost $300.

But if your jacket leaves you:

Cold.

Wet.

Sweaty.

Restricted.

Or miserable halfway through the day...

YOUR SKI DAY IS BASICALLY OVER.

😂

That's why I think:

https://t.co/eMwOA7eIRk

has a very clear commercial opportunity.

I wouldn't build another generic winter-clothing store.

I'd build:

🎿 THE GLOBAL SEARCH + SHOPPING ENGINE FOR SKI JACKETS.

One category.

One obsession.

One promise:

FIND THE JACKET BUILT FOR YOUR MOUNTAIN.™

And the category is big enough to justify specialization. The global snow-apparel market is estimated at $26.8B in 2026, with skiing representing more than 60% of 2025 revenue and top-wear more than 65%. In North America alone, ski apparel was estimated at $2.27B in 2024, with outerwear accounting for more than half of revenue. (Grand View Research)

🔥🔥🔥

🏔️ JACKET FINDER™

Don't begin with:

MEN / WOMEN / BRAND / PRICE.

Start with:

WHERE DO YOU SKI?

Québec?

Colorado?

Whistler?

Utah?

Alps?

Japan?

Then:

How cold?

How hard do you ski?

Resort or backcountry?

Do you run hot?

Do you want insulation?

How important is weight?

Budget?

Fit?

Now recommend:

THE RIGHT JACKET FOR THE CONDITIONS.

Because the best ski jacket for:

-20°C at Mont-Sainte-Anne

isn't necessarily the best jacket for:

A wet +2°C day at Whistler.

🔥

🌡️ TEMP MATCH™

This could become the signature feature.

Choose:

🥶 EXTREME COLD

❄️ COLD

🌨️ WET SNOW

☀️ SPRING SKIING

🏃 HIGH OUTPUT

Then SkiingJacket matches:

Insulation.

Shell construction.

Breathability.

Ventilation.

Layering strategy.

Weather protection.

Finally:

SHOP BY WEATHER.

Not marketing jargon.

💧 STAY DRY™

10K.

20K.

30K.

GORE-TEX.

3L.

2L.

DWR.

Membrane.

Seam taped.

😂

Most buyers see this stuff and think:

OKAY... BUT WILL I GET WET?

SkiingJacket translates technical specifications into:

Light snowfall.

Wet chairlift.

Storm skiing.

All-day exposure.

Backcountry.

Then explains:

WHY IT MATTERS.

🔥🔥🔥

💨 BREATHABILITY MATCH™

A warmer jacket isn't automatically:

A better jacket.

Aggressive skier?

Touring?

Hiking terrain?

Spring conditions?

You may need:

LESS INSULATION + MORE BREATHABILITY.

SkiingJacket should understand the skier.

Not simply the temperature.

That's where specialization beats a generic clothing marketplace.

🧥 SHELL OR INSULATED?™

The eternal question.

SkiingJacket asks:

Do you layer?

Do you run cold?

Do you ski mostly lifts?

Do you tour?

What climate?

Then:

SHELL

or:

INSULATED

or:

3-IN-1

with an explanation.

No gear-snob nonsense.

😂

Just:

WHAT WORKS FOR YOU?

🎯 JACKET MATCH™

Imagine:

Arc'teryx — 94% match

Helly Hansen — 92%

Patagonia — 89%

Norrona — 87%

But not because one brand paid more.

Because the jacket matches:

Climate.

Ski style.

Fit.

Budget.

Features.

Now SkiingJacket becomes:

DECISION INTELLIGENCE FOR OUTERWEAR.

🔥

⚖️ COMPARE JACKETS™

Put two jackets side by side.

Waterproofing.

Breathability.

Insulation.

Weight.

Vents.

Powder skirt.

Hood.

Pockets.

Pass pocket.

RECCO where offered.

Fit.

Price.

Warranty.

Sustainability attributes.

Then:

BEST FOR YOU.

Not:

“Both are excellent choices.”

😂

Tell me why one wins.

💰 PRICE WATCH™

Found the jacket?

$799.

No thanks.

😂

Set:

BUY UNDER $599.

SkiingJacket watches participating retailers.

Sale appears.

Last year's color gets discounted.

Price drops.

Alert:

YOUR JACKET JUST HIT YOUR PRICE.

Now you've created a reason to return.

🔥🔥🔥

🏷️ LAST SEASON™

This could be an entire business.

The technology may still be excellent.

The color changed.

The logo moved 3 centimeters.

MSRP:

$800.

Last-season inventory:

$479.

😂

For many skiers:

THAT'S THE DEAL.

Create a dedicated marketplace for:

Previous-season premium ski jackets.

Closeouts.

Outlet inventory.

Overstock.

Verified new-old-stock.

Suddenly SkiingJacket isn't only helping people find:

The best jacket.

It's helping them find:

THE BEST VALUE.

💎 PREMIUM JACKET™

Other buyer?

Doesn't care about price.

Wants:

Best materials.

Best construction.

Best protection.

Best fit.

Best durability.

Best design.

Give them:

NO-COMPROMISE OUTERWEAR.

Premium ski apparel is projected to outgrow the broader North American category through 2030, while online ski-apparel sales are also expected to expand faster than the overall market. (Grand View Research)

That's exactly where a specialist commerce brand can live.

👩 WOMEN'S FIT™

Don't treat women's jackets as:

MEN'S JACKET, BUT PINK.

😂

Fit.

Torso.

Mobility.

Layering.

Pocket placement.

Sizing.

Style.

Different needs.

Women's snow-sports apparel has also been forecast to grow faster than the overall category. (Grand View Research)

Build genuinely useful:

FIT INTELLIGENCE.

👦 KIDS SKI™

Parents have different questions:

Will it stay warm?

Is it waterproof?

Can it survive two kids?

Room to grow?

Helmet-compatible hood?

Easy pockets?

Bright enough to see on the hill?

Budget?

Now:

FIND THE JACKET THE PARENT WANTS TO BUY.

🔥🔥🔥

📏 PERFECT FIT™

This is one of e-commerce's biggest opportunities.

Height.

Weight.

Chest.

Waist.

Arm length.

Preferred fit.

Base layers.

Midlayer.

Then:

YOUR SIZE: LARGE

But maybe:

Brand A → Large

Brand B → XL

Brand C → Large, relaxed

That's much more useful.

Online snow-sports apparel is expected to keep gaining share, helped by better product information, sizing and return experiences. (Grand View Research)

So solve the uncertainty.

FIT BETTER. RETURN LESS.™

📸 FIT CHECK™

Upload photo.

Optional measurements.

AI-assisted fit recommendation.

Then visualize:

Slim.

Regular.

Relaxed.

Long.

No pretending the prediction is perfect.

Show:

CONFIDENCE.

That's important.

🔥

🎒 BACKCOUNTRY™

Different world.

Weight.

Packability.

Breathability.

Helmet hood.

Harness compatibility.

Durability.

Weather protection.

Touring ventilation.

Now SkiingJacket can create:

BACKCOUNTRY JACKET FINDER™

for serious users.

⛷️ RESORT™

Chairlift.

Wind.

Cold.

Snowmaking.

Long days.

Phone.

Pass.

Goggles.

Gloves.

Lunch.

😂

Resort skier may prioritize:

Warmth.

Comfort.

Storage.

Durability.

Weatherproofing.

Ski-pass pocket.

Powder skirt.

Different environment.

Different recommendation.

🏂 FREERIDE™

Loose fit.

Mobility.

Storm protection.

Helmet hood.

Durability.

Style.

Longer cut.

Big pockets.

Now the taxonomy becomes:

HOW YOU SKI.

Not merely:

What size are you?

🔥🔥🔥

🌨️ STORM JACKET™

Powder day tomorrow.

Weather forecast:

Heavy snow.

High wind.

Cold.

SkiingJacket says:

THESE ARE THE JACKETS I'D WANT TOMORROW.

That's content + commerce combined.

☀️ SPRING JACKET™

Bluebird.

+5°C.

You're going to cook in that giant insulated jacket.

😂

Recommend:

Shell.

Ventilation.

Lightweight protection.

Layer strategy.

The product becomes seasonal and contextual.

🤖 SKI AI™

Ask naturally:

“I'm skiing Banff in February. I get cold easily, ski mostly groomers, don't do backcountry, and have about $600.”

Ski AI returns:

Three jackets.

Why each fits.

What size to investigate.

What layer setup makes sense.

Best current value.

Potential tradeoffs.

That's much better than:

1,247 RESULTS.

🔥

🌤️ PACK FOR THE MOUNTAIN™

Trip booked?

Enter:

Resort.

Dates.

SkiingJacket checks forecast closer to departure and builds:

Shell.

Midlayer.

Base layer.

Gloves.

Neck warmer.

Pants.

Goggles.

Now the domain begins with jackets...

but naturally expands into:

SKI CLOTHING INTELLIGENCE.

🧅 LAYER BUILDER™

Jacket alone isn't warmth.

Build:

BASE

MID

OUTER

based on:

Temperature.

Activity.

Wind.

Moisture.

Personal cold tolerance.

Then:

YOUR SYSTEM.

This creates natural cross-sell without turning the site into:

Random sporting goods.

🔥🔥🔥

♻️ SECOND RUN™

Premium ski jackets can have long usable lives.

Build authenticated/condition-graded resale.

Excellent.

Very good.

Good.

Repair needed.

Now someone sells:

$900 jacket.

Someone buys:

$350 jacket.

SkiingJacket earns:

Marketplace fee.

And the product stays on the mountain.

♻️ REPAIR IT™

Broken zipper?

Torn shell?

Damaged cuff?

Lost snap?

Don't immediately say:

BUY ANOTHER JACKET.

Connect:

Manufacturer repair.

Authorized repair.

Technical garment repair.

Local specialists.

That's good sustainability.

And good brand trust.

🌱 IMPACT VIEW™

Where credible information exists, show:

Recycled content.

PFAS-related disclosures.

Repairability.

Warranty.

Manufacturing certifications.

Durability.

But don't create fake:

GREEN SCORE: 97!!!

😂

Show facts.

Let users decide.

🔥

🏆 JACKET OF THE YEAR™

Editorial authority.

Best resort jacket.

Best shell.

Best value.

Best women's.

Best backcountry.

Best cold-weather.

Best premium.

Best under $300.

Best last-season deal.

Now SkiingJacket builds:

CONTENT THAT CONVERTS.

🎥 JACKET TEST™

Real testing.

Wet snow.

Wind.

Chairlift.

Touring.

Cold.

Pocket usability.

Hood.

Ventilation.

Mobility.

Durability.

Then:

WE SKIED IT.

Not:

We read the manufacturer description.

😂

That distinction can create a trusted media brand.

🔥🔥🔥

📍 SKI SHOP NEAR ME™

Need it today?

Find:

Local inventory.

Size.

Color.

Price.

Store.

Distance.

Then:

RESERVE & TRY ON.

Online discovery.

Physical fitting.

Local purchase.

That's a strong bridge because specialty stores still account for a major share of ski-apparel commerce and consumers value expert advice and fit evaluation. (Grand View Research)

🏔️ RESORT DELIVERY™

Forgot your jacket?

Luggage lost?

Weather colder than expected?

😂

You're in Whistler.

Find jacket.

Choose size.

Deliver to:

Hotel.

Condo.

Resort.

Or reserve nearby.

Now SkiingJacket owns a very high-intent moment:

text:
Harvesting Grace, A Forty-Day Devotional by C.S. McDonald is a warm, reflective Christian devotional that invites readers to slow down and reconnect with God’s grace, especially during the beauty of autumn.

Inspired by the author’s love of the fall season—with its vibrant colors, crisp air, and sense of harvest and gratitude—the book offers forty days of gentle spiritual nourishment. Each entry includes a daily Bible verse, a peaceful and thought-provoking observation, and soft reflections designed to refresh faith and cultivate joy. McDonald encourages readers to pause amid life’s busyness, sit quietly or take a walk, and intentionally harvest God’s steadfast love and boundless grace. It serves as a humble, encouraging guide that can be used in autumn or anytime throughout the year. Readers looking for a calming, faith-centered companion will find it uplifting and accessible.

About the author
C.S. McDonald taught dance and choreographed shows for twenty-six years before turning to writing. She lives with her husband Bill and their dogs on a Thoroughbred farm near Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. She is the author of the popular clean Fiona Quinn Mysteries (cozy mysteries featuring a kindergarten teacher turned sleuth) and the Owl’s Nest Mysteries, as well as children’s books inspired by farm life. In recent years she has added devotionals, including *Harvesting Grace*, as part of her spiritual writing. She is a wife, mom, grandma, dog lover, and self-described helpless chocoholic.

#AI #Science
 AI trained to 'think' like human pathologists may be better at spotting cancer  https://t.co/mqU7SfCzLf

Artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms that hunt for cancer may do a better job when they approach the analysis as if they were a human pathologist, a new study suggests.

Many AI systems analyze preselected regions of a tissue sample, or they split a whole pathology slide into patches of a fixed size. By contrast, a pathologist searches more dynamically, panning across the tissue, zooming in and out, and pausing over areas that raise red flags. A whole slide can contain billions of pixels, while the evidence of cancer may occupy only a tiny patch.

Study co-author Zhi Huang, an assistant professor of pathology and laboratory medicine at the University of Pennsylvania, compared the process to a search-and-rescue helicopter. "You don't start by inspecting one square meter of ground," Huang told Live Science. You scan the landscape first and then swoop in for a closer look.

In the new study, published in July in the journal Nature, Huang and colleagues demonstrated that cancer-detecting AI might work better when it takes this humanized approach.

Training AI to hunt for cancer

AI algorithms called vision language models (VLMs) struggle with the first step that Huang described — that initial, cursory scan. That's in part because many pathology AI systems learn from what pathologists leave behind at the end of that search: a labeled image pointing out where the cancer is or an official diagnosis. 

Instead, the researchers trained their new AI on pathologists' search behavior. They called this approach to training "Pathology-CoT," short for "chain of thought." It turns observable actions, including where pathologists move around and zoom in on an image, into training data.

To collect the data, the team created a tool that recorded how pathologists moved around a slide and changed magnification. The raw logs, gathered from eight pathologists, were messy, as a given pathologist might drift across a slide, overshoot their intended region of focus or fiddle with magnification to adjust it to their liking. 

To clean up the data, the researchers filtered out those incidental movements, focusing on  moments that appeared to represent deliberate attention, such as lingering over one view or making a sustained pan. Then, they compared those regions with eye-tracking data to check that the software was capturing where pathologists were actually looking.

For each region a pathologist inspected, the VLM also drafted a short rationale explaining why the region was worth examining and what features were visible; human pathologists could then accept, edit, or reject the rationale, creating additional training data for the AI. In one example, the AI flagged a portion of a slide as potentially metastatic and suggested zooming in to look for atypical cells. Other inspected regions were flagged as healthy tissue.

Ultimately, the researchers used this training method to build a new tool called Pathology-o3. It scans a slide at low resolution, uses a model trained on pathologists' behavior to choose regions worth a closer look, then sends higher-resolution views of those regions to a VLM for analysis.

Pathology-CoT trains algorithms to scan over a whole slide and then return to regions of interest for a closer look. (Image credit: Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Putting it to the test

Huang said the goal of the new study was not to show that Pathology-o3 worked better than specialized AI models that are specifically built to detect specific types of cancer; those models are often trained disease by disease. Rather, the researchers wanted to see whether their new training approach could help a general-purpose AI navigate a pathology slide more effectively.

They compared Pathology-o3 to other general-use AI systems, such as OpenAI's o3, and asked the algorithms to examine slides containing lymph node tissue. These slides were collected from colorectal cancer cases and some contained metastatic cancer, which human pathologists had already labeled.

The algorithm correctly identified slides that were positive for cancer 100% of the time. However, of the slides it identified as positive, 15.5% were actually negative. By comparison, OpenAI o3 correctly identified slides that were positive for cancer 87.5% of the time. Of the slides it identified as positive, 53.3% were actually negative.

The researchers designed Pathology-o3 to err on the side of flagging something for another look, rather than potentially missing cancer. That might help to explain the rate of false positives, Huang said.

Whether that rate of false alarms is acceptable depends on how Pathology-o3 is used, said Mohammad Asadi, a data scientist at Stanford University who was not involved in the research. It's not precise enough for the AI to diagnose patients on its own, but it could still be useful for a system to point a human toward regions of a slide that are worth double-checking. It may be an advantage that the approach shows the pathologist a specific region to inspect rather than declaring an entire slide suspicious, he said.

The researchers tried repeating the test on an independent dataset that the algorithms hadn't seen before to see how well it worked on unfamiliar slides. Pathology-o3 correctly identified slides that were positive for cancer 97.6% of the time. Of the slides it identified as positive, 37.1% were actually negative. The finding is an example of how AI performance can change when the data source changes, even when the medical task stays the same.

Asadi explained this result suggests the system can still work with slides from a different source. But that result does not yet show that using this tool would make pathologists more accurate or efficient in practice.

Can it help pathologists?

The researchers applied their training approach to several existing VLMs, finding that the models' performance consistently improved after the training. That suggests that the navigation data from pathologists was useful across settings, Asadi said.

For Huang, that is the most important result. "The takeaway isn't our system," he said. "It's that the missing ingredient has been sitting in hospitals this whole time."

The study did not compare Pathology-o3 directly with human pathologists, but the researchers said that wasn't their aim. 

Related stories

More young people are getting colorectal cancer — here's what scientists think might be happening

When is cancer considered cured, versus in remission?

New AI model spots pancreatic cancer up to 3 years earlier than human doctors in test

"The right question isn't whether it beats a pathologist," Huang said. "It's whether a pathologist working with it catches more [cancer cases] and works faster."  The current study did not address the latter question, either, but the team's next experiment is designed to test pathologists on the same cases with and without Pathology-o3, measuring what they catch and how long they take to do so.

The system's most plausible use is as a prescreening tool, Asadi said, but he stressed that the research has not yet shown that doctors who use it become faster or more accurate. Asadi wants an even tougher test: trials conducted across multiple hospitals that measure not just accuracy and speed but also pathologists' workloads. He wants the trails to assess the burden of false alarms from the AI algorithms and whether doctors recognize when the AI is wrong.

Importantly, cancer diagnoses can require information from multiple slides, stains and a patient's medical history, while the current system just reads one slide at a time. "I wouldn't claim it should diagnose on its own," Huang said.

- Testers ($SPCX folder, Sep 8–12): unlock mechanics (319M shares / ~17% float; another 59.1M unlock; next unlock Sep 24; price talk ~$140–$154 peaks; Sep 11 close above $150 / +~$16 vs IPO per testers). Desk talk of NASDAQ-100 add / ~$12.4B passive buy (tester markflowchatter). Compute GW talk: >2 GW YE / 5–10 GW next year; SpaceXAI ~$3.43B/mo from Dec 1 framed toward $100B ARR (testers). - Full Starship vehicle/flight detail lives in the separate Starship note. This note only keeps what these folders say.

FALCON / LAUNCHES
- Official SpaceX (Sep 10): USSF-153 Falcon 9 from California — propellant load / weather ~70% favorable. Testers (XFreeze, Sep 11): USSF-153 launched successfully from Vandenberg; B1081 27th flight, landed on Of Course I Still Love You — Testers for launch/landing claim (no Official launch confirm in this dump). Testers also cite 658 successful Falcon booster landings (DimaZeniuk).
- Testers (Aug 26): 101st Falcon 9 of 2026 from Vandenberg with 27 Starlink; B1082 24th flight; droneship Of Course I Still Love You. Testers pair it with a Florida “100th” ~24h earlier — cadence labels remain Testers only; no Official “101st” post in this dump.
- Testers (Aug 25): 100th Falcon 9 of 2026 on a Florida 29-sat Starlink; Official posts confirm that launch/deployment but not the “100th” label. Prior dump testers dated a “100th Falcon” around Aug 22 (California 27-sat) — tester cadence labels conflict; do not treat as Official.
- Testers: last planned Falcon 9 Starlink from Florida (Starlink 10-49); F9 Starlink continues from Vandenberg; Florida framed as shifting to Starship. B1067 record 37th flight and droneship landing.
- Testers (SERobinsonJr): B1067 at Port Canaveral after that 37th flight/landing from Starlink 10-49. Testers also spotted droneships ASOG and JRTI plus a newly added Starship transport barge You’ll Thank Me Later (Marmac 31). Testers only.
- Testers (XFreeze, prior dump): Falcon family ~681 F9 + 12 FH; individual boosters flown 36× (this dump: 37×). Dual Falcon 9s 38.5 minutes apart (record). Regular Starlink cadence from Cape and Vandenberg.
- Elon (Mar 2026): over 500 rocket landings; Falcon 9 ~20 tons to orbit with reusable booster and fairing; delivered 119 satellites in one launch.
- Testers quoting Elon: Falcon 9 retired when Starship flies reliably several times/week; no new Falcon bookings past 2028; some expendable hardware production already stopped — Testers.
- Testers (VladSaigau / BassonBrain, prior): Falcon 9 list ~$70–74M; tester reuse-cost models — not Official.
- Official SpaceX (Dec 2025): approval to develop SLC-37 at Cape Canaveral for Starship; construction started; three Florida pads framed for airport-like ops.
- Elon (May 2026): considering several domestic and international sites for advanced spaceports.
- Testers: classified USSF-366 from Vandenberg; analysts say likely Starshield. Official Q2: >$6B multi-year U.S. Starshield contracts.
- Testers (cb_doge / XFreeze, Space Force filing): new PLEO firm-fixed-price task order (awarded July 28, published Aug 25) for Starshield aviation. At least 500 Mbps down / 100 Mbps up, worldwide, Tile + Tile Mini on cargo through fighters; one-year base through July 2027 plus option through July 2028. Testers say Space Force called SpaceX the only capable provider; value and aircraft count redacted. Not Official.
- Official SpaceX (Jun 2026): Starfall demo — new recoverable microgravity / in-space manufacturing return vehicle; deployment confirmed; splashdown in the Pacific.
- Official SpaceX: NASA Roman Space Telescope encapsulated in Falcon Heavy; launch Sunday Aug 30 from pad 39A. Testers: ~$4.3B payload, 7:26 a.m. EDT. Testers this dump: ~8 months ahead of schedule and under budget; Falcon Heavy “then and now” framing.

STARSHIP
- Testers quoting SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen (Goldman Communacopia, Sep 10): Flight 14 later this month framed as revenue-generating — first operational Starlink V3s on Starship. Testers only for the quote framing; not an Official SpaceX post in this dump.
- Testers (wvmattz / SERobinsonJr): Ship 42 (Flight 15) emerged from MB2 / left Massey’s short stay and returning to production; road-delay transport talk Sep 10–11. Testers (FelixSchlang, Sep 11): Ship 42 lifted at Pad 2 — framed as alignment test for post-catch ops. Testers only.
- Testers (MarcusHouse): Pad 1 new roof + black sides lifted into place at Starbase (Sep 9). Testers only.
- Keep light here. See the separate Starship how-to for flights, catch timeline, and V3/V4 detail.
- Testers (is_OwenLewis): once Starship is fully operational, annual mass-to-space framed as making everyone else (incl. China) a rounding error vs ~7,117 launches / 22k+ sats historical totals — Testers only.
- Official SpaceX: Flight 13 liftoff / next-gen flight deploying advanced Starlink sats; Flight 14 ship did a 60-second six-Raptor static fire.
- Official SpaceX (Aug 25): Booster 21 moved to the pad at Starbase for static fire testing ahead of Flight 14. Testers: Pad 2; out of Megabay 1.
- Official SpaceX (Aug 27): engineers spent several days inspecting Ship 40 in the waters off Christmas Island; collected heatshield samples and reentry data; improvements planned on future vehicles.
- Testers (LaceyPresley): Raptor 3 is 250 tf (~551,000 lb) from one methane engine; booster carries 33. Testers only (not in the Official Ship 40 post).
- Testers: Ship 41 Massey’s fires; Flight 14 framed as first real orbital / product flight with deorbit-burn work; testers also say Flight 14 uses a special internal alloy (not 301).
- CONFLICT: some Aug 14 tester posts say Flight 14 is the first ship-catch attempt; Elon via Aug 20 testers says catch “in a few months.” Prefer the Aug 20 Elon line (same conflict as the Starship note).
- Testers (Aug 25 announcement coverage): Starbase Louisiana / Pecan Island / Vermilion Parish — $100B+, construction 2027, first Starship 2029, thousands of flights/year, 30+/day and “over a dozen” towers via Elon quotes, airport + propellant/power/shipping. No Official SpaceX post of that announcement in this dump. Acreage 125k–136k and pad counts conflict across testers.
- Testers (LAGovJeffLandry): Louisiana governor says SpaceX’s $100 billion investment will transform Louisiana. Testers/governor, not Official SpaceX.
- Testers (FelixSchlang): Pad 39A flame diverter almost finished; pad in final stages; testers say first Starship from 39A is coming fast. Testers only (no Official SpaceX 39A Starship post in this dump).
- Testers (LaceyPresley): tower ship-catch framed as operational unlock (no ocean recovery / landing legs; vehicle back same day); Flight 13 landing precise enough chopsticks would have caught it; remaining limiter is heat-shield (quick look vs tile-by-tile). Testers only.
- Testers (LevLime): Starbase PA for a static fire (attempt 2). Testers only; no Official static-fire result in this dump.

STARLINK
- Testers (DividendDad1): UK spent nearly $40M on Starlink and Starshield; framed as first country outside the US to confirm Starshield for military communications — Testers, not Official.
- Testers (BassonBrain / Bloomberg Opinion): Chris Hughes argues Starlink is becoming a real threat to terrestrial telecoms (indoor/dense-city limits noted). Testers/opinion, not Official.
- Official Q2 2026 (testers quoting the release + Official summary): Connectivity revenue $4.29B (+66% YoY); Starlink subscribers 12M (doubled YoY; +1.7M in Q2); ARPU ~$66/mo (tester earnings rundown). Testers also cite 167 countries and ~10,200 sats in orbit at Q2; this dump testers say constellation now passed 11,000.
- Official SpaceX this dump: 29 Starlink launched from Florida + deployment confirmed; 27 Starlink deployment confirmed.
- Testers this dump: another 27 Starlink from Vandenberg (paired with the “101st Falcon” claim); constellation still framed as past 11,000.
- Official Starlink: Stargaze SSA / conjunction data offered free to all operators.
- Official / testers: Flight 13 deployed Starlink V3 sats for the first time; testers — up to ~60 V3s per Starship, ~1 Tbps downlink each.
- Testers: FCC filing talk of up to 100,000 Gen3 Starlink sats at ~1 Tbps each (news/tester, not an Official post in this dump).
- Testers: last planned F9 Starlink from Florida; remaining F9 Starlink from Vandenberg.
- Testers (XFreeze): TGS vessels 200 GB/day seismic → as much as 10 TB/day over Starlink; 30× lower latency; 15× faster uploads; Arctic.
- Testers: Sherman, TX mall parking approved as a Starlink gateway; 800 MHz spectrum interest with ASTS for direct-to-device voice (reported). Testers also: Starlink Mobile 2027 / D2C from Starship.
- Testers (muskonomy / FCC DA 26-747, WT Docket 26-187): Starlink Spectrum Holdings buying Tristar License Group outright for three uplink-only licences at 1695-1710 MHz (62 counties / 8 states / about 4% of U.S. pop). SpaceX asks renew, extend the terrestrial-build deadline to July 2027, and permanently waive ground-coverage duties in favor of satellite obligations. Light Reading: Tristar paid about $6M. Not Official.
- Testers (cb_doge): SpaceX urging FCC to block Viasat-3 F2 from key U.S. spectrum; testers say Viasat failed a coordination agreement and Viasat’s own data shows excessive downlink interference ~1/3 of the time. Testers/filing, not Official.
- Testers (cb_doge): SpaceX FCC filing urging review of outdated broadband funding (~97% of U.S. households have ≥2 high-speed providers; ~77% have ≥3) and redirect toward affordability. Testers/filing, not Official.
- Testers (muskonomy): SpaceX asking FCC to scrutinize Iridium over blocking next-gen Starlink gateways; testers say Iridium filed 50+ petitions in 8 months and FCC rejected challenges 20 times. Testers/filing, not Official.

SPACEXAI / XAI
- Testers quoting SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen (Goldman Communacopia, Sep 10): another AI compute hosting deal ~$1.11B/month starting Dec 1, 2026 (~$13B annualized); more conviction on $100B ARR target. Testers also: Grok Bot “viral product” demand + Grok 4.6/4.7 → modeling revenue/GW rising from ~$30–50B/GW (aaronburnett). Not Official SpaceX posts in this dump.
- Testers (travel_invest): CFO restated orbital compute — first Starmind satellite 2027 (aligns with prior Elon Q4 2027 AI1 / 2028 scale). Testers.
- Official SpaceX (Jun 16, 2026): exercised option to acquire cursor_ai in an all-stock deal; SpaceXAI had been jointly training a model with Cursor (to ship in Cursor and Grok Build). Q2 Official: Cursor agreement at $60B; Grok 4.5 released in July.
- Testers quoting Gwynne Shotwell (TIME): xAI merger happened quickly; xAI largely operates as its own entity with integration over time; Elon’s decision, Shotwell supportive.
- Official Q2: AI revenue $2.56B (+247% YoY); $14.1B Cloud Services Agreements contracted; AI Capex $15.8B in the quarter.
- Testers quoting Elon (earnings / company talk): AI revenue to exceed all other SpaceX revenue by September and significantly exceed it in Q4; ~$100B+ ARR targeted by December 2026; internal $1T revenue target moved to 2030 (non-zero chance 2029). Testers also quote Elon: AI ~99% of SpaceX’s value in ~4–5 years.
- Testers (herbertong / Jo Bhakdi): Elon reportedly told employees AI revenue could be bigger than the rest of SpaceX next quarter; another major compute deal possible; $SPCX ~$135 — Testers/analyst.
- Testers (JPMorgan): Cursor ~$4B ARR (~75% business); Grok 4.6 cheaper than peers; monthly models through 2026; Grok 5 expected December; Grok Bot as enterprise agents — analyst, not Official.
- Testers on Colossus rentals: Anthropic ~$1.25B/mo, Google ~$920M/mo, Reflection ~$150M/mo (tester rundowns of compute deals).
- Elon (Aug 1): hiring for AI supercomputer clusters on and off Earth — https://t.co/4su2Wmajf1.
- Testers (muskonomy): xAI–OpenAI trade-secret litigation; 9th Circuit appeal; OpenAI fee ask ~$1M — Testers/MLex, not SpaceX Official.
- Space X Tesla XAi folder (2 posts, Testers only): merger / $200Tn combo speculation — not Official.

DATA CENTERS / ORBITAL COMPUTE
- Official SpaceX (Aug 4): partnering with Nvidia to design the Starmind AI1 satellite compute payload; each Starmind sat to include NVIDIA Rubin GPUs and Vera CPUs for datacenter-class space compute.
- Testers on AI1 specs (not in the Official post text here): up to ~150 kW compute / ~120 kW sustained; solar + vacuum radiators; Starlink laser links; Gigasat factory in Bastrop; mass production / deployment talk for late 2027–2028.
- Testers this dump: space-optimized Vera Rubin NVL72 (72 GPU / 36 CPU) launch window Q4 2027, scale 2028 — Testers.
- Testers (SPCX100T): ~100–120 Starship launches per 1 GW orbital compute; Louisiana >30 flights/day → ~4 days per GW at that cadence — Testers only.
- Testers quoting Elon: AI ~99% of SpaceX’s value in ~4–5 years; training on the ground, inference toward orbit.
- Space X Data Centers folder: Testers say Elon declared launching “space data centers” next year; Testers quote Anthropic’s Daniela Amodei — preliminary interest, but space DCs “not on our to do list in 2027”; Testers quote SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen — within a couple of years.
- CONFLICT: “next year” / “couple of years” / Amodei “not 2027” / tester Q4 2027 NVL72 launch window / tester late-2027 production — timelines disagree; label all Testers except the Official Nvidia/Starmind post.

STOCK / BUSINESS

- Official Q2 2026: revenue $7.8B (+92% YoY); net loss $541M (improved $467M YoY); Adjusted EBITDA $3.5B (+191% YoY); segments Space / Connectivity / AI as above.
- Testers: $SPCX IPO mid-2026; staggered lockups (float started ~5%); Aug unlocks and a second ~319M-share unlock around Aug 20 (tester timelines). This dump: ~$135–$137 chatter and a ~$1.86T valuation at $137 — do not treat as fact.
- Testers (JPMorgan): Overweight, $240 PT. Testers quoting Elon: will “exceed” analyst 5-yr growth estimates (SpaceX +2,090% cited by testers).

- Testers (BassonBrain): Nvidia SEC filing read — 122.7 million $SPCX shares valued at $21B. Testers/filing, not Official SpaceX.
- Testers quoting Elon (Teslaconomics / niccruzpatane): “My best guess for ~$3.5T revenue is roughly around 2033.” Testers quote (not an Official elonmusk or SpaceX post in this dump). Testers pair it with $SPCX ~$137 / ~$1.86T (already in this section) and contrast Morgan Stanley’s $3.5T in 2040.
- Testers: Buffett/Berkshire ~0.04% indirect stake via nested holdings (~$700M estimate) — not a direct Official announcement.
- Testers (Ron Baron, Chamath, Citi, MS, Polymarket IPO bets, “$100T” posts, 18,712 BTC hold): bull cases and valuations. Label Testers; they conflict with each other and with Official financials.
- Folder Space X$ is mostly market chatter. Prefer Official earnings and Elon quotes over price-target threads.

ACCESS AND PLANS
- Elon: “Sign up for SpaceX investor relations updates!” (Jun 15, 2026). Public equity access in these posts is via $SPCX after the IPO — details beyond IR signup are tester.
- Testers (SERobinsonJr): CFO Bret Johnsen at Goldman Sachs Communacopia and Technology Conference Thu Sep 10, 12:25 p.m. PT, Palace Hotel San Francisco; testers say live audio/replay on SpaceX IR. Testers, not Official.
- Starlink: consumer / enterprise / government service (12M subs at Q2 per earnings rundowns). Watch Official SpaceX / Starlink for coverage and plans.
- Starship rides are not a ticketed public product here; watch Official streams. Deep Starship plans → separate Starship note.
- Elon: hiring for on/off-Earth AI datacenter clusters (https://t.co/4su2Wmajf1).
- Official Starfall: path toward routine microgravity research / manufacturing return (demo flown; Redwire SpaceMD booking is tester news for late 2028).
- Testers: https://t.co/oV7Sgd9i96 “Sites” page now lists U.S. locations including Starbase Louisiana.

USEFUL WORKFLOWS
- Cadence: follow Official SpaceX and tester launch boards (e.g. upcoming Starlink windows) for Falcon / Starlink; treat NET times as air-traffic hints. Next Official-dated payload: Roman on Falcon Heavy Aug 30 pad 39A.
- Earnings / IR: use Official Q2 post + Elon IR signup; ignore unlocked-float panic, JPM price targets, and “$100T” threads as investment advice.
- Earnings / IR this dump: testers date CFO Bret Johnsen at Goldman Sachs Communacopia Sep 10 (12:25 p.m. PT). Still testers, not Official.
- Starship: Flight 14 gate is B21 pad static fire (Official); for catch timing and vehicle detail open the Starship note. Louisiana Starbase, Pad 39A flame-diverter, and this dump’s static-fire PA are Testers-only (no Official SpaceX announcement post).
- Orbital compute: Official Nvidia/Starmind post is the anchor; treat “next year” / Q4 2027 NVL72 / GW-scale / AI1 kW posts as Testers and flag timeline conflicts.
- National security / Starshield: expect thin Official detail; mission numbers (e.g. USSF-366) are often all that appears. This dump's aviation PLEO task order is Testers/filing only (no Official SpaceX post).

text:
2. Saudi-backed forces prepare response after Houthis seize Perim Island

Date/location: September 11–12 — Bab el-Mandeb and western Yemen 🇾🇪 
Status: Developing

Reuters and AP independently report that Houthi forces captured Perim/Mayun Island, which divides the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Saudi-backed Yemeni forces indicate they intend to retake recently lost territory around Perim, Dhubab and Mokha.

What changed: Reuters reports that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman requested direct U.S. military assistance. Washington declined immediate strikes but reportedly offered intelligence and targeting support. Trump confirmed speaking with the crown prince and said the Houthis had separately contacted his administration seeking to avoid U.S. intervention.

Why it matters: Houthi positions now lie inside a strategic maritime chokepoint while Hormuz traffic remains severely restricted.

Principal uncertainty: Bab el-Mandeb remains open. Houthi statements that most shipping is safe are not guarantees, while reports of Iranian operational direction rely on unidentified Iranian sources and are denied by Tehran.

Here's how the Coordination Framework's plan for four deputy prime minister (DPM) posts reportedly collapsed. 

🔴 Around three weeks ago, 11 of 12 CF leaders voted to create four DPM posts. Maliki was the sole objector, arguing Iraq is in a fiscal crisis and can't absorb four new offices but said he wouldn't block a majority decision.

🔴 The plan died anyway as messages from the Najaf marja'iyya reached CF leaders carrying what was framed as "non-binding advice" rejecting the posts. Hammam Hammoudi is the likely intermediary. It's not clear  whether Maliki prompted Najaf or Najaf moved on its own in response to public criticism.

🔴 The posts were already being staffed. One party, likely AAH, had reportedly fitted out an office for its expected DPM at $5M and secured 800 job grades to stand up a protection regiment. 

🔴 Names in circulation for DPM is Laith Khazali (Qais's brother and who is on US Treasury's sanctions list over oil smuggling), Mohsen al-Mandalawi (who's two brothers have just been sanctioned by US), Mohammed Tamim (Taqadum), and a Kurdish figure who has not been decided on by KDP/PUK.

🔴 At a CF meeting at former PM Abadi's house, Maliki and Qais Khazali clashed openly. Khazali demanded Interior Ministry, which is Maliki's share.

🔴 Khazali offered to give up Labour Ministry and said he'd forfeit all 28 of AAH's parliamentary seats to get Interior. 

🔴 Maliki insists on Qasim Atta despite his failed first vote in parliament, PM Zaidi has been shifting the ministry's powers to his revived Military Office, and Washington treats the post as central to the weapons-disarmament. 

Moving forward

🔴 The government has run on 14 of 23 ministries since May. Completing the cabinet before the Sept 30 US withdrawal date now looks unlikely; one MP says ministers are already running multiple portfolios.

🔴 Expect ministries to pass in "instalments," one or two at a time with a vote and then back to the table, rather than a package.

🔴 The Maliki–Khazali feud predates this. Khazali blocked Maliki's last bid for PM, and the two clashed in 2023 over AAH's reported attempt to poach then-oil minister Hayyan Abdul Ghani from State of Law.

🔴 The bigger signal is Najaf. If the reporting is accurate, the marja'iyya just overrode an 11–1 CF vote through "non-binding" advice, showing it still functions as a veto player on the structure of government.

A wild cheetah introducing her cubs to a photographer is one of those rare moments that feels almost unreal. 🐆🥹

Female cheetahs are fiercely protective mothers. For the first few months of life, cubs are extremely vulnerable to predators such as lions, hyenas, and leopards, and many don't survive to adulthood. That's why a mother cheetah carefully chooses when and where to reveal her cubs.

While cheetahs are generally shy and avoid humans, experienced wildlife photographers occasionally witness extraordinary displays of calm curiosity, moments that offer a glimpse into the trust and intelligence of these remarkable animals.

Fun fact: Cheetah cubs are born with a long, silvery mantle of fur along their backs that helps camouflage them and may make them resemble honey badgers, an animal many predators prefer to avoid.

The cheetah's reaction:

"These are my kids. Please admire them respectfully and keep your distance." 😂❤️

Nature's greatest privilege isn't getting close to wildlife, it's being accepted as a harmless observer for a few unforgettable seconds.

What's the most heartwarming animal moment you've ever seen? 🐆👇💛
