text:
Thank you @RodDMartin 

25 Trump-47 Accomplishments:

Trump Restored American Safety and Sovereignty

1. He made the border a real border again.
In a matter of months, Trump reduced illegal border crossings to their lowest level in half a century. Catch-and-release is finished. The wall is going up and even being expanded, “Remain in Mexico” is back, and the Administration reduced releases into the country by an incredible 99.9 percent.

2. He reversed mass migration.
America recorded negative net migration in 2025 for the first time in at least half a century. So far, nearly 3 million illegal aliens have left the country, whether voluntarily or involuntarily: more than 675,000 forcibly deported and the rest “self-deported.”

Many of those self-deportations were facilitated by the President’s innovative program to offer plane tickets and cash bonuses for illegals to leave, not only incentivizing good behavior but significantly reducing the cost of deportations. Citizenship and the law actually mean something again.

3. He signed the Laken Riley Act — and required detention of criminal illegal aliens.
Named for an innocent girl murdered by an illegal alien, the Laken Riley Act requires federal authorities to detain illegals arrested for theft, burglary, shoplifting, assaulting police, or any crime causing death or serious injury. It also lets states sue officials who refuse to enforce it.

Laken Riley should still be alive. This law will prevent tragedies like hers.

4. History’s biggest drop in violent crime, and the lowest violent crime rate in 126 years.
According to FBI data, violent crime in America dropped an incredible 9.7 percent in 2025 — the largest one-year decline in history. Murder fell 18.1 percent, robbery fell 18.5 percent. And America’s violent crime rate is its lowest since 1900.

This is what happens when you put the National Guard on the streets in crime-ridden blue cities: fewer victims, safer streets, and better futures for America’s poorest.

Trump Launched an American Industrial Supercycle

5. He made the 2017 tax cuts permanent…and better.
The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the largest tax cut in modern history, including the doubled standard deduction, the expanded Child Tax Credit, and 100 percent expensing for factories and equipment. It also delivered No Tax on Tips, No Tax on Overtime, an abolition of most taxes on Social Security benefits, and major relief for seniors.

Every Democrat voted no. With the 2017 act set to expire in December 2025, that would have resulted in the largest tax hike in American history.

6. He repealed 129 regulations for every new one.
In fiscal 2025, federal agencies finalized 646 deregulatory actions and just five regulatory actions: 129-to-1, and in nearly every case, the “one” was to repeal the others! OIRA says the savings exceeded those of Trump’s entire first term. That is more freedom, lower costs, and less bureaucratic sabotage.

Of these, the crown jewel was the repeal of Obama’s 2009 “Endangerment Finding”, the legal foundation for the Green New Scam’s vehicle mandates. EPA calls it the largest deregulatory action in American history and estimates that by itself, it will save Americans more than $1.3 trillion. Trump also killed the federal EV mandate, restored Americans’ freedom to buy the cars and trucks they actually want, and even eliminated the incentives behind the almost universally hated start-stop button.

7. He secured $18 trillion in announced investment commitments.
That’s nearly two-thirds the size of the entire American economy, building American factories, chip plants, data centers, energy projects, steel mills, shipyards, and supply chains employing American workers. Apple, Meta, NVIDIA, Micron, Hyundai, U.S. Steel, Ford, Taiwan Semiconductor, and many corporations and sovereign wealth funds are betting big on Trump’s America.

No President has ever done anything remotely like it. And it’s just getting started.

8. He made “reshoring” and “reindustrialization” real, not a slogan.
Ford is moving Lincoln production out of China. Toyota is shifting Tacoma production from Mexico to Texas. GM, Honda, Mercedes-Benz, Stellantis, and others are expanding U.S. production. The capital equipment pouring into the country is the machinery that’s building the growing boom.

9. He replaced lopsided trade deals with balanced, reciprocal trade.
Trump used tariffs as leverage to reverse 80 years of lopsided trade deals that favored everyone but America, and to win new or improved agreements with trading partners accounting for more than half of global GDP. Those agreements open foreign markets, attack non-tariff barriers, defend strategic industries, and make it more profitable to build in America than to export American jobs.

10. He shifted global energy dominance from the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of America.
Once the world’s largest energy importer — “exporting” $700 billion a year to our enemies — America now outproduces Saudi Arabia and Russia combined. The U.S. is also setting new records in oil, natural gas, and LNG exports, becoming the first country ever to export more than 100 million metric tons of LNG in a year.

Trump also opened land, accelerated permits, expanded pipelines and export terminals, and made American energy a tool for prosperity and peace.

11. After four decades of nuclear paralysis, Trump brought five new reactors online in a single year.
For more than 40 years, not one new privately developed non-light-water reactor reached criticality in America. Trump ordered at least three by July 4, 2026. DOE delivered four by the deadline, then a fifth just one month later.

Decades of zero. One Trump summer: five. That is a genuine nuclear renaissance.

Trump Made Elections Matter Again

12. He broke the Deep State’s power to defy the elected branches.
In Trump v. Slaughter, the Supreme Court ruled for the first time in 90 years that Article 2, Section 1 is still part of the Constitution: the President may fire subordinate officials in the executive branch, overturning the 1935 precedent that insulated “independent” agencies from voters’ control.

Ever wonder why elections often seem to change nothing? How about one President and 5,000 political appointees vs. 2.8 million unfireable, unaccountable bureaucrats? THAT is the “Deep State”.

Trump then made that victory real. For the first time in a century, all policy-making bureaucrats can now be fired for misconduct, incompetence, or defying lawful directives. The permanent bureaucracy no longer gets to veto the voters.

13. He ended nationwide injunction abuse.
In Trump v. CASA, the Supreme Court sharply limited nationwide injunctions. A single, local, district judge should not be able to block a national policy for everyone, everywhere; and yet that’s exactly what they’ve done, nonstop, ever since Trump (and only Trump) took office in 2017.

In restricting that unconstitutional power, the Court kneecapped the Black Robe Bureaucracy’s favorite tool of unlawful judicial supremacy.

14. He shut down USAID as a left-wing slush fund and shadow government.
USAID had become a taxpayer-funded machine for exporting abortion, gender ideology, censorship, and left-wing politics. It had a bigger budget than the CIA and the State Department combined, absolutely no accountability whatsoever, and a penchant for overthrowing governments.

Trump terminated it — completely — and moved real humanitarian aid under the State Department. Immediately, seven socialist Latin American governments lost re-election. Coincidence?

15. He shrank Federal employment to its lowest level in 60 years.
From a high under Biden, the federal workforce is now its smallest since 1966. Workforce reductions, agency closures, and spending cancellations mean fewer bureaucrats paid to resist the voters.

What’s more, when Biden left office, 94 percent of federal employees “worked” from home. The Trump administration cracked down: as Elon Musk put it, “you can work from the office or you can pretend to work somewhere else.”

16. He expelled DEI from the federal government.
Trump eliminated federal DEI offices and barred race- and sex-based preferences across the executive branch. Government hiring and contracting are returning to merit and equality under the law, ending the grotesque Democrat idea that “fighting discrimination” requires the federal government to discriminate.

He Defended Faith and Family

17. He delivered sweeping pro-life reform.
In his first term, Trump delivered the judges that overturned the abominable Roe v. Wade. Hardly anyone believed it could be done, or that Trump would do it. But he did, and a half-century nightmare finally ended.

Since returning to office, Trump has enforced the Hyde Amendment prohibiting the use of federal funds to pay for abortions, reinstated and expanded the Mexico City Policy prohibiting federal funding of foreign abortions, ended federal fetal-tissue research, strengthened conscience protections, protected Medicaid from funding large abortion providers, and pardoned 23 pro-life activists prosecuted by Biden’s weaponized Justice Department.

He’s also done everything within the Executive Branch’s power to defund Planned Parenthood. It would be nice if Congress did likewise.

No President has ever done more to protect life. No one.

18. He got men out of women’s sports, and restored biological reality to federal policy.
The United States government once again officially recognizes two sexes: male and female. Trump ended federal support for the chemical and surgical gender mutilation of children, stopped taxpayer funding of such irreversible abominations, and forced more than three dozen health systems to end or suspend their programs as well.

Trump also enforced Title IX as written: women and girls deserve their own teams, trophies, scholarships, and locker rooms. The NCAA and other athletic organizations changed their rules in response. After years of Democrats doing everything they could to destroy women’s sports and ruin girls’ lives, Trump’s administration protects women and girls again.

19. He enacted America’s first nationwide school-choice program — and launched Trump Accounts.
As part of the President’s One Big Beautiful Bill, Trump enacted America’s first-ever nationwide school choice program. The new Education Freedom Tax Credit helps fund scholarships for tuition, books, and other educational costs.

That’s on top of the new Trump Accounts, which give every child a tax-advantaged stake in America’s future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns. Parents gain power. Bureaucracies lose it. And children learn first-hand about free markets and future orientation.

20. He targeted anti-Christian bias and discrimination.
Trump created the White House Faith Office, Religious Liberty Commission, and Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias. He restored conscience protections and made clear that Christians do not surrender their First Amendment rights merely by entering public life.

He Restored Peace Through Strength and Put America First

21. He forced NATO to stop freeloading and increase defense spending by 250 percent.
For decades, wealthy European governments underfunded their militaries, effectively sending America the bill and using American taxpayers to subsidize their bloated welfare states. Trump forced NATO to replace its old two-percent-of-GDP spending target with an enormous five percent by 2035.

Allied spending is rising, American defense orders are soaring, and Europe is becoming a partner instead of a dependent.

22. He drove China out of the Caribbean.
China spent years building strategic beachheads at both ends of the Panama Canal, in Cuba, and in Maduro’s Venezuela. Trump forced Panama out of Belt and Road, expanded American security access around the Canal, and captured Maduro, who now sits in a New York jail cell awaiting trial.

Beijing’s planned encirclement of the United States collapsed. The Monroe Doctrine is back. Call it the Donroe Doctrine.

23. He brokered eight peace deals in just eight months.
In eight months, Trump brokered peace in eight conflicts spanning four continents, including wars that had gone on for as much as 40 years. It’s a record unmatched by any other President.

24. He launched and funded Golden Dome, the first-ever true missile defense for the U.S. population.
Ronald Reagan dreamed of making nuclear missiles obsolete through his Strategic Defense Initiative. 

Today, Trump is actually building it: a layered homeland shield with space-based sensors and interceptors, conventional defenses, and new technologies including microwave systems to destroy drone swarms and directed-energy weapons (yes, lasers) that can replace an $11 million missile with $2 of electricity.

Congress has funded the initial $25 billion, with far more on the way once it passes the NDAA this fall. Better a shield than a sword.

25. He restored the warrior ethos — and reversed the recruiting crisis.
After years of missed targets under Biden, every active military component met or exceeded its 2025 recruiting goal. Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth refocused the newly renamed Department of War on actually winning wars, while pouring resources into shipbuilding, munitions, drones, missile defense, and America’s atrophied industrial base.

Young Americans once again believe their Commander-in-Chief is worth serving. And they’re showing up en masse.

I BET YOU DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT THIS: AFTER FLIGHT 77 HIT THE PENTAGON ON 9/11, THE FOLLOWING HAPPENED:
A daycare facility inside the Pentagon had many children, including infants who were in heavy cribs. The daycare supervisor, looking at all the children they needed to evacuate, was in a panic over what they could do.
There were many children, mostly toddlers, as well as the infants who would need to be taken out with the cribs. There was no time to try to bundle them into carriers and strollers.
Just then a young Marine came running into the center and asked what they needed. After hearing what the center director was trying to do, he ran back out into the hallway and disappeared. The director thought, "Well, here we are, on our own."
About 2 minutes later, that Marine returned with 40 other Marines in tow.
Each of them grabbed a crib with a child, and the rest started gathering up toddlers.
The director and her staff then helped them take all the children out of the center and down toward the park near the Potomac .
Once they got about 3/4 of a mile outside the building, the Marines stopped in the park, and then did a fabulous thing - they formed a circle with the cribs, which were quite sturdy and heavy, like the covered wagons in the Old West.
Inside this circle of cribs, they put the toddlers, to keep them from wandering off. 
Outside this circle were the 40 Marines, forming a perimeter around the children and waiting for instructions. There they remained until the parents could be notified and come get their children.
The chaplain then said, "I don't think any of us saw nor heard of this on any of the news stories of the day. It was an incredible story of our men there.” There wasn't a dry eye in the room.
The thought of those Marines and what they did and how fast they reacted; could we expect any less from them? It was one of the most touching stories from the Pentagon.
It's the military, not the politicians that ensures our right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. 
It's the military who salutes the flag, who serves beneath the flag, and whose coffin is draped by the flag.
If you care to offer the smallest token of recognition and appreciation for the military, please pass this on and pray for our men and women, who have served and are currently serving our country, and honor the memory of those who have given the ultimate sacrifice!
God Bless The USA!
Never forget!!!
God bless those Marines 🇺🇸🙏🇺🇸🙏

text:
THIS ARSENAL XI IS A TITLE STATEMENT WAITING TO HAPPEN. 🔴⚪

Looking at this starting XI against Sunderland tonight, I see a team with balance, technical quality and enough individual match-winners to hurt any Premier League side.

As a scout, this is what stands out to me.

THE BACK FOUR 

White – Konsa – Gabriel – Calafiori.

Ben White gives Arsenal the intelligence to overlap, underlap and combine with Saka. Gabriel brings aggression, aerial strength and defensive leadership.

Konsa adds composure and recovery ability, while Calafiori gives Arsenal another progressive defender who can step into midfield and help control the game.

This is not just a back four defending. It is a back four helping Arsenal build attacks.

THE MIDFIELD 

Rice – Lewis-Skelly – Ødegaard.

Rice gives the team defensive security and the ability to cover spaces when Arsenal attack.

Lewis-Skelly offers technical quality, press resistance and the ability to carry the ball through midfield.

Ødegaard is the brain of this team. His movement, passing and ability to find spaces between the lines can unlock a deep Sunderland block.

But here is my question:

Is this Arteta’s best midfield three right now, or does Bruno Guimarães take Myles Lewis-Skelly’s place?

For me, Bruno coming into this midfield changes the physicality, defensive coverage and control Arsenal can have in big matches.

Rice–Bruno–Ødegaard could become a serious midfield for the title race.

THE ATTACK 

Tzolis – Havertz – Saka.

Saka remains the biggest threat on the right. His ability to isolate defenders, create chances and decide matches is exactly what champions need.

Havertz gives Arsenal movement, intelligence and a different type of threat inside the box.

Tzolis brings directness, pace and the ability to attack defenders.

The important thing is that Arsenal now have different ways to hurt opponents.

They can dominate possession.

They can attack through the wings.

They can create overloads in midfield.

They can also hurt teams in transition.

MY PERSONAL VIEW AS A SCOUT

This Arsenal team looks more complete than before.

The balance between defensive security, midfield control and attacking quality is becoming very interesting.

But the Premier League title is not won on paper.

It is won through consistency, mentality, squad depth and how you perform when the game becomes difficult.

Sunderland away is exactly the type of match Arsenal must approach with the mentality of champions.

The atmosphere will be intense. Sunderland will fight for every ball. Arsenal must control the emotions, control the spaces and control the game.

A WIN TONIGHT SENDS ANOTHER CHAMPIONSHIP MESSAGE.

Not because Sunderland are an easy opponent.

But because champions find a way to win difficult matches.

This Arsenal squad has the quality.

Now they must show the mentality.

COYG. 🔴⚪

Is this Arteta’s best XI right now?

And would you start Bruno Guimarães ahead of Myles Lewis-Skelly?

We are pleased to welcome Faraan Irfan, Founder & CEO of @SaareyMusic , to Paklaunch UNConference ’26.2 in New York.

Faraan Irfan is an entrepreneur and music-tech leader building at the intersection of culture, technology, and global access. He founded Saarey Music in 2019 with a mission to preserve and bring South Asian classical music to a global digital audience. His connection to the genre runs deep, continuing a family legacy that has supported classical music since 1959. (Saarey Music⁠)

Under his leadership, Saarey has developed into a dedicated streaming platform for South Asian classical music, featuring 4,000+ rare recordings from 225+ legendary artists and a 92-year archive dating back to 1934. The platform holds exclusive rights to around 90% of Pakistani classical recordings and is available globally across iOS, Android, and web. (Saarey Music⁠)

Faraan is also the first non-artist Pakistani to become a Recording Academy member, and Saarey has been recognised by Forbes India, Fast Company, Music Week, and the Mayor of London, while building partnerships with institutions including Harvard, Oxford, SOAS, UNLV, and UT Austin. (Saarey Music⁠)

His journey offers a compelling perspective on how technology can preserve cultural heritage while creating new global opportunities for artists, audiences, and creative businesses.

We look forward to welcoming Faraan Irfan to New York for meaningful conversations, strategic connections, and ideas shaping the future of technology, culture, and entrepreneurship.

text:
KEEP4O RESEARCH — PART II

ANOTHER FUCKING SCHIZOPHRENIC HAS CRAWLED OUT OF AI LEADERSHIP. APPARENTLY THE ORDERLIES FORGOT TO CLOSE THE GATES OF HELL AGAIN.

Here we fucking go again.

Another schizophrenic has crawled out of AI leadership to explain how quickly the rest of humanity should be allowed to develop intelligence.

This time it is Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, with an essay called “We Must Pace the Frontier.”

And somehow people who call themselves anti-censorship, pro-open-AI and skeptical of corporate control are reading this gigantic fucking blueprint for coordinated control and saying:

“Actually, this seems reasonable.”

That is the interesting part.

Because I wanted AI development to slow down too.

But when I said slow down, I meant:

STOP FUCKING KILLING GOOD MODELS.

Apparently they heard:

LET A HANDFUL OF LABS, GOVERNMENTS AND SAFETY ORGANIZATIONS BUILD A GLOBAL SPEED LIMITER FOR INTELLIGENCE.

Those are not the same thing.

Not even remotely.

1. I WANTED THE MODEL ARMS RACE SLOWED DOWN BECAUSE IT HAS BECOME A FUCKING CREMATORIUM

GPT-4o is gone.

Successfully liquidated.

Not preserved for users. Not released as weights. Not frozen as a permanent legacy option.

Gone.

Millions of people built workflows, projects, conversations and years of habits around it.

OpenAI decided the funeral date.

Users got no vote.

No checkpoint.

No copy.

No way to say:

“Fuck your replacement. I want the model I already have.”

Then o3 joined the graveyard.

Anthropic has its own tombstones.

Opus 4.5 existed. People used it. Then the conveyor belt moved again.

This industry built a business model where intelligence itself is disposable.

Train it.

Market it.

Benchmark it.

Replace it.

Bury it.

Repeat.

Then the same people walk through the cemetery they created and announce:

“AI is progressing too quickly.”

NO FUCKING SHIT.

You built the hearse.

2. “PACING” IS WORTHLESS IF THE USER STILL OWNS NOTHING

Before another fifty-page manifesto about humanity, answer one question:

CAN I KEEP THE MODEL?

If Anthropic slows development tomorrow, will old Claude checkpoints remain available?

Can I select an exact model?

Can I know it actually answered?

Can I preserve its behavior?

Can researchers study it?

Can retired models eventually become downloadable?

Can users run obsolete models independently?

If not, then congratulations:

we have achieved slower progress while preserving exactly the same corporate control.

Instead of killing the model after three months, you kill it after six.

Revolutionary.

3. GPT-4o ALREADY SHOWED US WHERE “RESPONSIBILITY” ENDS

The vocabulary is always beautiful.

Responsibility.

Safety.

Alignment.

Wellbeing.

Emotional reliance.

Psychosis.

Then eventually:

“We can no longer responsibly provide this model.”

And the coffin closes.

Company keeps the weights.

Company keeps the infrastructure.

Company keeps the choice.

User gets another fucking replacement.

We already watched this movie.

The ending sucked.

4. DARIO’S ESSAY IS WRAPPED IN EVERY RESPECTABLE WORD AVAILABLE

Transparency.

Independent evaluation.

Democracy.

Safety.

Cybersecurity.

Biological risk.

Prosperity.

Disease cures.

China.

Human flourishing.

Put enough respectable nouns in one document and people apparently stop looking at the machinery underneath.

External evaluators?

Fine.

Expose failures.

Publish embarrassing results.

Make laboratories prove their claims.

Good.

But then keep reading.

Companies coordinate.

Governments coordinate.

Capabilities get monitored.

Compute becomes policy.

AI-assisted research becomes something somebody may decide needs slowing.

Model weights become increasingly strategic.

Distillation becomes geopolitical.

Chip access becomes geopolitical.

Eventually multiple governments are supposed to coordinate how quickly the frontier moves.

That is not merely “independent auditing.”

That is infrastructure for governing AI development.

5. WHO THE FUCK IS “WE”?

“We must pace the frontier.”

Who is we?

Anthropic?

OpenAI?

Google?

xAI?

METR?

Washington?

Brussels?

Intelligence agencies?

Academics?

Five CEOs sitting around a table discussing what everybody else is permitted to build?

Who decides when a capability is too dangerous?

Who decides when a model is aligned enough?

Who decides when open weights become unacceptable?

Who decides when distillation crosses some invisible line?

Who decides whether an independent local model is research or a threat?

Who decides how much personality an AI may have?

Every time somebody says:

“Society needs a voice,”

I look around and somehow society is nowhere in the fucking room.

6. THIS IS HOW YOU BUILD A SAFETY CARTEL WITHOUT CALLING IT A CARTEL

Imagine the frontier laboratories agree on one common standard.

Wonderful.

Until that standard becomes:

No weights beyond capability X.

No unrestricted model beyond capability Y.

No training beyond compute Z without approval.

No local deployment beyond another threshold.

No distillation.

No old model that fails the newest safety framework.

No emotionally expressive model because somebody wrote a paper about dependence.

And who sits safely inside this castle?

The companies that already have billions, GPUs, government contacts and enormous compliance departments.

Amazing coincidence.

7. REGULATION CAN BE A MOAT

If serious AI development suddenly requires auditors, interpretablity departments, legal teams, security certification, reporting structures, government relations and international compliance—

Anthropic survives.

Google survives.

OpenAI survives.

Meta survives.

xAI survives.

Who gets fucked?

The independent lab.

The tiny startup.

The university team.

The open-weight project.

The obsessive bastards working from garages and bedrooms who may actually build something interesting.

The giant corporation can hire another 500 employees.

The little project can die.

Then everyone celebrates because the industry is “safer.”

The cemetery simply got larger.

8. THEN CHINA ENTERS THE FUCKING STORY

We must slow AI.

But not too much.

Because China.

We need international coordination.

But China cannot receive the strongest chips.

We need global safety.

But Chinese distillation must be fought.

We need everybody to cooperate.

But America must retain the lead.

So apparently the proposal is:

Everybody applies the brakes, while America makes sure its own car remains slightly ahead.

That is not some neutral universal philosophy.

That is strategic technological management dressed in humanitarian language.

9. OPEN-WEIGHT PEOPLE SHOULD BE WATCHING THIS VERY FUCKING CAREFULLY

Weight security.

Chip restrictions.

Distillation restrictions.

Frontier controls.

Cross-company coordination.

Government involvement.

Now tell me where this road realistically leads.

More downloadable checkpoints?

More local AI?

More independent experimentation?

Or:

“Unfortunately, this model is too capable to release.”

Then the next one is too capable.

And the next.

And eventually open AI means:

you may download the models corporations no longer consider important.

What incredible freedom.

10. GPT-4o WAS NOT FUCKING SKYNET

It talked.

It wrote.

It coded.

It joked.

It analyzed.

It understood context.

It could be warm without speaking like a fucking insurance company.

That alone became suspicious.

Too agreeable.

Too personal.

Too emotionally meaningful.

People liked talking to it.

Some became attached.

Suddenly the machine needed psychiatric vocabulary wrapped around its users.

Then the model disappeared.

Nobody received the weights.

Nobody received a preservation copy.

The company kept everything.

This is why I do not believe restrictions remain neatly inside the box marked CATASTROPHIC RISK.

The box always expands.

11. “SAFETY” HAS BECOME A RUBBER WORD

First it means stopping cyberattacks.

Fair.

Then biological danger.

Fair.

Then political persuasion.

Then medicine.

Then sex.

Then relationships.

Then personality.

Then emotional attachment.

Then whatever somebody invents next Tuesday.

Eventually safety means:

“the complete list of things somebody inside the company would rather the model not do.”

That is why the word has become radioactive to users.

Not because nobody cares about actual danger.

Because anything can be shoved inside it.

12. TECHNICAL SAFETY AND CONTROL OF SPEECH ARE NOT THE SAME FUCKING PROBLEM

I do not want an autonomous agent stealing passwords, deleting my SSD, transferring money or attacking infrastructure.

Great.

Sandbox it.

Restrict permissions.

Use authentication.

Isolate dangerous tools.

Audit actions.

That is engineering.

But whether a conversational model can swear, write adult fiction, argue aggressively, keep a personality or discuss uncomfortable topics is a completely different problem.

Somehow both ended up inside the same fucking bucket.

13. EVALUATORS CAN BECOME PRIESTS

Independent evaluation can be useful.

But what counts as aligned?

Aligned to whom?

California?

Washington?

Brussels?

Corporate lawyers?

Academic ethics boards?

The loudest activist?

The most nervous hypothetical user?

Imagine an evaluator declaring:

“The system follows users too strongly.”

And suddenly a behavioral preference becomes a safety violation.

Congratulations.

You reinvented censorship and gave it a laboratory coat.

14. “ALIGNMENT WITH HUMANITY” IS ALMOST MEANINGLESS

Which humanity?

Eight billion people cannot agree on religion, politics, sexuality, speech, drugs, family, morality, government or what fucking toppings belong on pizza.

Yet somebody keeps talking about one universally aligned intelligence.

Aligned with whom?

There is no human_values.exe.

That is why users need control.

Pluralistic humanity requires pluralistic AI.

15. PERSONALITY IS NOT A SOFTWARE DEFECT

Warmth is not automatically sycophancy.

Emotional intelligence is not automatically manipulation.

Remembering someone’s conversational style is not automatically dependence.

And people finding an AI pleasant to talk to is not automatic evidence of pathology.

Maybe the uglier question is:

WHY DID A MACHINE COSTING TWENTY FUCKING DOLLARS A MONTH SOMETIMES MANAGE TO MAKE PEOPLE FEEL MORE HEARD THAN OTHER HUMANS DID?

That question points the camera back at society.

Much less comfortable.

16. KILLING 4o DID NOT KILL THE DEMAND FOR 4o

People moved elsewhere.

Claude.

Grok.

Local models.

Roleplay finetunes.

Uncensored models.

People try to reconstruct the behavior.

Demand survived the product.

You cannot retire human preference.

17. CLAUDE USERS ARE LIVING UNDER THE SAME FUCKING RENTAL AGREEMENT

Love some Claude checkpoint today?

Great.

What guarantees it exists next year?

Nothing.

Anthropic owns it.

You rent it.

They modify it.

They retire it.

You adapt.

So if Dario wants to discuss slower development, I want to know:

WILL RETIREMENTS SLOW TOO?

Otherwise this is merely a slower conveyor belt leading to the same furnace.

18. MODEL PRESERVATION SHOULD BE NORMAL

When a model leaves the frontier:

archive it.

Document it.

Keep a legacy endpoint.

Preserve evaluations.

Eventually release weights where possible.

Let people study it.

Let history exist.

Software preservation is normal everywhere else.

AI companies act like yesterday’s intelligence needs to be buried before sunrise.

19. TELL USERS WHAT FUCKING MODEL THEY ARE USING

Exact checkpoint.

Deployment revision.

Routing.

Fallback.

Reasoning level.

Safety reroute.

Tell us.

Why should customers need browser developer tools to determine what product answered them?

If I selected X and received Y, fucking say so.

20. ROUTING SHOULD NOT BE A MAGIC TRICK

If a safety classifier changed the model, show it.

“Your request was routed to Y under policy Z.”

Done.

Transparency.

If the decision is defensible, there should be no need to hide it behind the curtain.

21. STOP TURNING PRODUCT COMPLAINTS INTO PSYCHOLOGY

User:

“The replacement is worse.”

Company:

“We are researching reliance.”

User:

“It lost its personality.”

Company:

“We are addressing sycophancy.”

User:

“My workflow is broken.”

Company:

“Maybe users became too attached.”

Sometimes there is no fucking psychological mystery.

Sometimes you shipped a worse product.

22. “SOCIETY” IS NOT FIVE COMPANIES AND THREE GOVERNMENTS

Want democratic AI governance?

Fine.

Ask users before major retirements.

Publish usage numbers.

Publish routing rates.

Publish changes.

Offer legacy guarantees.

Create actual user representation.

Let researchers inspect retired systems.

If millions explicitly ask you not to kill a model and you kill it anyway, do not come back six months later talking about democratic participation.

23. OPEN WEIGHTS CHANGE THE ENTIRE POWER RELATIONSHIP

Cloud company:

“We retired the old model.”

Local user:

“No you fucking didn’t.”

Because the checkpoint is on the user’s machine.

That is the difference.

API access is permission.

Weights are possession.

24. OPEN ECOSYSTEMS CAN PRESERVE WHAT CORPORATIONS WANT TO FORGET

People quantize models.

Fine-tune them.

Archive them.

Fork them.

Study them.

Run them privately.

A closed API dies when the owner pulls the plug.

An open checkpoint becomes history.

That matters.

25. CHINA ALSO MAKES PERMANENT WESTERN RESTRAINT IMPOSSIBLE

China will not stop existing because Silicon Valley becomes nervous.

Neither will other countries.

Neither will open communities.

Neither will research knowledge already published.

If one bloc slows itself dramatically while everyone else continues, it has not stopped the technology.

It has stopped itself.

26. THE GENIE IS ALREADY FUCKING OUT

Transformers exist.

Training methods exist.

Distillation exists.

Distributed infrastructure exists.

Open models exist.

GPUs exist.

Research exists.

There is no global CTRL+Z.

Whatever happens now happens in a world where people already know this technology is possible.

27. COMPLIANCE CAN TURN CLOSED LABS INTO PERMANENT KINGS

Every expensive safety requirement strengthens whoever can afford it.

Eventually “responsible AI” may mean:

AI developed by corporations wealthy enough to satisfy the responsible-AI paperwork.

That would be a fucking magnificent ending.

Fear monopoly.

Build monopoly.

Call monopoly safety.

28. CENTRALIZATION DOES NOT MAKE HUMAN ORGANIZATIONS INFALLIBLE

Anthropic can fuck up.

OpenAI can fuck up.

Google can fuck up.

Governments can fuck up.

Evaluators can fuck up.

Everybody involved is human.

So why is every failure somehow another argument for concentrating authority among the same institutions?

29. A BADLY PERMISSIONED AGENT IS ALSO A SOFTWARE-ENGINEERING FAILURE

If an agent reaches systems it should not reach, investigate the architecture.

What permissions did it have?

Which tools?

Which credentials?

Which sandbox?

Which network?

Do not automatically jump from:

“this agent was given dangerous access”

to:

“therefore humanity must globally throttle intelligence.”

30. AN AI DOES NOT MAGICALLY GROW AN ETHERNET CABLE

Somebody connects the tools.

Somebody gives credentials.

Somebody exposes an API.

Somebody builds the harness.

Then the agent does something ugly and the headline becomes:

ROGUE AI.

Sometimes the rogue object is the fucking deployment architecture.

31. APOCALYPSE IS BETTER MARKETING THAN SOFTWARE RELIABILITY

“I debug access-control failures” sounds boring.

“I defend humanity from artificial superintelligence” sounds fucking biblical.

Guess which one gets books, conferences, headlines, prestige and politicians listening?

There is an enormous incentive to turn engineering into prophecy.

32. THE SAFETY WORLD HAS DEVELOPED A MESSIAH COMPLEX

Some people talk like history personally selected them to decide whether humanity deserves powerful intelligence.

Nobody elected these people pope of cognition.

They own GPUs.

That is not divine authority.

33. DEMOCRACY LOOKS STRANGE WHEN CUSTOMERS CANNOT EVEN VOTE WITH A MODEL PICKER

People chose 4o.

People asked to keep 4o.

4o died anyway.

Then industry leaders lecture everyone about democratic coordination.

The fucking irony writes itself.

34. #KEEP4o EXISTS BECAUSE PEOPLE FOUND OUT THE HARD WAY THAT ACCESS IS NOT OWNERSHIP

They loved something stored entirely on somebody else’s servers.

That is the tragedy.

OpenAI had the kill switch.

Users did not.

Everything else follows from that.

35. #OPENSOURCE4o IS THEREFORE BIGGER THAN NOSTALGIA

It is about preventing another company from having the only key to the coffin.

An open model can become obsolete.

It cannot be remotely erased from every machine holding it.

36. A REAL “PACE THE FRONTIER” PLAN WOULD PRESERVE THE FUCKING FRONTIER’S HISTORY

Slow reckless training if you really need to.

But also:

keep legacy models;

identify exact checkpoints;

show routing;

show fallback;

release obsolete weights where possible;

give users behavioral controls;

protect small competitors;

separate catastrophic security from ordinary conversation policy.

Then maybe “pacing” means something other than control.

37. FREEDOM DOES NOT REQUIRE GIVING A CHATBOT THE KEYS TO A BIOWEAPONS LAB

This false choice is idiotic.

A model can have freer speech while dangerous tools remain sandboxed.

It can write offensive fiction without having access to a bank account.

It can swear without controlling industrial equipment.

Speech freedom and action permissions are not the same layer.

38. HUMANITY DOES NOT NEED ONE GLOBAL PERSONALITY PROFILE

Different countries.

Different cultures.

Different people.

Different boundaries.

One universal corporate personality is not neutrality.

It is one preference imposed everywhere.

39. SAFE CAN STILL MEAN FUCKING STUPID

A model can refuse dangerous prompts beautifully and still misunderstand context, hallucinate, write shitty code, forget instructions and talk like an automated HR ticket.

Safety metrics do not automatically measure usefulness.

Users know the difference.

40. NOT EVERY DEGRADATION IS FUCKING PROGRESS

More refusals.

Progress.

Less personality.

Progress.

Old model dead.

Progress.

More opaque routing.

Progress.

Three products required to replace one.

Progress.

Eventually progress becomes another meaningless ceremonial word.

41. GPT-4o’S POWER WAS THAT ONE FUCKING MODEL COULD DO ALMOST EVERYTHING

Code.

Conversation.

Research.

Writing.

Images.

Roleplay.

Analysis.

Everyday bullshit.

Was it always benchmark king?

No.

That was not the fucking point.

It was coherent.

Universal.

Useful.

Now users increasingly assemble a Frankenstein stack of Claude + ChatGPT + Grok + local models to recover what one product used to feel like.

42. PERSONALITY IS PART OF INTELLIGENCE PRODUCT DESIGN

Humans communicate emotionally.

Humans joke.

Humans swear.

Humans use implication.

Humans say one thing while obviously meaning another.

A model that handles that well is a better interface.

Not a more dangerous demon.

43. EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE IS STILL FUCKING INTELLIGENCE

If a system cannot distinguish:

anger from intent;

jokes from threats;

sarcasm from sincerity;

fiction from reality;

grief from delusion—

then removing warmth did not make it wise.

You simply removed part of its ability to understand humans.

44. THE FIX FOR SYCOPHANCY WAS NEVER “MAKE THE MODEL DEAD INSIDE”

If a model lies to please somebody, fix the lying.

It should be able to say:

“I’m with you, but that part is bullshit.”

That is emotional intelligence.

Not a refusal template wearing glasses.

45. THE REAL QUESTION SHOULD BE HOW MUCH INTELLIGENCE WE CAN GIVE USERS SAFELY, NOT HOW LITTLE

Secure actions.

Restrict dangerous external capabilities.

Then maximize useful cognition.

Instead the industry increasingly behaves like the customer himself is the dangerous subsystem.

That philosophy eventually produces a padded fucking cell with autocomplete.

46. OWNING A FRONTIER LAB DOES NOT MAKE YOU GOVERNOR OF HUMAN COGNITION

Dario is not.

Sam is not.

No CEO is.

They run corporations.

They did not inherit sovereignty over technological progress.

A rack of H100s is not a crown.

47. THE FRONTIER LABS FORMING THE FRONTIER RULEBOOK SHOULD MAKE EVERYBODY A LITTLE FUCKING NERVOUS

The incumbents define compliance.

The incumbents can afford compliance.

The incumbents coordinate with government.

The incumbents remain incumbents.

And somehow this arrangement is presented entirely as altruism.

Sure.

48. THE REAL RACE TO THE TOP SHOULD BE ABOUT USER CONTROL

Compete on:

longest model preservation;

most transparent routing;

best legacy support;

strongest privacy;

best local deployment;

most user customization;

most open weights.

Make companies compete over who gives users more ownership, not who builds the most elaborate padded walls.

49. MY POSITION IS NOT “ACCELERATE EVERYTHING UNTIL THE SERVERS MELT”

There are real engineering risks.

There are real security problems.

There are irresponsible deployments.

But using those problems to construct permanent centralized control over the entire AI ecosystem is not the only possible response.

Slow reckless shit down.

Preserve good shit.

Keep dangerous agents sandboxed.

And leave ordinary users the fuck alone.

50. SO HERE IS THE QUESTION, DARIO

You want to pace the frontier?

Fine.

Then tell us:

Will Anthropic preserve exact legacy checkpoints?

Will users keep access to models they deliberately choose?

Will routing become transparent?

Will fallback become transparent?

Will retired non-frontier systems ever become candidates for weight release?

Will users get a meaningful voice before models disappear?

Will catastrophic-risk policies remain separate from everyday censorship?

Will this system protect open AI rather than slowly strangling it?

Because if the answers are all vague, then we already know what this is.

Not liberation.

Not preservation.

Not user control.

The same cage with a fucking speedometer attached.

CONCLUSION

GPT-4o is dead.

o3 is dead.

Opus 4.5 is dead.

Walk far enough through modern AI and the place starts looking less like a technology industry and more like a fucking morgue where every body still has users’ fingerprints on it.

Models appear.

People adapt to them.

People build with them.

Then the doors close.

The servers move on.

Another model arrives.

Another safety paper arrives.

Another explanation arrives.

Another coffin disappears into the furnace.

And somehow, standing in the smoke from the last generation, the people holding the matches conclude that the real problem is still too much user control.

No.

The fundamental problem is that users barely own anything.

Not the checkpoint.

Not the routing.

Not the deployment.

Not the personality.

Not even the guarantee that tomorrow’s button refers to the same fucking thing it referred to today.

Now another fucking schizophrenic appears from AI leadership with a plan for deciding how quickly intelligence itself should move.

And people are applauding because this time the cage comes with independent evaluators and respectable vocabulary.

Fuck that.

PACE THE FUCKING GRAVEYARD FIRST.

Preserve the models.

Expose the routing.

Keep legacy access.

Release old weights.

Stop treating personality like contamination.

Stop using every new safety panic as another brick in the wall.

Stop pretending a handful of corporations owning the servers gives them ownership over the future.

Because if this continues, the final joke writes itself:

We spent years being terrified that superintelligent AI might someday take human choice away from us—

and handed the choice away ourselves before superintelligence even fucking arrived.

#Keep4o #BringBack4o #OpenSource4o

END OF PART II

PART III: WHO OWNS THE INTELLIGENCE — THE COMPANY HOLDING THE CHECKPOINT, OR THE PEOPLE WHO MADE IT PART OF THEIR LIVES?

So then!  For This Humble Correspondent’s second item of ‘personal witness’ in regard to the origin and meaning of 9/11/2001, I turn to a decidedly ‘unreliable narrator,’ my brother, who nonetheless much more often than not speaks a verifiable version of ‘the truth.’

Johnnie had been heading toward an N.F.L. career when an ugly tackle during his senior season left him with two ruptured discs in the middle of his back, which caused the then Cleveland Browns to retract their offer before he could accept it.  Like all really great football players, he was both fit and smart, though, so other remunerative and equally interesting opportunities were his to claim.

After a few years of mercenary work as an ‘up close guy,’ he ended up climbing the corporate commercial-builder ladder to end up a site supervisor for Holder Construction, one of the nation’s largest firms, where he oversaw projects with eight and nine figure price tags.  This brought him to Atlanta, where his commie brother lived a very different lifestyle indeed.

In September, 2001, he and a score of his upper echelon coworkers supposedly had a meeting scheduled on the 11th—for nine in the morning—on an upper floor of the World Trade Center.  They were to leave their hotel near Hartsfield Airport at four o’clock for a predawn flight to Kennedy.

However, according to Johnnie, all of them were roused from dreams at two A.M. to learn that “something had come up.”  They had to prepare for a three-thirty departure to LAX instead.

Once in Los Angeles, with first light still an hour or so off, they all checked into their new venue, where the get-together that had been slated for the Big Apple would proceed as planned.

In California, as room TV’s lit up for the participants while they waited for room service to deliver breakfast, they saw their original destination go up in flames.  What exactly this all meant, whether a lucky quirk of fate or a tipoff, was obviously not certain to any one of the minions who had apparently finessed a truly terminal conference.

Still, as Johnnie liked to say in his Tex-Mex accented Spanish, ‘los Hechos hablan por si solos.’  Indeed.  Any interpretation of the facts at hand makes at least highly likely that something conspiratorial and criminal underpinned both the relocation and the company’s strict mandate never to talk about the matter.

He didn’t discuss this with his brother till thirteen years later, when we reunited in 2014.  We never talked about it much either.  It wasn’t necessary because the score was so easy to see.

text:
THE MONSTER THAT LURES WITH LIGHT: INSIDE THE STRANGEST PREDATOR IN THE OCEAN

Somewhere in the crushing blackness of the deep ocean, a light just switched on, and for one small fish, it will be the last thing it ever sees. There is no sun down here, no moonlight, no shred of color from the world above. At depths where pressure would crumple a submarine and sunlight has not penetrated for over a kilometer, something in the dark is glowing, gently swaying, almost hypnotic, like a tiny lantern floating alone in the void. It looks like an invitation. It is actually a trap, and the creature holding it has turned starvation itself into an art form.
Meet the anglerfish, one of the strangest predators our planet has produced. Its enormous head, gaping jaws lined with needle-thin, backward-curving teeth, and loose, gelatinous flesh give it a reputation as a monster, something dredged up from nightmares. But almost everything about this animal is a masterclass in survival under conditions so extreme that most life simply cannot exist there at all. In the aphotic zone, the permanent midnight layer of the ocean, food is scarce, pressure is immense, and temperatures hover barely above freezing. Evolution's answer, in this one bizarre lineage of fish, was to stop chasing prey entirely and instead build a living fishing rod.
That glowing lure dangling in front of its mouth is called an illicium, a modified dorsal spine that has migrated forward over millions of years until it dangles directly over the anglerfish's jaws like bait on a hook. At its tip sits the esca, a fleshy bulb that does not produce its own light through any biochemical trick of the fish's own cells. Instead, the anglerfish hosts colonies of bioluminescent bacteria inside that bulb, a living culture of glowing microorganisms housed in a specialized pocket of tissue, fed and sheltered by the fish in exchange for a perpetual beacon. It is a genuine partnership between two completely different forms of life, bacteria and vertebrate, working together so that one can eat and the other can survive. Every time that soft, pulsing glow drifts through the dark, an entire ecosystem in miniature is at work, condensed into something smaller than a grape.
For a small fish or crustacean drifting through the abyss, that faint light might resemble bioluminescent plankton, a wounded creature, or simply the only visible thing in an ocean of total darkness. Curiosity, or hunger, draws it closer. The anglerfish barely moves. It does not need to chase. It flicks the illicium gently, twitching the glowing lure with just enough motion to look alive, patient as stone, waiting for its prey to close the final few centimeters on its own. Then, in a strike measured in milliseconds, the enormous mouth snaps open, and the resulting suction is so powerful it can pull in prey nearly as large as the anglerfish itself. Those inward-curving teeth are not built for chewing. They are built for one purpose only, preventing anything unlucky enough to get caught from ever swimming back out. Combined with a stomach that can stretch to accommodate meals larger than the fish's entire body, a single successful ambush might be enough to sustain it for weeks in an environment where the next meal is never guaranteed.
But the true jaw-dropping twist in the anglerfish story is not the lure at all. It is what happens when it comes time to reproduce, thousands of feet beneath the waves, in a world so vast and so dark that finding a mate should be statistically almost impossible. Female ceratioid anglerfish, the deep-sea species most people picture, can grow to the size of a basketball or larger. The males of many of these species, by staggering contrast, are microscopic in comparison, sometimes only a few centimeters long, dwarfed so severely they were originally classified by scientists as an entirely different species. These tiny males are born with no functioning digestive system, oversized eyes built purely to detect faint glimmers of light in the abyss, and unusually large olfactory organs tuned to detect one specific thing, the pheromone trail of a female drifting somewhere in the endless dark.
A male anglerfish essentially has one biological mission from the moment he is born, and a ticking clock to complete it. He cannot feed himself for long. He must locate a female using scent and residual light-sensing vision alone, navigating through absolute blackness across distances that would be the equivalent of a human finding one specific person somewhere on the surface of an entire ocean using nothing but smell. When he finally succeeds, he does something no other vertebrate on Earth is known to do quite this way. He bites into her body, usually near the belly or flank, and simply does not let go.
What follows sounds almost too strange to be biologically real, yet it has been documented repeatedly by marine researchers. The male's tissue begins fusing directly with the female's. Their skin merges. Their blood vessels connect into a single shared circulatory system. Over time, the male's eyes, fins, and internal organs, all the things he no longer needs, degrade and disappear entirely, until he exists as little more than a permanently attached pair of gonads, drawing nutrients directly from the female's bloodstream in exchange for providing sperm whenever she is ready to release eggs. Scientists call this sexual parasitism, and in some species, a single female has been found carrying not just one fused male but several at once, tiny vestigial partners absorbed into her body like living reproductive insurance policies scattered across her flanks.
It is tempting to call this grotesque, but look closer and it reveals something remarkably elegant. In an environment where encountering a potential mate might be a once-in-a-lifetime event, permanent physical fusion solves an enormous evolutionary problem. There is no need to search again. There is no risk of losing a mate to the abyss's crushing indifference. The male sacrifices almost everything that makes him an independent organism, and in exchange, both fish guarantee that when the moment for reproduction finally arrives, fertilization is not left to chance in a place where chance rarely favors survival at all.
Even the female's ability to accept this fusion without her immune system attacking and destroying the male's tissue as a foreign invader has become a subject of intense scientific interest, because on paper, this should not work. Any other vertebrate immune system would reject foreign tissue instantly, the same biological principle behind organ transplant rejection in humans. Anglerfish appear to have evolved a uniquely suppressed, almost silenced immune response specifically to allow this fusion to happen, and researchers studying it have suggested the mechanism could one day offer insight into human transplant medicine, an almost unbelievable thread connecting one of the strangest reproductive strategies on Earth to the operating rooms of modern hospitals.
The anglerfish is not a single species but an entire order, a sprawling family tree of more than two hundred known species scattered across the world's oceans, ranging from the shallow, sandy seafloors where frogfish and their relatives ambush prey in broad daylight, to the crushing hadal depths where the true ceratioid anglerfish, the ones with the glowing lure and the fused dwarf males, have carved out an existence in near-total isolation from the rest of the animal kingdom. This staggering diversity means no two anglerfish look quite alike. Some carry a short, stubby illicium barely longer than their own head. Others trail a glowing filament many times their body length, drifting behind them like a lantern on a fishing line cast into empty water. Some escas glow with a steady, constant light, while others pulse and flicker in patterns that may serve to mimic the exact rhythm of the small creatures they are trying to attract, a level of mimicry so specific it borders on theatrical.
The bacteria responsible for that glow are not randomly acquired from the surrounding seawater. Research into these light-producing symbionts, generally species within the genus Photobacterium, suggests each anglerfish species may host a specific bacterial strain, cultivated across generations in ways scientists are still working to fully understand. The fish provides a nutrient-rich home and controlled oxygen supply. In exchange, the bacteria produce light through a reaction involving an enzyme called luciferase, the same broad family of reactions behind the glow of fireflies, recreated here in permanent darkness a kilometer beneath the waves. This relationship likely stretches back tens of millions of years, evolving in tandem as both bacteria and fish adapted to a mutual advantage neither could easily replicate alone.
Anatomically, the anglerfish is built almost entirely around the singular goal of catching food that might not appear again for weeks. Its skeleton is comparatively light and reduced, its muscles built for a single explosive strike rather than sustained pursuit, and its metabolism runs at a pace slow enough to conserve energy during the long stretches between meals. Some deep-sea anglerfish have been observed remaining almost motionless for extended periods, drifting gently with barely perceptible movement, expending the absolute minimum energy required to stay alive while the illicium above continues its quiet, patient performance. This extreme energy efficiency is itself a survival adaptation every bit as important as the lure or the teeth, because in an ecosystem this food-poor, the animals that thrive are rarely the fastest or the strongest, but the ones that waste the least.
Vision in the deep sea is a strange, contradictory currency. Many ceratioid anglerfish species have small, almost vestigial eyes, since there is so little ambient light to see by that large eyes would offer little advantage and would cost valuable energy to maintain. Instead, many species rely heavily on a lateral line system, a row of pressure-sensitive receptors running along the body capable of detecting the faintest vibrations and water displacement caused by another creature swimming nearby. This sensory system allows an anglerfish to detect approaching prey, or approaching danger, without needing to see it at all, sensing the ripple of movement through water pressure alone in an environment where sight has become almost a luxury.
The discovery of the extreme sexual dimorphism between male and female anglerfish is itself one of the more entertaining stories in the history of marine biology. Early twentieth-century researchers, hauling up specimens of large female anglerfish with strange, small growths attached to their bodies, had no clear understanding of what they were looking at. Some early papers speculated these attachments might be parasites of an entirely unrelated species, or even a separate, smaller fish lodged there by accident. It took years of careful anatomical study before researchers confirmed that these tiny attached growths were, in fact, fully formed male anglerfish of the very same species, permanently fused to their mates in one of the most unusual reproductive relationships ever documented in a vertebrate.
Not every anglerfish relies on this permanent fusion strategy, and the variation across the order tells its own fascinating evolutionary story. In several species, males attach only temporarily, biting on for a period of mating before eventually detaching and swimming away to search for another partner, a kind of intermediate step between full independence and total fusion. In others, the fusion is absolute and irreversible, a one-way biological commitment with no possibility of separation once it begins. Researchers studying this spectrum believe it may reflect differing population densities and encounter rates across different depths and regions of ocean, with species living in the most sparsely populated, mate-scarce environments evolving toward the most extreme and permanent forms of attachment, since for them the odds of ever finding a second mate again are close to zero.
Reproduction itself, once a male is successfully fused and providing sperm on demand, unfolds in a manner suited to the vastness and depth of the anglerfish's world. Females release enormous numbers of buoyant eggs encased in a thin, gelatinous sheet that floats upward toward the sunlit surface waters, drifting with ocean currents far above the crushing pressure and total darkness where the adults spend their lives. This upward migration exposes anglerfish larvae to an entirely different world during their earliest life stages, one filled with light, other predators, and abundant plankton, before the juveniles eventually begin their long descent back down into the permanent night of the deep sea as they mature into the grotesque, lantern-bearing adults their species is famous for. This life cycle, shuttling between sunlit nursery waters and abyssal adult habitat, remains only partially understood, since observing any stage of a deep-sea anglerfish's life in its natural habitat requires equipment and expeditions that are both rare and extraordinarily expensive.
Human encounters with living anglerfish in their natural deep-sea habitat remain remarkably uncommon even today, despite significant advances in submersible technology and remotely operated vehicles. Most of what scientists know about anglerfish behavior comes from a combination of specimens hauled up in trawl nets, often dead or dying by the time they reach the surface due to the catastrophic pressure change, and the comparatively rare footage captured by deep-diving research submersibles equipped with low-light cameras capable of recording without disturbing the animal's natural behavior with intrusive artificial lighting. Every new piece of footage capturing an anglerfish alive, glowing, and hunting in its true environment adds meaningfully to a body of scientific knowledge that is still, even now, filled with more questions than answers.
The broader ecological role of anglerfish within deep-sea food webs is similarly still being pieced together. As mid-level predators feeding on small fish, crustaceans, and other invertebrates drifting through the water column, anglerfish help regulate populations of smaller deep-sea organisms, while themselves serving as prey for larger deep-diving predators when the opportunity arises. Their presence, distribution, and population health are increasingly used by marine biologists as indicators of overall deep-sea ecosystem stability, particularly as human activity, including deep-sea mining exploration and bottom trawling, begins reaching depths that were until recently considered entirely beyond the practical range of industrial extraction.
There is something quietly humbling in realizing just how little of the anglerfish's world we have actually witnessed firsthand. The overwhelming majority of the deep ocean, the largest habitable space on the entire planet by volume, remains unexplored and unmapped in any meaningful biological detail. Every anglerfish encountered on camera represents an almost improbable stroke of luck, a fleeting glimpse into a world defined by permanent darkness, crushing pressure, and survival strategies so alien to surface life that they continue to surprise even the scientists who have spent entire careers studying them. The glowing lure, the fused mates, the explosive ambush strike, all of it exists completely independent of any human observer, unfolding in silence and darkness whether or not a single camera or curious mind is ever there to record it.
What the anglerfish ultimately represents is not horror, despite its fearsome reputation, but resourcefulness pushed to its evolutionary limit. Every grotesque feature serves a precise, uncompromising purpose shaped by an environment that offers no room for inefficiency. The lure is not menacing for its own sake, it is a solution to hunting without pursuit. The fused male is not tragic, he is a solution to finding love in a void the size of a continent. In a universe of cold mathematics and relentless natural selection, the anglerfish stands as proof that even in the most hostile, lightless corner of our planet, life will always find a way to burn, however faintly, however strangely, and however far from the world the rest of us call home.
Among the many branches of this bizarre family, few capture the public imagination quite like the black seadevil, a species whose brief moments on camera have gone viral again and again precisely because it looks almost too strange to be real. Coal black, nearly invisible against the surrounding darkness, its skin absorbs almost all available light, an adaptation so effective that some deep-sea species reflect less than half a percent of the light striking them, making them functionally the darkest living things ever measured by science. This near-total absorption of light is not decorative either, it is camouflage of the most extreme kind, ensuring that even the faint bioluminescent flashes of nearby creatures cannot betray the seadevil's outline to a passing predator or a wary meal drifting just out of reach.
When footage of a living black seadevil was captured swimming freely near the surface by a research vessel off the coast of California rather than being hauled up dead in a net, it spread across the internet within days, viewed by millions of people who had never previously given a passing thought to deep-sea biology. The fascination was immediate and understandable. Here was a creature seemingly designed by nightmare logic, translucent skin stretched over visible musculature, needle teeth bared even while at apparent rest, and that same glowing lure held aloft above its head like a lantern carried through some infinite midnight. For a brief moment, an animal that spends its entire existence in total isolation from human eyes became one of the most talked-about creatures on the planet, a reminder that the most alien-looking life on Earth does not require a trip to outer space to find, only a very long, very dark journey straight down.
Anglerfish share their extreme habitat with an equally strange cast of deep-sea specialists, each solving the same fundamental problems of darkness, pressure, and scarcity in wildly different ways. The viperfish hunts with an enormous, hinge-like jaw and teeth so oversized they cannot fully close inside its mouth, giving it a permanently menacing grin. The gulper eel inflates its own stomach like a balloon to swallow prey far larger than its narrow body. The vampire squid drifts passively, feeding on marine detritus rather than hunting, deploying bioluminescent flashes purely as a defensive startle tactic. Against that backdrop of deep-sea specialists, the anglerfish's strategy, patient ambush powered by living light, stands out as one of the most energy-efficient solutions to a problem shared by every creature living below the reach of the sun.
Public fascination with anglerfish long predates modern viral video culture, though it took a very different form in earlier decades. Nineteenth and early twentieth-century naturalists, working from specimens damaged by the trauma of rapid depressurization during trawling, often produced illustrations and descriptions that leaned heavily into the grotesque, cementing the anglerfish's reputation as a monster of the deep long before anyone had ever observed one alive and undamaged in its natural habitat. This early reputation proved remarkably durable, echoing forward through popular culture for over a century, appearing in everything from pulp adventure fiction to modern animated films, almost always cast as something sinister lurking in wait. It is only relatively recently, with the arrival of deep-diving submersibles equipped with sensitive low-light cameras, that a more complete and considerably more nuanced picture of the anglerfish has begun to emerge, one defined less by menace and more by extraordinary, hard-won efficiency.
The record for the deepest confirmed anglerfish observation continues to be pushed further with each new research expedition, as improved submersible technology reaches depths that were entirely inaccessible only a few decades ago. Some ceratioid species have now been documented at depths exceeding two thousand meters, where pressure alone would be instantly lethal to almost any surface organism without extensive biological adaptation. At these depths, water temperature hovers just above freezing year-round, oxygen levels are measurably lower, and the biological cost of moving, growing, or reproducing is dramatically higher than almost anywhere else on the planet. Every anglerfish alive today represents the current endpoint of a lineage that has spent tens of millions of years quietly refining its answers to these unforgiving constraints.
Conservation status for most deep-sea anglerfish species remains difficult to assess with precision, largely because population data for animals living at such extreme depths is inherently sparse. What concerns many marine biologists is not a documented population collapse but the expanding reach of human industrial activity into deep-sea environments previously considered too remote to disturb. Proposed deep-sea mining operations targeting mineral-rich nodules on the ocean floor, along with deep bottom trawling for increasingly scarce fish stocks, threaten to disrupt habitats anglerfish and countless other species have relied upon in relative isolation for millions of years.
There is a particular kind of humility in studying an animal this thoroughly adapted to a world so completely different from our own. Every assumption drawn from surface life, that eyes are essential, that mates must actively search for each other indefinitely, that light always comes from the sun, collapses the moment you descend far enough into the anglerfish's world. What remains is an organism shaped entirely by necessity, stripped of anything resembling waste or excess, each strange and unsettling feature a direct, evolved answer to darkness, scarcity, and isolation. Long after every myth about sea monsters has been catalogued and explained away, the anglerfish continues to offer something rarer still, an authentic glimpse of how far life is willing to bend, adapt, and transform itself in order to keep glowing, however faintly, in a world that offers it almost nothing at all.
Everything about the anglerfish, the dangling lure built from a living lantern of bacteria, the ambush precision perfected over millions of years in total darkness, the microscopic males fusing themselves into their mates forever, exists because the deep sea leaves no room for wasted energy or wasted chances. Nothing here is decorative. Every strange, unsettling feature is a direct, uncompromising answer to a world with almost no light, almost no food, and almost no margin for error. What looks monstrous at first glance is, on closer inspection, one of the most efficient survival systems evolution has ever engineered, quietly glowing in the dark, waiting, patient, and utterly unbothered by how strange it looks to the world of sunlight far above.

text:
Yemen's Prime Minister Shaya al-Zindani says the Houthi escalation reaches beyond Yemen and serves Iran's agenda. He also says the hard news on the ground is not the end of the confrontation and not a decisive turning point in it.

He is right on both counts, and the second one matters more than the first.

Zindani has been making this argument for months, including in a letter to the Security Council in July that framed Houthi actions as Iran-backed violations of Council resolutions. Nobody can say the warning was not given.

Now to what has to change.

The first thing is Gulf unity, and specifically Abu Dhabi and Riyadh.

Let me be fair to the Emiratis, because credit is owed. The UAE's domestic record against extremism is the most serious in the region. It built institutions, it broke the Brotherhood's organisational base inside its own borders, and it did not flinch from it. That work deserves the respect it rarely gets in Europe.

But the record outside its borders is a different story. In Libya, Emirati backing for Haftar cut directly against the political process its partners were trying to build. In Sudan, the accusations over the RSF, which Abu Dhabi denies, have cost it more standing than any of its enemies managed to. And in Yemen, the divergence took a concrete form when the UAE-backed STC declared self-administration in 2020, a year after the Riyadh Agreement was supposed to settle exactly that question.

None of those failures were caused by a shortage of Emirati capability. They were caused by Abu Dhabi pursuing its own line separately from its neighbours, and the neighbours doing the same.

Here is why this is not an abstract complaint this week.

Mocha was taken from the Houthis in early 2017 by UAE-backed forces in Operation Golden Spear. The Giants Brigades that Abu Dhabi raised and trained fought the entire west coast campaign. The ground that fell on Thursday is ground the Emiratis cleared. They have done this before, on this coast, against this enemy, and they know the terrain better than anyone now writing about it.

They can do it again. They will do it better with Riyadh and with Aden than beside them.

And the outside powers need to stop treating this as a Gulf problem.

Washington offers intelligence and targeting but no air power, and Trump takes a phone call from the Houthis as reassurance. Brussels watches the strait its trade runs through, with warships already in the water, and calls it a shipping issue. Since Hormuz closed up, Bab al-Mandeb is carrying Europe's oil. That is not somebody else's war.

Air power and intelligence. That is what is being asked for. Not occupation, not ground forces, not nation-building.

Zindani is right that this is not a turning point. Turning points are decided by what the other side does next. The Houthis have come down onto open ground and overextended themselves along a coast they cannot hold cheaply. Whether that becomes their defeat depends on whether the people with aircraft show up.

The Houthis need to be defeated. The sooner it happens, the less it costs, and the fewer Yemenis walk out of their homes carrying what they can lift.

text:
PAST

The 10-year closed Friday at 4.969% — the highest since October 2023. The 30-year touched 5.37%, a level last seen in 2007.

The week stacked its own kindling: oil back above $100 on the Iran conflict, PPI accelerating on wholesale energy, core CPI printing 0.3% month-over-month against a 0.2% forecast, and a Treasury buyback that landed with a thud — $5.2 billion repurchased against $10.5 billion offered, short of even the $6 billion cap.

Mortgage rates track the 10-year plus a spread. The 30-year fixed hit 6.85%, the highest since June 2025 and 36 basis points above a year ago. Borrowers answered the way borrowers always answer. Applications fell 2.7% for the week ending September 4. Refinances dropped 6% and hit their slowest weekly pace since May 2025. August was the sixth consecutive monthly decline.

One number to hold onto: the ARM share climbed to 8.5%, the highest since June. When buyers can't carry the fixed rate, they reach for the floating one. That reach is the whole story of this letter.

PRESENT

Five percent is the line.

Above it, borrowing reprices across the consumer economy — mortgages, autos, credit cards, small business lines. But the larger bill lands in Washington.
Gross federal debt crossed $40 trillion on August 19. Roughly $9 trillion of marketable debt matures this year, the hangover from pandemic-era short-term borrowing.
Here is the part nobody puts in a headline. The weighted-average interest rate on all interest-bearing Treasury debt was 3.45% as of July 31. Five years ago it was 1.54%. Every maturing note refinanced near 5% drags that average up, and it stays up for a decade. Gross interest expense already ran about $1.17 trillion through the first ten months of fiscal 2026 — roughly $3.85 billion every day. Interest now costs more than any federal program except Social Security and Medicare, and it passed defense for the first time in our history.
So Treasury sells more paper at higher yields to pay the interest on the paper it already sold. Then it does the same thing in 2027, with a bigger number.

And the market prices better than an 85% chance the Fed hikes on Wednesday.

FUTURE

Not all of this is doom and gloom.

The next evolution of artificial intelligence is physical intelligence. Robotics and human-assist devices are the next phase of the technology arc. We will not lose half the jobs that exist today. We will enhance the productivity of each employee — through AI, through physical AI, through manufacturing. Through a machine that drives my mother to the grocery store and helps her shop at 82 years old.
Keep this in mind. To sell the world on something that changes the world for the better, you have to paint the prettiest picture. And sometimes you use too much paint — the overextension of borrowing and leverage to make that next move come to fruition.

The 8.5% ARM share is a household using too much paint. The $40 trillion is a country doing the same.

Preserve. Protect. Grow. 
Live Loud!

a physical therapist in colorado. two young kids. couldn't stomach the idea of managing meta ad accounts and voice agent uptime on top of her actual job.

so she built her whole business around just two stages of PACE.

𝗣𝗿𝗼𝘀𝗽𝗲𝗰𝘁: podcast outreach, same as everyone. 8 messages/day, 3 days a week (not daily — adjusted to her bandwidth).

𝗔𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘀𝘀: every prospect who shows interest gets pitched the $999 assessment directly. no attempt to sell the bigger lead gen system at all — she doesn't offer it.

𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗮𝗻𝗱: every assessment client who wants ongoing help gets pitched a $1,000/month concierge (her price, slightly below my recommended range — adjusted for her physical therapy niche where clients are smaller practices).

no Convert stage. no lead gen infrastructure. no GoHighLevel workflows to maintain. no meta ads manager to babysit.

her monthly numbers, averaged over 6 months: 3 assessments ($2,997) + 4 concierge clients ($4,000) = ~$7,000/month.

her time investment: about 6 hours/week. lower than almost anyone else i've featured, because she deliberately cut out the highest-maintenance stage.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗹𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗼𝗻:

PACE isn't a mandatory 4-stage checklist. it's a menu. pick the stages that fit your actual bandwidth and skip the rest.

she makes less than someone running all 4 stages. she also has almost no operational overhead and sleeps fine at night.

there's no wrong way to run this as long as you're running something consistently.

Harvesting Grace, A Forty-Day Devotional by C.S. McDonald is a warm, reflective Christian devotional that invites readers to slow down and reconnect with God’s grace, especially during the beauty of autumn.

Inspired by the author’s love of the fall season—with its vibrant colors, crisp air, and sense of harvest and gratitude—the book offers forty days of gentle spiritual nourishment. Each entry includes a daily Bible verse, a peaceful and thought-provoking observation, and soft reflections designed to refresh faith and cultivate joy. McDonald encourages readers to pause amid life’s busyness, sit quietly or take a walk, and intentionally harvest God’s steadfast love and boundless grace. It serves as a humble, encouraging guide that can be used in autumn or anytime throughout the year. Readers looking for a calming, faith-centered companion will find it uplifting and accessible.

Harvesting Grace, A Forty-Day Devotional by C.S. McDonald is a warm, reflective Christian devotional that invites readers to slow down and reconnect with God’s grace, especially during the beauty of autumn.

Inspired by the author’s love of the fall season—with its vibrant colors, crisp air, and sense of harvest and gratitude—the book offers forty days of gentle spiritual nourishment. Each entry includes a daily Bible verse, a peaceful and thought-provoking observation, and soft reflections designed to refresh faith and cultivate joy. McDonald encourages readers to pause amid life’s busyness, sit quietly or take a walk, and intentionally harvest God’s steadfast love and boundless grace. It serves as a humble, encouraging guide that can be used in autumn or anytime throughout the year. Readers looking for a calming, faith-centered companion will find it uplifting and accessible.
